segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā antarā ca madhuraṁ antarā ca verañjaṁ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was traveling along the road between Madhurā and Verañjā,

segs.p: Sambahulāpi kho gahapatī ca gahapatāniyo ca antarā ca madhuraṁ antarā ca verañjaṁ addhānamaggappaṭipannā honti.
segs.e: as were several householders, both women and men.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle (…) nisīdi.
segs.e: The Buddha left the road and sat at the root of a tree,

segs.p: Addasaṁsu kho gahapatī ca gahapatāniyo ca bhagavantaṁ aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle nisinnaṁ.
segs.e: where the householders saw him.

segs.p: Disvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te gahapatī ca gahapatāniyo ca bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: They went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to them:
“Householders, there are four ways of living together.
What four?
A male zombie living with a female zombie;
a male zombie living with a goddess;
a god living with a female zombie;
a god living with a goddess.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapatayo, chavo chavāya saddhiṁ saṁvasati?
segs.e: And how does a male zombie live with a female zombie?

segs.p: Idha, gahapatayo, sāmiko hoti pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī dussīlo pāpadhammo maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati akkosakaparibhāsako samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when the husband kills living creatures, steals, commits sexual misconduct, lies, and consumes intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor. He’s unethical, of bad character, living at home with his heart full of the stain of stinginess, abusing and insulting ascetics and brahmins.

segs.p: bhariyāpissa hoti pāṇātipātinī adinnādāyinī kāmesumicchācārinī musāvādinī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyinī dussīlā pāpadhammā maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati akkosikaparibhāsikā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ.
segs.e: And the wife is also … unethical, of bad character …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapatayo, chavo chavāya saddhiṁ saṁvasati.
segs.e: That’s how a male zombie lives with a female zombie.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapatayo, chavo deviyā saddhiṁ saṁvasati?
segs.e: And how does a male zombie live with a goddess?

segs.p: Idha, gahapatayo, sāmiko hoti pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī dussīlo pāpadhammo maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati akkosakaparibhāsako samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when the husband … is unethical, of bad character …

segs.p: bhariyā khvassa hoti pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā adinnādānā paṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā musāvādā paṭiviratā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati anakkosikaparibhāsikā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ.
segs.e: But the wife doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants. She’s ethical, of good character, living at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, not abusing and insulting ascetics and brahmins.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapatayo, chavo deviyā saddhiṁ saṁvasati.
segs.e: That’s how a male zombie lives with a goddess.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapatayo, devo chavāya saddhiṁ saṁvasati?
segs.e: And how does a god live with a female zombie?

segs.p: Idha, gahapatayo, sāmiko hoti pāṇātipātā paṭivirato adinnādānā paṭivirato kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato musāvādā paṭivirato surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati anakkosakaparibhāsako samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when the husband … is ethical, of good character …

segs.p: bhariyā khvassa hoti pāṇātipātinī …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyinī dussīlā pāpadhammā maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati akkosikaparibhāsikā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ.
segs.e: But the wife … is unethical, of bad character …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapatayo, devo chavāya saddhiṁ saṁvasati.
segs.e: That’s how a god lives with a female zombie.

segs.p: Kathañca, gahapatayo, devo deviyā saddhiṁ saṁvasati?
segs.e: And how does a god live with a goddess?

segs.p: Idha, gahapatayo, sāmiko hoti pāṇātipātā paṭivirato …pe… sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati anakkosakaparibhāsako samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ;
segs.e: It’s when the husband … is ethical, of good character …

segs.p: bhariyāpissa hoti pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratā sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati anakkosikaparibhāsikā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ.
segs.e: And the wife is also … ethical, of good character …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, gahapatayo, devo deviyā saddhiṁ saṁvasati.
segs.e: That’s how a god lives with a goddess.
These are the four ways of living together.
When both are unethical,
miserly and abusive,
then wife and husband
live together as zombies.
When the husband is unethical,
miserly and abusive,
but the wife is ethical,
bountiful, rid of stinginess,
she’s a goddess living
with a zombie for a husband.
When the husband is ethical,
bountiful, rid of stinginess,
but the wife is unethical,
miserly and abusive,
she’s a zombie living
with a god for a husband.
When both are faithful and bountiful,
disciplined, living righteously,
then wife and husband
say nice things to each other.
Their needs are amply satisfied,
so they live at ease.
Their enemies are downhearted,
when both are equal in ethics.
Having practiced the teaching here,
both equal in precepts and observances,
they delight in the heavenly realm,
enjoying all the pleasures they desire.”
Numbered Discourses 4.54
6. Overflowing Merit
Living Together (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are four ways of living together.
What four?
A male zombie living with a female zombie;
a male zombie living with a goddess;
a god living with a female zombie;
a god living with a goddess.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, chavo chavāya saddhiṁ saṁvasati.
segs.e: And how does a male zombie live with a female zombie?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sāmiko hoti pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhiko dussīlo pāpadhammo maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati akkosakaparibhāsako samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ;

He’s unethical, of bad character, living at home with his heart full of the stain of stinginess, abusing and insulting ascetics and brahmins.

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sāmiko hoti pāṇātipātī …pe… micchādiṭṭhiko dussīlo pāpadhammo maccheramalapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati akkosakaparibhāsako samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ;

segs.e: But the wife … is unethical, of bad character …

segs.e: That’s how a god lives with a female zombie.

segs.e: It’s when the husband … is ethical, of good character …

segs.p: bhariyāpissa hoti pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā …pe… sammādiṭṭhikā sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati anakkosikaparibhāsikā samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṁ.
segs.e: And the wife is also … ethical, of good character …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, devo deviyā saddhiṁ saṁvasati.
segs.e: That’s how a god lives with a goddess.
These are the four ways of living together.” …
Numbered Discourses 4.55
6. Overflowing Merit
Equality (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Bhaggas at Crocodile’s Bellow, in the deer park at Bhesakaḷā’s Wood.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena nakulapituno gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the householder Nakula’s father, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho nakulapitā ca gahapati nakulamātā ca gahapatānī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho nakulapitā gahapati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Nakula’s father and the housewife Nakula’s mother went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. Nakula’s father said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “Yato me, bhante, nakulamātā gahapatānī daharasseva daharā ānītā, nābhijānāmi nakulamātaraṁ gahapatāniṁ manasāpi aticaritā, kuto pana kāyena.
segs.e: “Sir, ever since we were both young, and Nakula’s mother was given to me in marriage, I can’t recall betraying her even in thought, still less in deed.

segs.p: Iccheyyāma mayaṁ, bhante, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme aññamaññaṁ passituṁ abhisamparāyañca aññamaññaṁ passitun”ti.
segs.e: We want to see each other in both this life and the next.”
Then Nakula’s mother said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “yatohaṁ, bhante, nakulapituno gahapatissa daharasseva daharā ānītā, nābhijānāmi nakulapitaraṁ gahapatiṁ manasāpi aticaritā, kuto pana kāyena.
segs.e: “Sir, ever since we were both young, and I was given in marriage to Nakula’s father, I can’t recall betraying him even in thought, still less in deed.

segs.p: Iccheyyāma mayaṁ, bhante, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme aññamaññaṁ passituṁ abhisamparāyañca aññamaññaṁ passitun”ti.
segs.e: We want to see each other in both this life and the next.”

segs.p: “Ākaṅkheyyuñce, gahapatayo, ubho jānipatayo diṭṭhe ceva dhamme aññamaññaṁ passituṁ abhisamparāyañca aññamaññaṁ passituṁ ubhova assu samasaddhā samasīlā samacāgā samapaññā, te diṭṭhe ceva dhamme aññamaññaṁ passanti abhisamparāyañca aññamaññaṁ passantīti.
segs.e: “Householders, if wife and husband want to see each other in both this life and the next, they should be equals in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom.
When both are faithful and bountiful,
disciplined, living righteously,
then wife and husband
say nice things to each other.
Their needs are amply satisfied,
so they live at ease.
Their enemies are downhearted,
when both are equal in ethics.
Having practiced the teaching here,
both equal in precepts and observances,
they delight in the heavenly realm,
enjoying all the pleasures they desire.”
Numbered Discourses 4.56
6. Overflowing Merit
Equality (2nd)

segs.p: “Ākaṅkheyyuñce, bhikkhave, ubho jānipatayo diṭṭhe ceva dhamme aññamaññaṁ passituṁ abhisamparāyañca aññamaññaṁ passituṁ ubhova assu samasaddhā samasīlā samacāgā samapaññā, te diṭṭhe ceva dhamme aññamaññaṁ passanti abhisamparāyañca aññamaññaṁ passantīti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, if wife and husband want to see each other in both this life and the next, they should be equals in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom. …”
Numbered Discourses 4.57
6. Overflowing Merit
Suppavāsā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā koliyesu viharati pajjanikaṁ nāma koliyānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Koliyans, where they have a town named Pajjanika.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena suppavāsāya koliyadhītuyā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of Suppavāsā the Koliyan, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho suppavāsā koliyadhītā bhagavantaṁ paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena sahatthā santappesi sampavāresi.
segs.e: Then Suppavāsā served and satisfied the Buddha with her own hands with delicious fresh and cooked foods.

segs.p: Atha kho suppavāsā koliyadhītā bhagavantaṁ bhuttāviṁ onītapattapāṇiṁ ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When the Buddha had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, she sat down to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho suppavāsaṁ koliyadhītaraṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said to her:

segs.p: “Bhojanaṁ, suppavāse, dentī ariyasāvikā paṭiggāhakānaṁ cattāri ṭhānāni deti.
segs.e: “Suppavāsā, when a noble disciple gives food, she gives the recipients four things.
What four?

segs.p: Āyuṁ deti, vaṇṇaṁ deti, sukhaṁ deti, balaṁ deti.
segs.e: Long life, beauty, happiness, and strength.

segs.p: Āyuṁ kho pana datvā āyussa bhāginī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
segs.e: Giving long life, she has long life as a god or human.

segs.p: Vaṇṇaṁ datvā vaṇṇassa bhāginī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
segs.e: Giving beauty, she has beauty as a god or human.

segs.p: Sukhaṁ datvā sukhassa bhāginī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
segs.e: Giving happiness, she has happiness as a god or human.

segs.p: Balaṁ datvā balassa bhāginī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
segs.e: Giving strength, she has strength as a god or human.

segs.p: Bhojanaṁ, suppavāse, dentī ariyasāvikā paṭiggāhakānaṁ imāni cattāri ṭhānāni detīti.
segs.e: When a noble disciple gives food, she gives the recipients these four things.
When she gives well-prepared food,
pure, fine, and full of flavor,
that offering—given to the sincere,
who have good conduct, and are big-hearted—
joins merit to merit. It’s very fruitful,
and is praised by those who know the world.
Those who recall such sacrifices,
live in the world full of inspiration.
They’ve driven out the stain of stinginess, <j>root and all,
blameless, they go to a heavenly place.”
Numbered Discourses 4.58
6. Overflowing Merit
Sudatta

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Bhojanaṁ, gahapati, dadamāno ariyasāvako paṭiggāhakānaṁ cattāri ṭhānāni deti.
segs.e: “Householder, when a noble disciple gives food, they give the recipients four things.
What four?

segs.p: Āyuṁ deti, vaṇṇaṁ deti, sukhaṁ deti, balaṁ deti.
segs.e: Long life, beauty, happiness, and strength.

segs.p: Āyuṁ kho pana datvā āyussa bhāgī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
segs.e: Giving long life, they have long life as a god or human. …

segs.p: Vaṇṇaṁ datvā … sukhaṁ datvā … balaṁ datvā balassa bhāgī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
segs.e: Giving beauty … happiness … strength …

segs.p: Bhojanaṁ, gahapati, dadamāno ariyasāvako paṭiggāhakānaṁ imāni cattāri ṭhānāni detīti.
segs.e: When a noble disciple gives food, they give the recipients these four things.
Carefully giving food at the right time,
to those who are disciplined, <j>eating only what others give,
you provide them with four things:
long life, beauty, happiness, and strength.
A person who gives long life, beauty,
happiness, and strength,
has long life and fame
wherever they’re reborn.”
Numbered Discourses 4.59
6. Overflowing Merit
Food

segs.p: “Bhojanaṁ, bhikkhave, dadamāno dāyako paṭiggāhakānaṁ cattāri ṭhānāni deti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a donor gives food, they give the recipients four things.
What four?

segs.p: Āyuṁ deti, vaṇṇaṁ deti, sukhaṁ deti, balaṁ deti.
segs.e: Long life, beauty, happiness, and strength. …”

segs.p: Āyuṁ kho pana datvā āyussa bhāgī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
Vaṇṇaṁ datvā … sukhaṁ datvā … balaṁ datvā balassa bhāgī hoti dibbassa vā mānusassa vā.
Bhojanaṁ, bhikkhave, dadamāno dāyako paṭiggāhakānaṁ imāni cattāri ṭhānāni detīti.

segs.e: Numbered Discourses 4.60
6. Overflowing Merit
Lay Practice

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Catūhi kho, gahapati, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako gihisāmīcipaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti yasopaṭilābhiniṁ saggasaṁvattanikaṁ.
segs.e: “Householder, when a noble disciple does four things they are practicing appropriately for a layperson, which brings fame and leads to heaven.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paccupaṭṭhito hoti cīvarena, bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paccupaṭṭhito hoti piṇḍapātena, bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paccupaṭṭhito hoti senāsanena, bhikkhusaṅghaṁ paccupaṭṭhito hoti gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple serves the mendicant Saṅgha with robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Imehi kho, gahapati, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako gihisāmīcipaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti yasopaṭilābhiniṁ saggasaṁvattanikanti.
segs.e: When a noble disciple does these four things they are practicing appropriately for a layperson, which brings fame and leads to heaven.
Those who are astute practice the way
that’s appropriate for laypeople.
They provide those who are ethical
and rightly comported with robes,
almsfood, lodgings,
and supplies for the sick.
Their merit always grows
by day and by night.
They pass on to a place in heaven,
having done excellent deeds.”
Numbered Discourses 4.61
7. Fitting Deeds
Fitting Deeds

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Cattārome, gahapati, dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Householder, these four things, which are likable, desirable, and agreeable are hard to get in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Bhogā me uppajjantu sahadhammenāti, ayaṁ paṭhamo dhammo iṭṭho kanto manāpo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: The first thing is the wish: ‘May wealth come to me by legitimate means!’

segs.p: Bhoge laddhā sahadhammena yaso me āgacchatu saha ñātīhi saha upajjhāyehīti, ayaṁ dutiyo dhammo iṭṭho kanto manāpo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: The second thing, having got wealth by legitimate means, is the wish: ‘May fame come to me, together with my family and mentors.’

segs.p: Bhoge laddhā sahadhammena yasaṁ laddhā saha ñātīhi saha upajjhāyehi ciraṁ jīvāmi dīghamāyuṁ pālemīti, ayaṁ tatiyo dhammo iṭṭho kanto manāpo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: The third thing, having got wealth and fame, is the wish: ‘May I live long, keeping alive for a long time!’

segs.p: Bhoge laddhā sahadhammena yasaṁ laddhā saha ñātīhi saha upajjhāyehi ciraṁ jīvitvā dīghamāyuṁ pāletvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjāmīti, ayaṁ catuttho dhammo iṭṭho kanto manāpo dullabho lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: The fourth thing, having got wealth, fame, and long life, is the wish: ‘When my body breaks up, after death, may I be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm!’

segs.p: Ime kho, gahapati, cattāro dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the four things, which are likable, desirable, and agreeable, but hard to get in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, gahapati, catunnaṁ dhammānaṁ iṭṭhānaṁ kantānaṁ manāpānaṁ dullabhānaṁ lokasmiṁ cattāro dhammā paṭilābhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These next four things lead to the getting of those four things.
What four?
Accomplishment in faith, ethics, generosity, and wisdom.
And what is accomplishment in faith?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi, satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
This is called accomplishment in faith.
And what is accomplishment in ethics?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti …pe… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor.
This is called accomplishment in ethics.
And what is accomplishment in generosity?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vosaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.
This is called accomplishment in generosity.
And what is accomplishment in wisdom?

segs.p: Abhijjhāvisamalobhābhibhūtena, gahapati, cetasā viharanto akiccaṁ karoti, kiccaṁ aparādheti.
segs.e: When your heart is mastered by covetousness and immoral greed, you do what you shouldn’t, and fail to do what you should.

segs.p: Akiccaṁ karonto kiccaṁ aparādhento yasā ca sukhā ca dhaṁsati.
segs.e: Your fame and happiness fall to dust.

segs.p: Byāpādābhibhūtena, gahapati, cetasā viharanto akiccaṁ karoti, kiccaṁ aparādheti.
segs.e: When your heart is mastered by ill will …

segs.p: Akiccaṁ karonto kiccaṁ aparādhento yasā ca sukhā ca dhaṁsati.
Thinamiddhābhibhūtena, gahapati, cetasā viharanto akiccaṁ karoti kiccaṁ aparādheti.
segs.e: dullness and drowsiness …

segs.p: Akiccaṁ karonto kiccaṁ aparādhento yasā ca sukhā ca dhaṁsati.
Uddhaccakukkuccābhibhūtena, gahapati, cetasā viharanto akiccaṁ karoti, kiccaṁ aparādheti.
segs.e: restlessness and remorse …

segs.p: Akiccaṁ karonto kiccaṁ aparādhento yasā ca sukhā ca dhaṁsati.
Vicikicchābhibhūtena, gahapati, cetasā viharanto akiccaṁ karoti, kiccaṁ aparādheti.
segs.e: doubt, you do what you shouldn’t, and fail to do what you should.

segs.p: Akiccaṁ karonto kiccaṁ aparādhento yasā ca sukhā ca dhaṁsati.
segs.e: Your fame and happiness fall to dust.

segs.p: Sa kho so, gahapati, ariyasāvako abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: Knowing that ‘covetousness and immoral greed are corruptions of the mind’, that noble disciple gives them up.

segs.p: Byāpādo cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā byāpādaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: Knowing that ‘ill will …’ …

segs.p: Thinamiddhaṁ cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā thinamiddhaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: ‘dullness and drowsiness …’ …

segs.p: Uddhaccakukkuccaṁ cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: ‘restlessness and remorse …’ …

segs.p: Vicikicchā cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā vicikicchaṁ cittassa upakkilesaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: ‘doubt is a corruption of the mind’, that noble disciple gives it up.

segs.p: Yato ca kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā abhijjhāvisamalobho cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti.
segs.e: When a noble disciple has given up these things,

segs.p: Byāpādo cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā byāpādo cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti.
Thinamiddhaṁ cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā thinamiddhaṁ cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti.
Uddhaccakukkuccaṁ cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā uddhaccakukkuccaṁ cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti.
Vicikicchā cittassa upakkilesoti, iti viditvā vicikicchā cittassa upakkileso pahīno hoti.
Ayaṁ vuccati, gahapati, ariyasāvako mahāpañño puthupañño āpātadaso paññāsampanno.
segs.e: they’re called ‘a noble disciple of great wisdom, of widespread wisdom, who sees what matters, and is accomplished in wisdom’.
This is called accomplishment in wisdom.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, gahapati, catunnaṁ dhammānaṁ iṭṭhānaṁ kantānaṁ manāpānaṁ dullabhānaṁ lokasmiṁ ime cattāro dhammā paṭilābhāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These are the four things that lead to the getting of the four things, which are likable, desirable, and agreeable, but hard to get in the world.

segs.p: Sa kho so, gahapati, ariyasāvako uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi cattāri pattakammāni kattā hoti.
segs.e: There are four fitting deeds that a noble disciple does with the legitimate wealth he has earned by his efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi attānaṁ sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: To start with, with his legitimate wealth he makes himself happy and pleased, keeping himself properly happy.

segs.p: Mātāpitaro sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: He makes his mother and father happy …

segs.p: Puttadāradāsakammakaraporise sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: He makes his children, partners, bondservants, workers, and staff happy …

segs.p: Mittāmacce sukheti pīṇeti sammā sukhaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: He makes his friends and colleagues happy …

segs.p: Idamassa paṭhamaṁ ṭhānagataṁ hoti pattagataṁ āyatanaso paribhuttaṁ.
segs.e: This is his first usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, ariyasāvako uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi yā tā honti āpadā aggito vā udakato vā rājato vā corato vā appiyato vā dāyādato, tathārūpāsu āpadāsu pariyodhāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: Furthermore, with his legitimate wealth he defends himself against threats from such things as fire, flood, rulers, bandits, or unloved heirs.
He keeps himself safe.

segs.p: Idamassa dutiyaṁ ṭhānagataṁ hoti pattagataṁ āyatanaso paribhuttaṁ.
segs.e: This is his second usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, ariyasāvako uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi pañcabaliṁ kattā hoti—
segs.e: Furthermore, with his legitimate wealth he makes five spirit-offerings:
to relatives, guests, ancestors, king, and deities.

segs.p: Idamassa tatiyaṁ ṭhānagataṁ hoti pattagataṁ āyatanaso paribhuttaṁ.
segs.e: This is his third expenditure in an appropriate sphere on a deserved and fitting cause.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, ariyasāvako uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā madappamādā paṭiviratā khantisoracce niviṭṭhā ekamattānaṁ damenti, ekamattānaṁ samenti, ekamattānaṁ parinibbāpenti, tathārūpesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu uddhaggikaṁ dakkhiṇaṁ patiṭṭhāpeti sovaggikaṁ sukhavipākaṁ saggasaṁvattanikaṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, with his legitimate wealth he establishes an uplifting religious donation for ascetics and brahmins—those who refrain from intoxication and negligence, are settled in patience and gentleness, and who tame, calm, and extinguish themselves—that’s conducive to heaven, ripens in happiness, and leads to heaven.

segs.p: Idamassa catutthaṁ ṭhānagataṁ hoti pattagataṁ āyatanaso paribhuttaṁ.
segs.e: This is his fourth usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

segs.p: Sa kho so, gahapati, ariyasāvako uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi imāni cattāri pattakammāni kattā hoti.
segs.e: These are the four fitting deeds that a noble disciple does with the legitimate wealth he has earned by his efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow.

segs.p: Yassa kassaci, gahapati, aññatra imehi catūhi pattakammehi bhogā parikkhayaṁ gacchanti, ime vuccanti, gahapati, bhogā aṭṭhānagatā apattagatā anāyatanaso paribhuttā.
segs.e: Whatever wealth is spent on something other than these four fitting deeds is said to not be usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.

segs.p: Yassa kassaci, gahapati, imehi catūhi pattakammehi bhogā parikkhayaṁ gacchanti, ime vuccanti, gahapati, bhogā ṭhānagatā pattagatā āyatanaso paribhuttāti.
segs.e: But whatever wealth is spent on these four fitting deeds is said to be usage within means on a deserved and fitting cause.
‘I’ve enjoyed my wealth, <j>supporting those who depend on me;
I’ve overcome losses;
I’ve given uplifting religious donations;
and made the five spirit-offerings.
I have served the ethical and
disciplined spiritual practitioners.
I’ve achieved the goal
for which an astute layperson
wishes to gain wealth.
I don’t regret what I’ve done.’
A mortal man who recollects this
stands firm in the teaching of the noble ones.
They’re praised in this life,
and they depart to rejoice in heaven.”
Numbered Discourses 4.62
7. Fitting Deeds
Debtlessness

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Cattārimāni, gahapati, sukhāni adhigamanīyāni gihinā kāmabhoginā kālena kālaṁ samayena samayaṁ upādāya.
segs.e: “Householder, these four kinds of happiness can be earned by a layperson who enjoys sensual pleasures, depending on time and occasion.
What four?
The happiness of ownership, using wealth, debtlessness, and blamelessness.
And what is the happiness of ownership?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, kulaputtassa bhogā honti uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatā bāhābalaparicitā sedāvakkhittā dhammikā dhammaladdhā.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman owns legitimate wealth that he has earned by his own efforts and initiative, built up with his own hands, gathered by the sweat of the brow.

segs.p: So ‘bhogā me atthi uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatā bāhābalaparicitā sedāvakkhittā dhammikā dhammaladdhā’ti adhigacchati sukhaṁ, adhigacchati somanassaṁ.
segs.e: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.
This is called ‘the happiness of ownership’.
And what is the happiness of using wealth?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, kulaputto uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi paribhuñjati puññāni ca karoti.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman uses his legitimate wealth, and makes merit with it.

segs.p: So ‘uṭṭhānavīriyādhigatehi bhogehi bāhābalaparicitehi sedāvakkhittehi dhammikehi dhammaladdhehi paribhuñjāmi puññāni ca karomī’ti adhigacchati sukhaṁ, adhigacchati somanassaṁ.
segs.e: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.
This is called ‘the happiness of using wealth’.
And what is the happiness of debtlessness?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, kulaputto na kassaci kiñci dhāreti appaṁ vā bahuṁ vā.
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman owes no debt, large or small, to anyone.

segs.p: So ‘na kassaci kiñci dhāremi appaṁ vā bahuṁ vā’ti adhigacchati sukhaṁ, adhigacchati somanassaṁ.
segs.e: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.
This is called ‘the happiness of debtlessness’.
And what is the happiness of blamelessness?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako anavajjena kāyakammena samannāgato hoti, anavajjena vacīkammena samannāgato hoti, anavajjena manokammena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has blameless conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So ‘anavajjenamhi kāyakammena samannāgato, anavajjena vacīkammena samannāgato, anavajjena manokammena samannāgato’ti adhigacchati sukhaṁ, adhigacchati somanassaṁ.
segs.e: When he reflects on this, he’s filled with pleasure and happiness.
This is called ‘the happiness of blamelessness’.

segs.p: Imāni kho, gahapati, cattāri sukhāni adhigamanīyāni gihinā kāmabhoginā kālena kālaṁ samayena samayaṁ upādāyāti.
segs.e: These four kinds of happiness can be earned by a layperson who enjoys sensual pleasures, depending on time and occasion.
Knowing the happiness of debtlessness,
and the extra happiness of possession,
a mortal enjoying the happiness of using wealth,
then discerns clearly with wisdom.
Discerning clearly, a clever person knows
both kinds of happiness:
the other kind is not worth a sixteenth part
of the happiness of blamelessness.”
Numbered Discourses 4.63
7. Fitting Deeds
Living with Divinity

segs.p: “Sabrahmakāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with divinity.

segs.p: Sapubbācariyakāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni, yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with the first tutors.

segs.p: Sapubbadevatāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with the elder gods.

segs.p: Sāhuneyyakāni, bhikkhave, tāni kulāni yesaṁ puttānaṁ mātāpitaro ajjhāgāre pūjitā honti.
segs.e: A family where the children honor their parents in their home is said to live with those worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods.
‘Divinity’ is a term for your parents.
‘First tutors’ is a term for your parents.
‘Elder gods’ is a term for your parents.
‘Worthy of an offering dedicated to the gods’ is a term for your parents.
Why is that?

segs.p: Bahukārā, bhikkhave, mātāpitaro, puttānaṁ āpādakā posakā imassa lokassa dassetāroti.
segs.e: Parents are very helpful to their children, they raise them, nurture them, and show them the world.
Parents are said to be ‘Divinity’
and ‘first tutors’.
They’re worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods <j>from their children,
for they love their offspring.
Therefore an astute person
would revere them and honor them
with food and drink,
clothes and bedding,
by anointing and bathing,
and by washing their feet.
Because they look after
their parents like this,
they’re praised in this life by the astute,
and they depart to rejoice in heaven.”
Numbered Discourses 4.64
7. Fitting Deeds
Hell

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti—
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ nirayeti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
Killing, stealing,
telling lies,
and visiting others’ wives:
astute people don’t praise these things.”
Numbered Discourses 4.65
7. Fitting Deeds
Appearance
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Rūpappamāṇo rūpappasanno, ghosappamāṇo ghosappasanno, lūkhappamāṇo lūkhappasanno, dhammappamāṇo dhammappasanno—
segs.e: There are those whose estimation of and confidence in others is based on their appearance, on their voice, on their mortification, and on principle.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasminti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.
Those who judge on appearance,
and those swayed by a voice,
are full of desire and greed;
those people just don’t understand.
Not knowing what’s inside,
nor seeing what’s outside,
the fool shut in on every side,
gets carried away by a voice.
Not knowing what’s inside,
but discerning what’s outside,
seeing the fruit outside,
they’re also carried away by a voice.
Understanding what’s inside,
and discerning what’s outside,
seeing without hindrances,
they don’t get carried away by a voice.”
Numbered Discourses 4.66
7. Fitting Deeds
Greedy
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
The greedy, the hateful, the delusional, and the conceited.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasminti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.
Full of desire for desirable things,
enjoying things that seem pleasant,
beings veiled by delusion
only tighten their bonds.
Born of greed, born of hate,
born of delusion: the ignorant
do unskillful deeds
that afflict and produce pain.
If you act out of these qualities, <j>that’s what you become.
But men shrouded by ignorance,
are blind, with no eyes to see,
and they never imagine that this could be so.”
Numbered Discourses 4.67
7. Fitting Deeds
The Snake King

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sāvatthiyaṁ aññataro bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅkato hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time a monk in Sāvatthī passed away due to a snake bite.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “idha, bhante, sāvatthiyaṁ aññataro bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṅkato”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, a monk in Sāvatthī has passed away due to a snake bite.”

segs.p: “Na hi nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phari.
segs.e: “Mendicants, that monk mustn’t have spread a mind of love to the four royal snake families.

segs.p: Sace hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phareyya, na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṁ kareyya.
segs.e: If he had, he wouldn’t have died due to a snake bite.
What four?

segs.p: Virūpakkhaṁ ahirājakulaṁ, erāpathaṁ ahirājakulaṁ, chabyāputtaṁ ahirājakulaṁ, kaṇhāgotamakaṁ ahirājakulaṁ.
segs.e: The royal snake families of Virūpakkha, Erāpatha, Chabyāputta, and Kaṇhāgotamaka. …

segs.p: Na hi nūna so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phari.
Sace hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena phareyya, na hi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ahinā daṭṭho kālaṁ kareyya.
Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, imāni cattāri ahirājakulāni mettena cittena pharituṁ attaguttiyā attarakkhāya attaparittāyāti.
segs.e: Mendicants, I urge you to spread a mind of love to the four royal snake families, for your own safety, security, and protection.
I love the Virūpakkhas,
the Erāpathas I love,
I love the Chabyāputtas,
the Kaṇhāgotamakas I love.
I love the footless creatures,
the two-footed I love,
I love the four-footed,
the many-footed I love.
May the footless not harm me!
May I not be harmed by the two-footed!
May the four-footed not harm me!
May I not be harmed by the many-footed!
All sentient beings, all living things,
all creatures, every one:
may they see only nice things,
may bad not come to anyone.
The Buddha is immeasurable,
the teaching is immeasurable,
the Saṅgha is immeasurable.
But limited are reptiles,
snakes and scorpions, centipedes,
spiders and lizards and mice.

segs.p: Katā me rakkhā katā me parittā,
segs.e: I’ve made this safeguard, I’ve made this protection:
go away, creatures!
And so I revere the Blessed One,
I revere the seven perfectly awakened Buddhas.”
Numbered Discourses 4.68
7. Fitting Deeds
Devadatta

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate acirapakkante devadatte.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain, not long after Devadatta had left.

segs.p: Tatra kho bhagavā devadattaṁ ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There the Buddha spoke to the mendicants about Devadatta:
“Possessions, honor, and popularity came to Devadatta for his own ruin and downfall.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kadalī attavadhāya phalaṁ deti, parābhavāya phalaṁ deti;
segs.e: It’s like a banana plant …

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, veḷu attavadhāya phalaṁ deti, parābhavāya phalaṁ deti;
segs.e: or a bamboo …

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, naḷo attavadhāya phalaṁ deti, parābhavāya phalaṁ deti;
segs.e: or a reed, all of which bear fruit to their own ruin and downfall …

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi.
Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, assatarī attavadhāya gabbhaṁ gaṇhāti, parābhavāya gabbhaṁ gaṇhāti;
segs.e: It’s like a mule, which becomes pregnant to its own ruin and downfall.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, attavadhāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādi, parābhavāya devadattassa lābhasakkārasiloko udapādīti.
segs.e: In the same way, possessions, honor, and popularity came to Devadatta for his own ruin and downfall.
The banana plant is destroyed by its own fruit,
as are the bamboo and the reed.
Honor destroys a reprobate,
as pregnancy destroys a mule.”
Numbered Discourses 4.69
7. Fitting Deeds
Effort
“Mendicants, there are these four efforts.
What four?
The efforts to restrain, to give up, to develop, and to preserve.
And what, mendicants, is the effort to restrain?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ anuppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.
This is called the effort to restrain.
And what, mendicants, is the effort to give up?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that bad, unskillful qualities are given up.
This is called the effort to give up.
And what, mendicants, is the effort to develop?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ uppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities arise.
This is called the effort to develop.
And what, mendicants, is the effort to preserve?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: It’s when you generate enthusiasm, try, make an effort, exert the mind, and strive so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.
This is called the effort to preserve.
These are the four efforts.
Restraint and giving up,
development and preservation:
these are the four efforts
taught by the Kinsman of the Sun.
Any mendicant who keenly applies these
may attain the ending of suffering.”
Numbered Discourses 4.70
7. Fitting Deeds
Unprincipled

segs.p: “Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye rājāno adhammikā honti, rājāyuttāpi tasmiṁ samaye adhammikā honti.
segs.e: “At a time when kings are unprincipled, royal officials become unprincipled.

segs.p: Rājāyuttesu adhammikesu brāhmaṇagahapatikāpi tasmiṁ samaye adhammikā honti.
segs.e: When royal officials are unprincipled, brahmins and householders become unprincipled.

segs.p: Brāhmaṇagahapatikesu adhammikesu negamajānapadāpi tasmiṁ samaye adhammikā honti.
segs.e: When brahmins and householders are unprincipled, the people of town and country become unprincipled.
When the people of town and country are unprincipled, the courses of the moon and sun become erratic.

segs.p: Visamaṁ candimasūriyesu parivattantesu visamaṁ nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni parivattanti.
segs.e: … the courses of the stars and constellations …

segs.p: Visamaṁ nakkhattesu tārakarūpesu parivattantesu visamaṁ rattindivā parivattanti.
segs.e: the days and nights …

segs.p: Visamaṁ rattindivesu parivattantesu visamaṁ māsaddhamāsā parivattanti.
segs.e: the months and fortnights …

segs.p: Visamaṁ māsaddhamāsesu parivattantesu visamaṁ utusaṁvaccharā parivattanti.
segs.e: the seasons and years become erratic.

segs.p: Visamaṁ utusaṁvaccharesu parivattantesu visamaṁ vātā vāyanti visamā apañjasā.
segs.e: … the blowing of the winds becomes erratic and chaotic.

segs.p: Visamaṁ vātesu vāyantesu visamesu apañjasesu devatā parikupitā bhavanti.
segs.e: … the deities are angered.

segs.p: Devatāsu parikupitāsu devo na sammā dhāraṁ anuppavecchati.
segs.e: … the heavens don’t provide enough rain.

segs.p: Deve na sammā dhāraṁ anuppavecchante visamapākāni sassāni bhavanti.
segs.e: … the crops ripen erratically.

segs.p: Visamapākāni, bhikkhave, sassāni manussā paribhuñjantā appāyukā honti dubbaṇṇā ca bavhābādhā ca.
segs.e: When people eat crops that have ripened erratically, they become short-lived, ugly, weak, and sickly.

segs.p: Yasmiṁ, bhikkhave, samaye rājāno dhammikā honti, rājāyuttāpi tasmiṁ samaye dhammikā honti.
segs.e: At a time when kings are principled, royal officials become principled.

segs.p: Rājāyuttesu dhammikesu brāhmaṇagahapatikāpi tasmiṁ samaye dhammikā honti.
segs.e: … brahmins and householders …

segs.p: Brāhmaṇagahapatikesu dhammikesu negamajānapadāpi tasmiṁ samaye dhammikā honti.
segs.e: people of town and country become principled.
When the people of town and country are principled, the courses of the sun and moon become regular.

segs.p: Samaṁ candimasūriyesu parivattantesu samaṁ nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni parivattanti.
segs.e: … the stars and constellations …

segs.p: Samaṁ nakkhattesu tārakarūpesu parivattantesu samaṁ rattindivā parivattanti.
segs.e: the days and nights …

segs.p: Samaṁ rattindivesu parivattantesu samaṁ māsaddhamāsā parivattanti.
segs.e: the months and fortnights …

segs.p: Samaṁ māsaddhamāsesu parivattantesu samaṁ utusaṁvaccharā parivattanti.
segs.e: the seasons and years become regular.

segs.p: Samaṁ utusaṁvaccharesu parivattantesu samaṁ vātā vāyanti samā pañjasā.
segs.e: … the blowing of the winds becomes regular and orderly.

segs.p: Samaṁ vātesu vāyantesu samesu pañjasesu devatā aparikupitā bhavanti.
segs.e: … the deities are not angered.

segs.p: Devatāsu aparikupitāsu devo sammā dhāraṁ anuppavecchati.
segs.e: … the heavens provide plenty of rain.

segs.p: Deve sammā dhāraṁ anuppavecchante samapākāni sassāni bhavanti.
segs.e: When the heavens provide plenty of rain, the crops ripen well.

segs.p: Samapākāni, bhikkhave, sassāni manussā paribhuñjantā dīghāyukā ca honti vaṇṇavanto ca balavanto ca appābādhā cāti.
segs.e: When people eat crops that have ripened well, they become long-lived, beautiful, strong, and healthy.
When cattle cross a river,
if the bull goes off course,
they all go off course,
because their leader is off course.
So it is for humans:
when the one deemed chief
behaves badly,
what do you expect the rest to do?
The whole nation sleeps badly,
when the king is unprincipled.
When cattle cross a river,
if the bull goes straight,
they all go straight,
because their leader is straight.
So it is for humans:
when the one deemed chief
does the right thing,
what do you expect the rest to do?
The whole nation sleeps at ease,
when the king is just.”
Numbered Discourses 4.71
8.  Sure Bet
Effort

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu apaṇṇakappaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, bahussuto hoti, āraddhavīriyo hoti, paññavā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, learned, energetic, and wise.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu apaṇṇakappaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāyā”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 4.72
8.  Sure Bet
Right View

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu apaṇṇakappaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.
What four?
Thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness; and right view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu apaṇṇakappaṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti, yoni cassa āraddhā hoti āsavānaṁ khayāyā”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these four things their practice is a sure bet, and they have laid the groundwork for ending the defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 4.73
8.  Sure Bet
A True Person
“Mendicants, an untrue person can be known by four qualities.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti parassa avaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
segs.e: To start with, an untrue person speaks ill of another even when not asked, let alone when asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena parassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of another in full detail, not leaving anything out.
That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti parassa vaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
segs.e: Furthermore, an untrue person doesn’t speak well of another even when asked, let alone when not asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena parassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of another without giving the full details, leaving many things out.
That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti attano avaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
segs.e: Furthermore, an untrue person doesn’t speak ill of themselves even when asked, let alone when not asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena attano avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of themselves without giving the full details, leaving many things out.
That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti attano vaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
segs.e: Furthermore, an untrue person speaks well of themselves even when not asked, let alone when asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena attano vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of themselves in full detail, not leaving anything out.
That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato asappuriso veditabbo.
segs.e: An untrue person can be known by these four qualities.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato sappuriso veditabbo.
segs.e: A true person can be known by four qualities.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti parassa avaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
segs.e: To start with, a true person doesn’t speak ill of another even when asked, let alone when not asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena parassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of another without giving the full details, leaving many things out.
That’s how to know that this is a true person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti parassa vaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
segs.e: Furthermore, a true person speaks well of another even when not asked, let alone when asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena parassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of another in full detail, not leaving anything out.
That’s how to know that this is a true person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti attano avaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
segs.e: Furthermore, a true person speaks ill of themselves even when not asked, let alone when asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena attano avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when led on by questions they speak ill of themselves in full detail, not leaving anything out.
That’s how to know that this is a true person.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti attano vaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
segs.e: Furthermore, a true person doesn’t speak well of themselves even when asked, let alone when not asked.

segs.p: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena attano vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
segs.e: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of themselves without giving the full details, leaving many things out.
That’s how to know that this is a true person.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato sappuriso veditabbo.
segs.e: A true person can be known by these four qualities.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vadhukā yaññadeva rattiṁ vā divaṁ vā ānītā hoti, tāvadevassā tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sassuyāpi sasurepi sāmikepi antamaso dāsakammakaraporisesu.
segs.e: It’s like a bride on the day or night she’s first brought to her husband’s home. Right away she sets up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for her mother and father in law, her husband, and even the bondservants, workers, and staff.

segs.p: Sā aparena samayena saṁvāsamanvāya vissāsamanvāya sassumpi sasurampi sāmikampi evamāha:
segs.e: But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, she’ll even say to her mother and father in law, or to her husband:
‘Go away! What would you know?’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu yaññadeva rattiṁ vā divaṁ vā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti, tāvadevassa tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti bhikkhūsu bhikkhunīsu upāsakesu upāsikāsu antamaso ārāmikasamaṇuddesesu.
segs.e: In the same way, on the day or night a mendicant first goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, right away they set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, and even the monastery workers and novices.

segs.p: So aparena samayena saṁvāsamanvāya vissāsamanvāya ācariyampi upajjhāyampi evamāha:
segs.e: But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, they’ll even say to their tutor or mentor:
‘Go away! What would you know?’
So you should train like this:
‘We will live with hearts like that of a newly wedded bride.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 4.74
8.  Sure Bet
Best (1st)
“Mendicants, these four things are the best.
What four?
The best ethics, immersion, wisdom, and freedom.
These are the four things that are the best.”
Numbered Discourses 4.75
8.  Sure Bet
Best (2nd)
“Mendicants, these four things are the best.
What four?
The best form, feeling, perception, and existence.
These are the four things that are the best.”
Numbered Discourses 4.76
8.  Sure Bet
At Kusinārā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kusinārāyaṁ viharati upavattane mallānaṁ sālavane antarena yamakasālānaṁ parinibbānasamaye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying between a pair of sal trees in the sal forest of the Mallas at Upavattana near Kusinārā at the time of his full extinguishment.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “Siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussapi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha:
segs.e: “Perhaps even a single mendicant has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice. So ask, mendicants! Don’t regret it later, thinking:

segs.p: ‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi, nāsakkhimha bhagavantaṁ sammukhā paṭipucchitun’”ti.
segs.e: ‘We were in the Teacher’s presence and we weren’t able to ask the Buddha a question.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
segs.e: When this was said, the mendicants kept silent.
For a second time the Buddha addressed the mendicants: …

segs.p: “siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussapi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha:
‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi, nāsakkhimha bhagavantaṁ sammukhā paṭipucchitun’”ti.
Dutiyampi kho te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
segs.e: For a second time, the mendicants kept silent.
For a third time the Buddha addressed the mendicants: …

segs.p: “siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, ekabhikkhussapi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā, pucchatha, bhikkhave, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha:
‘sammukhībhūto no satthā ahosi, nāsakkhimha bhagavantaṁ sammukhā paṭipucchitun’”ti.
Tatiyampi kho te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
segs.e: For a third time, the mendicants kept silent.
Then the Buddha said to the mendicants:

segs.p: “siyā kho pana, bhikkhave, satthugāravenapi na puccheyyātha, sahāyakopi, bhikkhave, sahāyakassa ārocetū”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, perhaps you don’t ask out of respect for the Teacher. So let a friend tell a friend.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, te bhikkhū tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
segs.e: When this was said, the mendicants kept silent.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

segs.p: Evaṁ pasanno ahaṁ, bhante. Natthi imasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe ekabhikkhussapi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā”ti.
segs.e: I am quite confident that there’s not even a single mendicant in this Saṅgha who has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice.”

segs.p: “Pasādā kho tvaṁ, ānanda, vadesi. Ñāṇameva hettha, ānanda, tathāgatassa: ‘natthi imasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe ekabhikkhussapi kaṅkhā vā vimati vā buddhe vā dhamme vā saṅghe vā magge vā paṭipadāya vā’.
segs.e: “Ānanda, you speak from faith. But the Realized One knows that there’s not even a single mendicant in this Saṅgha who has doubt or uncertainty regarding the Buddha, the teaching, the Saṅgha, the path, or the practice.

segs.p: Imesañhi, ānanda, pañcannaṁ bhikkhusatānaṁ yo pacchimako bhikkhu so sotāpanno avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.
segs.e: Even the last of these five hundred mendicants is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”
Numbered Discourses 4.77
8.  Sure Bet
Unthinkable

segs.p: “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, acinteyyāni, na cintetabbāni; yāni cintento ummādassa vighātassa bhāgī assa.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these four things are unthinkable. They should not be thought about, and anyone who tries to think about them will go mad or get frustrated.
What four?

segs.p: Buddhānaṁ, bhikkhave, buddhavisayo acinteyyo, na cintetabbo;
segs.e: The domain of the Buddhas …

segs.p: yaṁ cintento ummādassa vighātassa bhāgī assa.
Jhāyissa, bhikkhave, jhānavisayo acinteyyo, na cintetabbo;
segs.e: The domain of one in absorption …

segs.p: yaṁ cintento ummādassa vighātassa bhāgī assa.

segs.e: The results of deeds …

segs.p: yaṁ cintento ummādassa vighātassa bhāgī assa.

segs.e: Speculation about the world …

segs.p: yaṁ cintento ummādassa vighātassa bhāgī assa.
Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri acinteyyāni, na cintetabbāni; yāni cintento ummādassa vighātassa bhāgī assā”ti.
segs.e: These are the four unthinkable things. They should not be thought about, and anyone who tries to think about them will go mad or get frustrated.”
Numbered Discourses 4.78
8.  Sure Bet
A Religious Donation
“Mendicants, there are these four ways of purifying a religious donation.
What four?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato;
segs.e: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the giver, not the recipient.

segs.p: atthi, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati, no dāyakato;
segs.e: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by the recipient, not the giver.

segs.p: atthi, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato;
segs.e: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by neither the giver nor the recipient.

segs.p: atthi, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca.
segs.e: There’s a religious donation that’s purified by both the giver and the recipient.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato?
segs.e: And how is a religious donation purified by the giver, not the recipient?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, dāyako hoti sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo; paṭiggāhakā honti dussīlā pāpadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when the giver is ethical, of good character, but the recipient is unethical, of bad character.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato.
Kathañca, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati, no dāyakato?
segs.e: And how is a religious donation purified by the recipient, not the giver?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, dāyako hoti dussīlo pāpadhammo; paṭiggāhakā honti sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when the giver is unethical, of bad character, but the recipient is ethical, of good character.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā paṭiggāhakato visujjhati, no dāyakato.
Kathañca, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato?
segs.e: And how is a religious donation purified by neither the giver nor the recipient?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, dāyako hoti dussīlo pāpadhammo; paṭiggāhakāpi honti dussīlā pāpadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when both the giver and the recipient are unethical, of bad character.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā neva dāyakato visujjhati, no paṭiggāhakato.
Kathañca, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca?
segs.e: And how is a religious donation purified by both the giver and the recipient?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, dāyako hoti sīlavā kalyāṇadhammo; paṭiggāhakāpi honti sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when both the giver and the recipient are ethical, of good character.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇā dāyakato ceva visujjhati paṭiggāhakato ca.
Imā kho, bhikkhave, catasso dakkhiṇā visuddhiyo”ti.
segs.e: These are the four ways of purifying a religious donation.”
Numbered Discourses 4.79
8.  Sure Bet
Business

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā chedagāminī hoti?
segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why for different people the same kind of business undertaking might fail,

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā na yathādhippāyā hoti?
segs.e: while another doesn’t meet expectations,

segs.p: Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā yathādhippāyā hoti?
segs.e: another meets expectations,

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā parādhippāyā hotī”ti?
segs.e: and another exceeds expectations?”

segs.p: “Idha, sāriputta, ekacco samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā upasaṅkamitvā pavāreti: ‘vadatu, bhante, paccayenā’ti. So yena pavāreti taṁ na deti.
segs.e: “Sāriputta, take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. But they fail to give what’s requested.

segs.p: So ce tato cuto itthattaṁ āgacchati, so yaññadeva vaṇijjaṁ payojeti, sāssa hoti chedagāminī.
segs.e: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake fails.

segs.p: Idha pana, sāriputta, ekacco samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā upasaṅkamitvā pavāreti: ‘vadatu, bhante, paccayenā’ti. So yena pavāreti taṁ na yathādhippāyaṁ deti.
segs.e: Take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. They give what’s requested, but don’t meet expectations.

segs.p: So ce tato cuto itthattaṁ āgacchati, so yaññadeva vaṇijjaṁ payojeti, sāssa na hoti yathādhippāyā.
segs.e: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake doesn’t meet expectations.

segs.p: Idha pana, sāriputta, ekacco samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā upasaṅkamitvā pavāreti: ‘vadatu, bhante, paccayenā’ti. So yena pavāreti taṁ yathādhippāyaṁ deti.
segs.e: Take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. They give what’s requested, meeting expectations.

segs.p: So ce tato cuto itthattaṁ āgacchati, so yaññadeva vaṇijjaṁ payojeti, sāssa hoti yathādhippāyā.
segs.e: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake meets expectations.

segs.p: Idha, sāriputta, ekacco samaṇaṁ vā brāhmaṇaṁ vā upasaṅkamitvā pavāreti: ‘vadatu, bhante, paccayenā’ti. So yena pavāreti taṁ parādhippāyaṁ deti.
segs.e: Take a case where someone goes to an ascetic or brahmin and invites them to ask for what they need. They give what’s requested, exceeding expectations.

segs.p: So ce tato cuto itthattaṁ āgacchati, so yaññadeva vaṇijjaṁ payojeti, sāssa hoti parādhippāyā.
segs.e: When they’ve passed away from that life, if they’re reborn in this place, whatever business they undertake exceeds expectations.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā chedagāminī hoti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why for different people the same kind of business undertaking might fail,

segs.p: Ayaṁ pana, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā na yathādhippāyā hoti.
segs.e: while another doesn’t meet expectations,

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho pana, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā yathādhippāyā hoti.
segs.e: another meets expectations,

segs.p: Ayaṁ pana, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekaccassa tādisāva vaṇijjā payuttā parādhippāyā hotī”ti.
segs.e: and another exceeds expectations.”
Numbered Discourses 4.80
8.  Sure Bet
Persia

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena mātugāmo neva sabhāyaṁ nisīdati, na kammantaṁ payojeti, na kambojaṁ gacchatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why ladies don’t attend council meetings, work for a living, or travel to Persia?”
“Ānanda, ladies are irritable,
jealous,
stingy,
and unintelligent.

segs.p: ayaṁ kho, ānanda, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena mātugāmo neva sabhāyaṁ nisīdati, na kammantaṁ payojeti, na kambojaṁ gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why ladies don’t attend council meetings, work for a living, or travel to Persia.”
Numbered Discourses 4.81
9. Confirmed
Killing Living Creatures

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti—
segs.e: They kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, and lie.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti—
segs.e: They don’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, or lie.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.82
9. Confirmed
Lying

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti—
segs.e: They use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti—
segs.e: They don’t use speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.83
9. Confirmed
Where Criticism Takes You

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?
Without examining or scrutinizing, they praise those deserving of criticism,
and they criticize those deserving of praise.

segs.p: ananuvicca apariyogāhetvā appasādanīye ṭhāne pasādaṁ upadaṁseti, ananuvicca apariyogāhetvā pasādanīye ṭhāne appasādaṁ upadaṁseti—
segs.e: They arouse faith in things that are dubious, and they don’t arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What four?
After examining and scrutinizing, they criticize those deserving of criticism,
and they praise those deserving of praise.

segs.p: anuvicca pariyogāhetvā appasādanīye ṭhāne appasādaṁ upadaṁseti
segs.e: They don’t arouse faith in things that are dubious,

segs.p: anuvicca pariyogāhetvā pasādanīye ṭhāne pasādaṁ upadaṁseti—
segs.e: and they do arouse faith in things that are inspiring.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.84
9. Confirmed
Valuing Anger

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Kodhagaru hoti na saddhammagaru, makkhagaru hoti na saddhammagaru, lābhagaru hoti na saddhammagaru, sakkāragaru hoti na saddhammagaru—
segs.e: They value anger, or denigration, or material things, or honor rather than the true teaching.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Saddhammagaru hoti na kodhagaru, saddhammagaru hoti na makkhagaru, saddhammagaru hoti na lābhagaru, saddhammagaru hoti na sakkāragaru—
segs.e: They value the true teaching rather than anger, or denigration, or material things, or honor.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.85
9. Confirmed
From Darkness to Darkness
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
The dark bound for darkness,
the dark bound for light,
the light bound for darkness, and
the light bound for light.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo tamo hoti tamaparāyaṇo?
segs.e: And how is an individual dark and bound for darkness?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo nīce kule paccājāto hoti—caṇḍālakule vā venakule vā nesādakule vā rathakārakule vā pukkusakule vā dalidde appannapānabhojane kasiravuttike, yattha kasirena ghāsacchādo labbhati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is reborn in a low family—a family of corpse-workers, bamboo-workers, hunters, chariot-makers, or scavengers—poor, with little to eat or drink, where life is tough, and food and shelter are hard to find.

segs.p: So ca hoti dubbaṇṇo duddasiko okoṭimako bavhābādho kāṇo vā kuṇī vā khañjo vā pakkhahato vā, na lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
segs.e: And they’re ugly, unsightly, deformed, sickly—one-eyed, crippled, lame, or half-paralyzed. They don’t get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; or bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: And they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya duccaritaṁ caritvā, manasā duccaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo tamo hoti tamaparāyaṇo.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is dark and bound for darkness.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo tamo hoti jotiparāyaṇo?
segs.e: And how is an individual dark and bound for light?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo nīce kule paccājāto hoti—caṇḍālakule vā venakule vā nesādakule vā rathakārakule vā pukkusakule vā dalidde appannapānabhojane kasiravuttike, yattha kasirena ghāsacchādo labbhati;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is reborn in a low family …

segs.p: so ca hoti dubbaṇṇo duddasiko okoṭimako bavhābādho kāṇo vā kuṇī vā khañjo vā pakkhahato vā na lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
So kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: But they do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena sucaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya sucaritaṁ caritvā, manasā sucaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo tamo hoti jotiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is dark and bound for light.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo joti hoti tamaparāyaṇo?
segs.e: And how is an individual light and bound for darkness?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ucce kule paccājāto hoti—khattiyamahāsālakule vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakule vā gahapatimahāsālakule vā aḍḍhe mahaddhane mahābhoge pahūtajātarūparajate pahūtavittūpakaraṇe pahūtadhanadhaññe;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is reborn in an eminent family—a well-to-do family of aristocrats, brahmins, or householders—rich, affluent, and wealthy, with lots of gold and silver, lots of property and assets, and lots of money and grain.

segs.p: so ca hoti abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato, lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
segs.e: And they’re attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty. They get to have food, drink, clothes, and vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ carati, vācāya duccaritaṁ carati, manasā duccaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: But they do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena duccaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya duccaritaṁ caritvā, manasā duccaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo joti hoti tamaparāyaṇo.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is light and bound for darkness.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo joti hoti jotiparāyaṇo?
segs.e: And how is an individual light and bound for light?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo ucce kule paccājāto hoti—khattiyamahāsālakule vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakule vā gahapatimahāsālakule vā aḍḍhe mahaddhane mahābhoge pahūtajātarūparajate pahūtavittūpakaraṇe pahūtadhanadhaññe;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is reborn in an eminent family …

segs.p: so ca hoti abhirūpo dassanīyo pāsādiko paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgato, lābhī annassa pānassa vatthassa yānassa mālāgandhavilepanassa seyyāvasathapadīpeyyassa.
So kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: And they do good things by way of body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: So kāyena sucaritaṁ caritvā, vācāya sucaritaṁ caritvā, manasā sucaritaṁ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo joti hoti jotiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is light and bound for light.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

one sunk low who rises high,
one risen high who sinks low, and
one risen high who rises higher.

segs.p: … Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
