9. Confirmed
The Son
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
The confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.
And how is an individual a confirmed ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekho hoti pāṭipado;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is a practicing trainee,
who lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhāvasittassa jeṭṭho putto ābhiseko anabhisitto macalappatto;
segs.e: It’s like the eldest son of an anointed aristocratic king. He has not yet been anointed, but is eligible, and has been confirmed in the succession.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sekho hoti pāṭipado, anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ patthayamāno viharati.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant is a practicing trainee, who lives aspiring to the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇamacalo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a confirmed ascetic.
And how is an individual a white lotus ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, no ca kho aṭṭha vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements. But they don’t have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇapuṇḍarīko hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a white lotus ascetic.
And how is an individual a pink lotus ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, aṭṭha ca vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life … And they have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇapadumo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a pink lotus ascetic.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo hoti?
segs.e: And how is an individual a delicate ascetic of ascetics?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yācitova bahulaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ senāsanaṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant usually uses only what they’ve been invited to accept—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—rarely using them without invitation.

segs.p: Yehi kho pana sabrahmacārīhi saddhiṁ viharati, tyassa manāpeneva bahulaṁ kāyakammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ vacīkammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ manokammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena;
segs.e: When living with other spiritual practitioners, they usually find themselves treated agreeably by them by way of body, speech, and mind, and rarely disagreeably.

segs.p: manāpaṁyeva bahulaṁ upahāraṁ upaharanti, appaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: And they are usually presented with agreeable things by them, rarely with disagreeable ones.

segs.p: Yāni kho pana tāni vedayitāni pittasamuṭṭhānāni vā semhasamuṭṭhānāni vā vātasamuṭṭhānāni vā sannipātikāni vā utupariṇāmajāni vā visamaparihārajāni vā opakkamikāni vā kammavipākajāni vā, tāni panassa na bahudeva uppajjanti. Appābādho hoti.
segs.e: They’re healthy, so the various unpleasant feelings—stemming from disorders of bile, phlegm, wind, or their conjunction; or caused by change in weather, by not taking care of yourself, by exertion, or as the result of past deeds—usually don’t come up.

segs.p: Catunnaṁ jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī,
segs.e: They get the four absorptions—blissful meditations in this life that belong to the higher mind—when they want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: And they realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya samaṇesu samaṇasukhumāloti, mameva taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya samaṇesu samaṇasukhumāloti.
segs.e: And if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhikkhave, yācitova bahulaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ piṇḍapātaṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ senāsanaṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito; yācitova bahulaṁ gilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhāraṁ paribhuñjāmi, appaṁ ayācito.
segs.e: For I usually use only what I’ve been invited to accept …

segs.p: Yehi kho pana bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ viharāmi te me manāpeneva bahulaṁ kāyakammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ vacīkammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpeneva bahulaṁ manokammena samudācaranti, appaṁ amanāpena; manāpaṁyeva bahulaṁ upahāraṁ upaharanti, appaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: When living with other mendicants, I am usually treated agreeably by them.  …

segs.p: Yāni kho pana tāni vedayitāni pittasamuṭṭhānāni vā semhasamuṭṭhānāni vā vātasamuṭṭhānāni vā sannipātikāni vā utupariṇāmajāni vā visamaparihārajāni vā opakkamikāni vā kammavipākajāni vā, tāni me na bahudeva uppajjanti. Appābādhohamasmi.
segs.e: I’m healthy …

segs.p: Catunnaṁ kho panasmi jhānānaṁ ābhicetasikānaṁ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṁ nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī,
segs.e: I get the four absorptions when I want, without trouble or difficulty.

segs.p: āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharāmi.
segs.e: And I’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya samaṇesu samaṇasukhumāloti, mameva taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya samaṇesu samaṇasukhumāloti.
segs.e: So if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.88
9. Confirmed
Fetters
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
The confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.
And how is an individual a confirmed ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant—with the ending of three fetters—is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇamacalo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a confirmed ascetic.
And how is an individual a white lotus ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā, rāgadosamohānaṁ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṁ lokaṁ āgantvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant—with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion—is a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇapuṇḍarīko hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a white lotus ascetic.
And how is an individual a pink lotus ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant—with the ending of the five lower fetters—is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇapadumo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a pink lotus ascetic.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo hoti?
segs.e: And how is an individual a delicate ascetic of ascetics?

segs.e: It’s when a mendicant realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇesu samaṇasukhumālo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a delicate ascetic of ascetics.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

Right View
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
The confirmed ascetic, the white lotus ascetic, the pink lotus ascetic, and the delicate ascetic of ascetics.
And how is an individual a confirmed ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo hoti, sammāvāco hoti, sammākammanto hoti, sammāājīvo hoti, sammāvāyāmo hoti, sammāsati hoti, sammāsamādhi hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant has right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇamacalo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a confirmed ascetic.
And how is an individual a white lotus ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo hoti, sammāvāco hoti, sammākammanto hoti, sammāājīvo hoti, sammāvāyāmo hoti, sammāsati hoti, sammāsamādhi hoti, sammāñāṇī hoti, sammāvimutti hoti, no ca kho aṭṭha vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: It’s when they have right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right immersion, right knowledge, and right freedom. But they don’t have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇapuṇḍarīko hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a white lotus ascetic.
And how is an individual a pink lotus ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sammādiṭṭhiko hoti …pe… sammāvimutti hoti, aṭṭha ca vimokkhe kāyena phusitvā viharati.
segs.e: It’s when they have right view … and right freedom. And they do have direct meditative experience of the eight liberations.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo samaṇapadumo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a pink lotus ascetic.

segs.e: And how is an individual a delicate ascetic of ascetics?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yācitova bahulaṁ cīvaraṁ paribhuñjati, appaṁ ayācito …pe… yañhi taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya samaṇesu samaṇasukhumāloti, mameva taṁ, bhikkhave, sammā vadamāno vadeyya samaṇesu samaṇasukhumāloti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant usually uses only what they’ve been invited to accept … And if anyone should be rightly called a delicate ascetic of ascetics, it’s me.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

10. Titans
Titans
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
A titan surrounded by titans,
a titan surrounded by gods,
a god surrounded by titans, and
a god surrounded by gods.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo asuro hoti asuraparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a titan surrounded by titans?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dussīlo hoti pāpadhammo, parisāpissa hoti dussīlā pāpadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character, and their followers are the same.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo asuro hoti asuraparivāro.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a titan surrounded by titans.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo asuro hoti devaparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a titan surrounded by gods?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dussīlo hoti pāpadhammo, parisā ca khvassa hoti sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character, but their followers are ethical, of good character.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo asuro hoti devaparivāro.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a titan surrounded by gods.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo devo hoti asuraparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a god surrounded by titans?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlavā hoti kalyāṇadhammo, parisā ca khvassa hoti dussīlā pāpadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character, but their followers are unethical, of bad character.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo devo hoti asuraparivāro.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a god surrounded by titans.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo devo hoti devaparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a god surrounded by gods?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlavā hoti kalyāṇadhammo, parisāpissa hoti sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character, and their followers are the same.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo devo hoti, devaparivāro.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a god surrounded by gods.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

What four?

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na ceva lābhī hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa na ca lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena ajjhattaṁ cetosamathe patiṭṭhāya adhipaññādhammavipassanāya yogo karaṇīyo.
segs.e: As for the individual who has serenity but not discernment: grounded on serenity, they should practice meditation to get discernment.

segs.p: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya na lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena adhipaññādhammavipassanāya patiṭṭhāya ajjhattaṁ cetosamathe yogo karaṇīyo.
segs.e: As for the individual who has discernment but not serenity: grounded on discernment, they should practice meditation to get serenity.

segs.p: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti adhipaññādhammavipassanāya lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa.
segs.e: After some time they have both discernment and serenity.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo na ceva lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa na ca lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena tesaṁyeva kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: As for the individual who has neither serenity nor discernment: in order to get those skillful qualities, they should apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṁ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya;
segs.e: Suppose your clothes or head were on fire. In order to extinguish it, you’d apply extraordinary enthusiasm, effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, tena puggalena tesaṁyeva kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, in order to get those skillful qualities, that individual should apply extraordinary enthusiasm …

segs.p: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena tesuyeva kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṁ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo.
segs.e: As for the individual who has both serenity and discernment: grounded on those skillful qualities, they should practice meditation further to end the defilements.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

Immersion (3rd)
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo lābhī hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na ceva lābhī hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa na ca lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: One individual has neither internal serenity of heart, nor the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: One individual has both internal serenity of heart, and the higher wisdom of discernment of principles.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: As for the individual who has serenity but not discernment: they should approach someone who has discernment and ask:
‘Reverend, how should conditions be seen?
How should they be comprehended?
How should they be discerned?’
They would answer from their own experience:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ kho, āvuso, saṅkhārā daṭṭhabbā, evaṁ saṅkhārā sammasitabbā, evaṁ saṅkhārā vipassitabbā’ti.
segs.e: ‘This is how conditions should be seen, comprehended, and discerned.’

segs.p: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya na lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: As for the individual who has discernment but not serenity: they should approach someone who has serenity and ask:
‘Reverend, how should the mind be stilled?
How should it be settled?
How should it be unified?
How should it be immersed in samādhi?’
They would answer from their own experience:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ kho, āvuso, cittaṁ saṇṭhapetabbaṁ, evaṁ cittaṁ sannisādetabbaṁ, evaṁ cittaṁ ekodi kātabbaṁ, evaṁ cittaṁ samādahātabban’ti.
segs.e: ‘Reverend, this is how the mind should be stilled, settled, unified, and immersed in samādhi.’

segs.p: So aparena samaye lābhī ceva hoti adhipaññādhammavipassanāya lābhī ca ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa.
segs.e: After some time they have both discernment and serenity.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo na ceva lābhī ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa na ca lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī ceva ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya so upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: As for the individual who has neither serenity nor discernment: they should approach someone who has serenity and discernment and ask:
‘Reverend, how should the mind be stilled?
How should it be settled?
How should it be unified?
How should it be immersed in samādhi?’
How should conditions be seen?
How should they be comprehended?
How should they be discerned?’
They would answer as they’ve seen and known:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ kho, āvuso, cittaṁ saṇṭhapetabbaṁ, evaṁ cittaṁ sannisādetabbaṁ, evaṁ cittaṁ ekodi kātabbaṁ, evaṁ cittaṁ samādahātabbaṁ, evaṁ saṅkhārā daṭṭhabbā, evaṁ saṅkhārā sammasitabbā, evaṁ saṅkhārā vipassitabbā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Reverend, this is how the mind should be stilled, settled, unified, and immersed in samādhi. And this is how conditions should be seen, comprehended, and discerned.’

segs.p: So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.
segs.e: After some time they have both serenity and discernment.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṁ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, tena, bhikkhave, puggalena tesu ceva kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṁ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo.
segs.e: As for the individual who has both serenity and discernment: grounded on those skillful qualities, they should practice meditation further to end the defilements.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.95
10. Titans
A Firebrand
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others;
one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;
one who practices to benefit themselves, but not others; and
one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, chavālātaṁ ubhato padittaṁ, majjhe gūthagataṁ, neva gāme kaṭṭhatthaṁ pharati na araññe (…);
segs.e: Suppose there was a firebrand for lighting a funeral pyre, burning at both ends, and smeared with dung in the middle. It couldn’t be used as timber either in the village or the wilderness.

segs.p: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ puggalaṁ vadāmi yvāyaṁ puggalo nevattahitāya paṭipanno no parahitāya.
segs.e: The individual who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others is like this, I say.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno no attahitāya, ayaṁ imesaṁ dvinnaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: The individual who practices to benefit others, but not themselves, is better than that.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno no parahitāya, ayaṁ imesaṁ tiṇṇaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: The individual who practices to benefit themselves, but not others, is better than both of those.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno parahitāya ca, ayaṁ imesaṁ catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca pāmokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca.
segs.e: But the individual who practices to benefit both themselves and others is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the four.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gavā khīraṁ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṁ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo, sappimaṇḍo tattha aggamakkhāyati;
segs.e: From a cow comes milk, from milk comes curds, from curds come butter, from butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes cream of ghee. And the cream of ghee is said to be the best of these.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yvāyaṁ puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno parahitāya ca, ayaṁ imesaṁ catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ aggo ca seṭṭho ca pāmokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca.
segs.e: In the same way, the individual who practices to benefit both themselves and others is the foremost, best, chief, highest, and finest of the four.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

10. Titans
Removing Greed
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One who practices to benefit themselves, but not others;
one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;
one who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others; and
one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno hoti no parahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit themselves, but not others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā rāgavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, no paraṁ rāgavinayāya samādapeti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual practices to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, but doesn’t encourage others to do the same.

segs.p: attanā dosavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, no paraṁ dosavinayāya samādapeti;
attanā mohavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, no paraṁ mohavinayāya samādapeti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit themselves, but not others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no attahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit others, but not themselves?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā na rāgavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, paraṁ rāgavinayāya samādapeti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t practice to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, but encourages others to remove theirs.

segs.p: attanā na dosavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, paraṁ dosavinayāya samādapeti;
attanā na mohavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, paraṁ mohavinayāya samādapeti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no attahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit others, but not themselves.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo nevattahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit neither themselves nor others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā na rāgavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, no paraṁ rāgavinayāya samādapeti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t practice to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, nor do they encourage others to remove theirs.

segs.p: attanā na dosavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, no paraṁ dosavinayāya samādapeti;
attanā na mohavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, no paraṁ mohavinayāya samādapeti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo nevattahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit neither themselves nor others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno hoti parahitāya ca?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit both themselves and others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā ca rāgavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, parañca rāgavinayāya samādapeti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual practices to remove their own greed, hate, and delusion, and encourages others to remove theirs.

segs.p: attanā ca dosavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, parañca dosavinayāya samādapeti;
attanā ca mohavinayāya paṭipanno hoti, parañca mohavinayāya samādapeti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno hoti parahitāya ca.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit both themselves and others.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.97
10. Titans
Quick-witted
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One who practices to benefit themselves, but not others;
one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;
one who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others; and
one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit themselves, but not others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo khippanisantī ca hoti kusalesu dhammesu, sutānañca dhammānaṁ dhārakajātiko hoti, dhātānañca dhammānaṁ atthūpaparikkhī hoti atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya, dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. They readily memorize the teachings they’ve heard. They examine the meaning of teachings they’ve memorized. Understanding the meaning and the teaching, they practice in line with the teaching.

segs.p: no ca kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, no ca sandassako hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: But they’re not a good speaker and do not enunciate well. Their voice isn’t polished, clear, articulate, and doesn’t express the meaning. They don’t educate, encourage, fire up, and inspire their spiritual companions.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit themselves, but not others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no attahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit others, but not themselves?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na heva kho khippanisantī hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no ca sutānaṁ dhammānaṁ dhārakajātiko hoti, no ca dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthūpaparikkhī hoti, no ca atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is not quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. …

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, sandassako ca hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: But they’re a good speaker. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no attahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit others, but not themselves.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo nevattahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit neither themselves nor others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na heva kho khippanisantī hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no ca sutānaṁ dhammānaṁ dhārakajātiko hoti, no ca dhātānaṁ dhammānaṁ atthūpaparikkhī hoti, no ca atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is not quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. …

segs.p: no ca kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, no ca sandassako hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: Nor are they a good speaker. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo nevattahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit neither themselves nor others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno hoti parahitāya ca?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit both themselves and others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo khippanisantī ca hoti kusalesu dhammesu, sutānañca dhammānaṁ dhārakajātiko hoti, dhātānañca dhammānaṁ atthūpaparikkhī hoti atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya, dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is quick-witted when it comes to skillful teachings. …

segs.p: kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagalāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, sandassako ca hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṁsako sabrahmacārīnaṁ.
segs.e: And they’re a good speaker. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno hoti parahitāya ca.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit both themselves and others.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

10. Titans
Training Rules
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One who practices to benefit themselves, but not others;
one who practices to benefit others, but not themselves;
one who practices to benefit neither themselves nor others; and
one who practices to benefit both themselves and others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit themselves, but not others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, no paraṁ pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor. But they don’t encourage others to do the same.

segs.p: attanā adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, no paraṁ adinnādānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
attanā kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, no paraṁ kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
attanā musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, no paraṁ musāvādā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
attanā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti, no paraṁ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit themselves, but not others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no attahitāya?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit others, but not themselves?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā pāṇātipātā appaṭivirato hoti, paraṁ pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
segs.e: It’s when an individual kills living creatures, steals, commits sexual misconduct, lies, and consumes intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor. But they encourage others to not do these things.

segs.p: attanā adinnādānā appaṭivirato hoti, paraṁ adinnādānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
attanā kāmesumicchācārā appaṭivirato hoti, paraṁ kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
attanā musāvādā appaṭivirato hoti, paraṁ musāvādā veramaṇiyā samādapeti;
attanā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā appaṭivirato hoti, paraṁ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo parahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no attahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit others, but not themselves.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo nevattahitāya paṭipanno hoti no parahitāya?
segs.e: And how does a person practice to benefit neither themselves nor others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā pāṇātipātā appaṭivirato hoti, no paraṁ pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti …pe… attanā surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā appaṭivirato hoti, no paraṁ surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti.
segs.e: It’s when an individual kills, etc. … and doesn’t encourage others to not do these things.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo nevattahitāya paṭipanno hoti, no parahitāya.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit neither themselves nor others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno hoti parahitāya ca?
segs.e: And how does an individual practice to benefit both themselves and others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo attanā ca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, parañca pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti …pe… attanā ca surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti, parañca surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti.
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t kill, etc. … and encourages others to do the same.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo attahitāya ceva paṭipanno hoti parahitāya ca.
segs.e: That’s how an individual practices to benefit both themselves and others.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.100
10. Titans
With Potaliya the Wanderer

segs.p: Atha kho potaliyo paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the wanderer Potaliya went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho potaliyaṁ paribbājakaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side, and the Buddha said to him:
“Potaliya, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, potaliya, ekacco puggalo avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca kho vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: One individual criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly. But they don’t praise those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: Idha pana, potaliya, ekacco puggalo vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca kho avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: Another individual praises those deserving of praise … But they don’t criticize those deserving of criticism …

segs.p: Idha pana, potaliya, ekacco puggalo neva avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: Another individual doesn’t praise those deserving of praise … Nor do they criticize those deserving of criticism …

segs.p: Idha pana, potaliya, ekacco puggalo avaṇṇārahassa ca avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, vaṇṇārahassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
segs.e: Another individual criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly. And they praise those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: Ime kho, potaliya, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, potaliya, catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ katamo te puggalo khamati abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro cā”ti?
segs.e: Of these four individuals, who do you believe to be the finest?”

segs.p: “Cattārome, bho gotama, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
Idha, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca kho vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Idha pana, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca kho avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Idha pana, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo neva avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Idha pana, bho gotama, ekacco puggalo avaṇṇārahassa ca avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, vaṇṇārahassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena.
Ime kho, bho gotama, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
Imesaṁ, bho gotama, catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ yvāyaṁ puggalo neva avaṇṇārahassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, no ca vaṇṇārahassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena;
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, of these four individuals, it is the individual who neither praises those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly; nor criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: ayaṁ me puggalo khamati imesaṁ catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: That is the individual I believe to be the finest.
Why is that?

segs.p: Abhikkantā hesā, bho gotama, yadidaṁ upekkhā”ti.
segs.e: Because, worthy Gotama, equanimity is the best.”

segs.p: Katame cattāro …pe… ime kho, potaliya, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
Imesaṁ kho, potaliya, catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ yvāyaṁ puggalo avaṇṇārahassa ca avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, vaṇṇārahassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena;
segs.e: “Potaliya, of these four individuals, it is the individual who criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly; and praises those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: ayaṁ imesaṁ catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: That is the individual I consider to be the finest.
Why is that?

segs.p: Abhikkantā hesā, potaliya, yadidaṁ tattha tattha kālaññutā”ti.
segs.e: Because, Potaliya, understanding of time and context is the best.”

segs.p: “Cattārome, bho gotama, puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
Katame cattāro …pe… ime kho, bho gotama, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
Imesaṁ, bho gotama, catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ yvāyaṁ puggalo avaṇṇārahassa ca avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena, vaṇṇārahassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā bhūtaṁ tacchaṁ kālena;
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, of these four individuals, it is the individual who criticizes those deserving of criticism at the right time, truthfully and correctly; and praises those deserving of praise at the right time, truthfully and correctly.

segs.p: ayaṁ me puggalo khamati imesaṁ catunnaṁ puggalānaṁ abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: That is the individual I believe to be the finest.
Why is that?

segs.p: Abhikkantā hesā, bho gotama, yadidaṁ tattha tattha kālaññutā.
segs.e: Because, worthy Gotama, understanding of time and context is the best.

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama.
segs.e: Excellent, worthy Gotama! Excellent!

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bho gotama, nikkujjitaṁ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṁ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṁ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṁ dhāreyya: ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti; evamevaṁ bhotā gotamena anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito.
segs.e: As if he were righting the overturned, or revealing the hidden, or pointing out the path to the lost, or lighting a lamp in the dark so people with clear eyes can see what’s there, worthy Gotama has made the teaching clear in many ways.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: I go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 4.101
11. Clouds
Clouds (1st)
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of clouds.
What four?
One thunders but doesn’t rain,
one rains but doesn’t thunder,
one neither thunders nor rains, and
one both rains and thunders.
These are the four kinds of clouds.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro valāhakūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.
What four?
One thunders but doesn’t rain,
one rains but doesn’t thunder,
one neither thunders nor rains, and
one both rains and thunders.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā hoti no vassitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual thunder but not rain?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo bhāsitā hoti, no kattā.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is a talker, not a doer.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā hoti, no vassitā.
segs.e: That’s how an individual thunders but doesn’t rain.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako gajjitā, no vassitā;
segs.e: That individual is like a cloud that thunders but doesn’t rain, I say.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo vassitā hoti, no gajjitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual rain but not thunder?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo kattā hoti, no bhāsitā.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is a doer, not a talker. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo vassitā hoti, no gajjitā.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako vassitā, no gajjitā;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo neva gajjitā hoti, no vassitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual neither thunder nor rain?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo neva bhāsitā hoti, no kattā.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is neither a talker nor a doer. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo neva gajjitā hoti, no vassitā.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako neva gajjitā, no vassitā;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā ca hoti vassitā ca?
segs.e: And how does an individual both thunder and rain?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo bhāsitā ca hoti kattā ca.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is both a talker and a doer. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā ca hoti vassitā ca.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako gajjitā ca vassitā ca;
Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro valāhakūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.102
11. Clouds
Clouds (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of clouds.
What four?
One thunders but doesn’t rain,
one rains but doesn’t thunder,
one neither thunders nor rains, and
one both rains and thunders.
These are the four kinds of clouds.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro valāhakūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.
What four?
One thunders but doesn’t rain,
one rains but doesn’t thunder,
one neither thunders nor rains, and
one both rains and thunders.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā hoti, no vassitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual thunder but not rain?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti, ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: But they don’t truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā hoti, no vassitā.
segs.e: That’s how an individual thunders but doesn’t rain.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako gajjitā, no vassitā;
segs.e: That individual is like a cloud that thunders but doesn’t rain, I say.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo vassitā hoti, no gajjitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual rain but not thunder?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dhammaṁ na pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: But they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo vassitā hoti, no gajjitā.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako vassitā, no gajjitā;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo neva gajjitā hoti, no vassitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual neither thunder nor rain?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo neva dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: Nor do they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo neva gajjitā hoti, no vassitā.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako neva gajjitā, no vassitā;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā ca hoti vassitā ca?
segs.e: And how does an individual both thunder and rain?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: And they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo gajjitā ca hoti vassitā ca.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, valāhako gajjitā ca vassitā ca;
Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro valāhakūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These four individuals similar to clouds are found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.103
11. Clouds
Pots
“Mendicants, there are these four pots.
What four?
Covered but hollow,
uncovered but full,
uncovered and hollow, and
covered and full.
These are the four pots.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro kumbhūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four individuals similar to pots are found in the world.
What four?
Covered but hollow,
uncovered but full,
uncovered and hollow, and
covered and full.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo tuccho hoti pihito?
segs.e: And how is an individual covered but hollow?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekaccassa puggalassa pāsādikaṁ hoti abhikkantaṁ paṭikkantaṁ ālokitaṁ vilokitaṁ samiñjitaṁ pasāritaṁ saṅghāṭipattacīvaradhāraṇaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is impressive when going out and coming back, when looking ahead and aside, when bending and extending the limbs, and when bearing the outer robe, bowl and robes.

segs.p: So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: But they don’t truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo tuccho hoti pihito.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is covered but hollow.

Mice
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of mice.
What four?
One makes a hole but doesn’t live in it,
one lives in a hole but doesn’t make it,
one neither makes a hole nor lives in it, and
one both makes a hole and lives in it.
These are the four kinds of mice.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro mūsikūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four individuals similar to mice are found in the world.
What four?
One makes a hole but doesn’t live in it,
one lives in a hole but doesn’t make it,
one neither makes a hole nor lives in it, and
one both makes a hole and lives in it.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo gādhaṁ kattā hoti no vasitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual make a hole but not live in it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
segs.e: But they don’t really understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo gādhaṁ kattā hoti, no vasitā.
segs.e: That’s how an individual makes a hole but doesn’t live in it.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi sā, bhikkhave, mūsikā gādhaṁ kattā, no vasitā;
segs.e: That individual is like a mouse that makes a hole but doesn’t live in it, I say.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo vasitā hoti, no gādhaṁ kattā?
segs.e: And how does an individual live in a hole but not make it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dhammaṁ na pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
So ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: But they really understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo vasitā hoti, no gādhaṁ kattā.
Seyyathāpi sā, bhikkhave, mūsikā vasitā hoti, no gādhaṁ kattā;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo neva gādhaṁ kattā hoti no vasitā?
segs.e: And how does an individual neither make a hole nor live in it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dhammaṁ na pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t memorize the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.

segs.e: Nor do they really understand: ‘This is suffering’ …

Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo gādhaṁ kattā ca hoti vasitā ca?
segs.e: And how does an individual both make a hole and live in it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: It’s when an individual memorizes the teaching …

Oxen
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of oxen.
What four?
One hostile to its own herd, not others;
one hostile to other herds, not its own;
one hostile to both its own herd and others; and
one hostile to neither its own herd nor others.
These are the four kinds of oxen.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro balībaddūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four individuals similar to oxen are found in the world.
What four?
One hostile to their own herd, not others;
one hostile to other herds, not their own;
one hostile to both their own herd and others; and
one hostile to neither their own herd nor others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo sagavacaṇḍo hoti, no paragavacaṇḍo?
segs.e: And how is an individual hostile to their own herd, not others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sakaparisaṁ ubbejetā hoti, no paraparisaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when an individual intimidates their own followers, not the followers of others.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo sagavacaṇḍo hoti, no paragavacaṇḍo.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is hostile to their own herd, not others.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, balībaddo sagavacaṇḍo, no paragavacaṇḍo;
segs.e: That individual is like an ox that’s hostile to its own herd, not others.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo paragavacaṇḍo hoti, no sagavacaṇḍo?
segs.e: And how is an individual hostile to other herds, not their own?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo paraparisaṁ ubbejetā hoti, no sakaparisaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when an individual intimidates the followers of others, not their own. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo paragavacaṇḍo hoti, no sagavacaṇḍo.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, balībaddo paragavacaṇḍo, no sagavacaṇḍo;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo sagavacaṇḍo ca hoti paragavacaṇḍo ca?
segs.e: And how is an individual hostile to both their own herd and others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sakaparisaṁ ubbejetā hoti paraparisañca.
segs.e: It’s when an individual intimidates their own followers and the followers of others. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo sagavacaṇḍo ca hoti paragavacaṇḍo ca.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, balībaddo sagavacaṇḍo ca paragavacaṇḍo ca;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo neva sagavacaṇḍo hoti no paragavacaṇḍo?
segs.e: And how is an individual hostile to neither their own herd nor others?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo neva sakaparisaṁ ubbejetā hoti, no paraparisañca.
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t intimidate their own followers or the followers of others.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo neva sagavacaṇḍo hoti, no paragavacaṇḍo.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, balībaddo neva sagavacaṇḍo, no paragavacaṇḍo;
Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro balībaddūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These four individuals similar to oxen are found in the world.”
