11. Clouds
Trees
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of tree.
What four?
One is a softwood surrounded by softwoods,
one is a softwood surrounded by hardwoods,
one is a hardwood surrounded by softwoods, and
one is a hardwood surrounded by hardwoods.
These are the four kinds of tree.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro rukkhūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four individuals similar to trees are found in the world.
What four?
One is a softwood surrounded by softwoods,
one is a softwood surrounded by hardwoods,
one is a hardwood surrounded by softwoods, and
one is a hardwood surrounded by hardwoods.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo pheggu hoti phegguparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a softwood surrounded by softwoods?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dussīlo hoti pāpadhammo;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character,
and their followers are the same.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo pheggu hoti phegguparivāro.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is a softwood surrounded by softwoods.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, rukkho pheggu phegguparivāro;
segs.e: That individual is like a softwood tree that’s surrounded by softwoods, I say.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo pheggu hoti sāraparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a softwood surrounded by hardwoods?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo dussīlo hoti pāpadhammo;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is unethical, of bad character,

segs.p: parisā ca khvassa hoti sīlavatī kalyāṇadhammā.
segs.e: but their followers are ethical, of good character. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo pheggu hoti sāraparivāro.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, rukkho pheggu sāraparivāro;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo sāro hoti phegguparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a hardwood surrounded by softwoods?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlavā hoti kalyāṇadhammo;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character,

segs.p: parisā ca khvassa hoti dussīlā pāpadhammā.
segs.e: but their followers are unethical, of bad character. …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo sāro hoti phegguparivāro.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, rukkho sāro phegguparivāro;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo sāro hoti sāraparivāro?
segs.e: And how is an individual a hardwood surrounded by hardwoods?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlavā hoti kalyāṇadhammo;
segs.e: It’s when an individual is ethical, of good character,
and their followers are the same.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo sāro hoti sāraparivāro.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, rukkho sāro sāraparivāro;
Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro rukkhūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These four individuals similar to trees are found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.110
11. Clouds
Vipers
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of viper.
What four?
One whose venom is fast-acting but not lethal,
one whose venom is lethal but not fast-acting,
one whose venom is both fast-acting and lethal, and
one whose venom is neither fast-acting nor lethal.
These are the four kinds of viper.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āsīvisūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four individuals similar to vipers are found in the world.
What four?
One whose venom is fast-acting but not lethal,
one whose venom is lethal but not fast-acting,
one whose venom is both fast-acting and lethal, and
one whose venom is neither fast-acting nor lethal.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo āgataviso hoti, na ghoraviso?
segs.e: And how is an individual’s venom fast-acting but not lethal?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho na dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: but their anger doesn’t linger long.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo āgataviso hoti, na ghoraviso.
segs.e: That’s how an individual’s venom is fast-acting but not lethal.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, āsīviso āgataviso, na ghoraviso;
segs.e: That individual is like a viper whose venom is fast-acting but not lethal.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo ghoraviso hoti, na āgataviso?
segs.e: And how is an individual’s venom lethal but not fast-acting?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na heva kho abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is not often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: but their anger lingers for a long time.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo ghoraviso hoti, na āgataviso.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, āsīviso ghoraviso, na āgataviso;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo āgataviso ca hoti ghoraviso ca?
segs.e: And how is an individual’s venom both fast-acting and lethal?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: and their anger lingers for a long time.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo āgataviso ca hoti ghoraviso ca.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, āsīviso āgataviso ca ghoraviso ca;
Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo nevāgataviso hoti na ghoraviso?
segs.e: And how is an individual’s venom neither fast-acting nor lethal?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na heva kho abhiṇhaṁ kujjhati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual is not often angry,

segs.p: So ca khvassa kodho na dīgharattaṁ anuseti.
segs.e: and their anger doesn’t linger long.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo nevāgataviso hoti, na ghoraviso.
Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, āsīviso nevāgataviso na ghoraviso;
Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro āsīvisūpamā puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These four individuals similar to vipers are found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.111
12. With Kesi
With Kesi

segs.p: Atha kho kesi assadammasārathi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho kesiṁ assadammasārathiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Kesi the horse trainer went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,
“Kesi, you’re known as a horse trainer.

segs.p: Kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, kesi, assadammaṁ vinesī”ti?
segs.e: Just how do you guide a horse in training?”

segs.p: “Ahaṁ kho, bhante, assadammaṁ saṇhenapi vinemi, pharusenapi vinemi, saṇhapharusenapi vinemī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I guide a horse in training sometimes gently, sometimes harshly, and sometimes both gently and harshly.”

segs.p: “Sace te, kesi, assadammo saṇhena vinayaṁ na upeti, pharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, saṇhapharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, kinti naṁ karosī”ti?
segs.e: “Kesi, what do you do with a horse in training that doesn’t follow these forms of training?”

segs.p: “Sace me, bhante, assadammo saṇhena vinayaṁ na upeti, pharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, saṇhapharusena vinayaṁ na upeti;

segs.e: “In that case, sir, I kill it.
Why is that?
So that I don’t disgrace my tutor’s community.
But sir, the Buddha is the supreme guide for those fit for training.

segs.p: Kathaṁ pana, bhante, bhagavā purisadammaṁ vinetī”ti?
segs.e: Just how do you guide a person in training?”

segs.p: “Ahaṁ kho, kesi, purisadammaṁ saṇhenapi vinemi, pharusenapi vinemi, saṇhapharusenapi vinemi.
segs.e: “Kesi, I guide a person in training sometimes gently, sometimes harshly, and sometimes both gently and harshly.
The gentle way is this:

segs.p: iti kāyasucaritaṁ iti kāyasucaritassa vipāko, iti vacīsucaritaṁ iti vacīsucaritassa vipāko, iti manosucaritaṁ iti manosucaritassa vipāko, iti devā, iti manussāti.
segs.e: ‘This is good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is the result of good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is life as a god. This is life as a human.’
The harsh way is this:

segs.p: iti kāyaduccaritaṁ iti kāyaduccaritassa vipāko, iti vacīduccaritaṁ iti vacīduccaritassa vipāko, iti manoduccaritaṁ iti manoduccaritassa vipāko, iti nirayo, iti tiracchānayoni, iti pettivisayoti.
segs.e: ‘This is bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is the result of bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind. This is life in hell. This is life as an animal. This is life as a ghost.’
The both gentle and harsh way is this:

segs.p: iti kāyasucaritaṁ iti kāyasucaritassa vipāko, iti kāyaduccaritaṁ iti kāyaduccaritassa vipāko, iti vacīsucaritaṁ iti vacīsucaritassa vipāko, iti vacīduccaritaṁ iti vacīduccaritassa vipāko, iti manosucaritaṁ iti manosucaritassa vipāko, iti manoduccaritaṁ iti manoduccaritassa vipāko, iti devā, iti manussā, iti nirayo, iti tiracchānayoni, iti pettivisayo”ti.
segs.e: ‘This is good conduct … this is bad conduct …’”

segs.p: “Sace te, bhante, purisadammo saṇhena vinayaṁ na upeti, pharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, saṇhapharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, kinti naṁ bhagavā karotī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what do you do with a person in training who doesn’t follow these forms of training?”

segs.p: “Sace me, kesi, purisadammo saṇhena vinayaṁ na upeti, pharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, saṇhapharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, hanāmi naṁ, kesī”ti.
segs.e: “In that case, Kesi, I kill them.”
“Sir, it’s not appropriate for the Buddha to kill living creatures.
And yet you say
you kill them.”
“It’s true, Kesi,
it’s not appropriate for a Realized One to kill living creatures.

segs.p: Api ca yo purisadammo saṇhena vinayaṁ na upeti, pharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, saṇhapharusena vinayaṁ na upeti, na taṁ tathāgato vattabbaṁ anusāsitabbaṁ maññati, nāpi viññū sabrahmacārī vattabbaṁ anusāsitabbaṁ maññanti.
segs.e: But when a person in training doesn’t follow any of these forms of training, the Realized One doesn’t think they’re worth advising or instructing, and neither do their sensible spiritual companions.
For it is killing in the training of the Noble One

segs.p: yaṁ na tathāgato vattabbaṁ anusāsitabbaṁ maññati, nāpi viññū sabrahmacārī vattabbaṁ anusāsitabbaṁ maññantī”ti.
segs.e: when the Realized One doesn’t think they’re worth advising or instructing, and neither do their sensible spiritual companions.”
“Well, they’re definitely dead

segs.p: yaṁ na tathāgato vattabbaṁ anusāsitabbaṁ maññati, nāpi viññū sabrahmacārī vattabbaṁ anusāsitabbaṁ maññantīti.
segs.e: when the Realized One doesn’t think they’re worth advising or instructing, and neither do their sensible spiritual companions.

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bhante, abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: Excellent, sir! … From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 4.112
12. With Kesi
Speed

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and reckoned a factor of kingship.
What four?
Integrity, speed, patience, and gentleness.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti, rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A fine royal thoroughbred with these four factors is worthy of a king. …

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What four?
Integrity, speed, patience, and gentleness.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.113
12. With Kesi
The Goad

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, bhadrā assājānīyā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, these four fine thoroughbreds are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco bhadro assājānīyo patodacchāyaṁ disvā saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati:
segs.e: One fine thoroughbred is moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho maṁ ajja assadammasārathi kāraṇaṁ kāressati, kimassāhaṁ paṭikaromī’ti.
segs.e: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro assājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo bhadro assājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the first fine thoroughbred found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro assājānīyo na heva kho patodacchāyaṁ disvā saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati, api ca kho lomavedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati:
segs.e: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred isn’t moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, but only when its hairs are struck, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho maṁ ajja assadammasārathi kāraṇaṁ kāressati, kimassāhaṁ paṭikaromī’ti.
segs.e: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro assājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo bhadro assājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the second fine thoroughbred found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro assājānīyo na heva kho patodacchāyaṁ disvā saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati nāpi lomavedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati, api ca kho cammavedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati:
segs.e: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred isn’t moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, nor when its hairs are struck, but only when its hide is struck, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho maṁ ajja assadammasārathi kāraṇaṁ kāressati, kimassāhaṁ paṭikaromī’ti.
segs.e: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro assājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo bhadro assājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the third fine thoroughbred found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro assājānīyo na heva kho patodacchāyaṁ disvā saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati nāpi lomavedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati nāpi cammavedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati, api ca kho aṭṭhivedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati:
segs.e: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred isn’t moved to act when it sees the shadow of the goad, nor when its hairs are struck, nor when its hide is struck, but only when its bone is struck, thinking:

segs.p: ‘kiṁ nu kho maṁ ajja assadammasārathi kāraṇaṁ kāressati, kimassāhaṁ paṭikaromī’ti.
segs.e: ‘What task will the horse trainer have me do today? How should I respond?’

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro assājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbreds are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho bhadro assājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the fourth fine thoroughbred found in the world.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro bhadrā assājānīyā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: These are the four fine thoroughbreds found in the world.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattārome bhadrā purisājānīyā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, these four fine thoroughbred people are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco bhadro purisājānīyo suṇāti:
segs.e: One fine thoroughbred person hears about

segs.p: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā puriso vā dukkhito vā kālaṅkato vā’ti.
segs.e: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town.
They’re moved to act by this,
and strive effectively.

segs.p: Pahitatto kāyena ceva paramasaccaṁ sacchikaroti, paññāya ca ativijjha passati.
segs.e: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, bhadro assājānīyo patodacchāyaṁ disvā saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati;
segs.e: This individual is like the fine thoroughbred

segs.p: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ bhadraṁ purisājānīyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: that’s shaken when it sees the shadow of the goad.

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro purisājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo bhadro purisājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the first fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro purisājānīyo na heva kho suṇāti:
segs.e: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred person doesn’t hear about

segs.p: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā puriso vā dukkhito vā kālaṅkato vā’ti, api ca kho sāmaṁ passati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā dukkhitaṁ vā kālaṅkataṁ vā.
segs.e: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town, but they see it themselves.
They’re moved to act by this,
and strive effectively.

segs.p: Pahitatto kāyena ceva paramasaccaṁ sacchikaroti, paññāya ca ativijjha passati.
segs.e: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, bhadro assājānīyo lomavedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati;
segs.e: This person is like the fine thoroughbred that’s moved to act

segs.p: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ bhadraṁ purisājānīyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: when its hairs are struck.

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro purisājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo bhadro purisājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the second fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro purisājānīyo na heva kho suṇāti:
segs.e: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred person doesn’t hear about

segs.p: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā puriso vā dukkhito vā kālaṅkato vā’ti, nāpi sāmaṁ passati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā dukkhitaṁ vā kālaṅkataṁ vā, api ca khvassa ñāti vā sālohito vā dukkhito vā hoti kālaṅkato vā.
segs.e: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town, nor do they see it themselves, but it happens to their own relative or family member.
They’re moved to act by this,
and strive effectively.

segs.p: Pahitatto kāyena ceva paramasaccaṁ sacchikaroti, paññāya ca ativijjha passati.
segs.e: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, bhadro assājānīyo cammavedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati;
segs.e: This person is like the fine thoroughbred that’s moved to act

segs.p: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ bhadraṁ purisājānīyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: when its skin is struck.

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro purisājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo bhadro purisājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the third fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro purisājānīyo na heva kho suṇāti:
segs.e: Furthermore, one fine thoroughbred person doesn’t hear about

segs.p: ‘amukasmiṁ nāma gāme vā nigame vā itthī vā puriso vā dukkhito vā kālaṅkato vā’ti, nāpi sāmaṁ passati itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā dukkhitaṁ vā kālaṅkataṁ vā, nāpissa ñāti vā sālohito vā dukkhito vā hoti kālaṅkato vā, api ca kho sāmaññeva phuṭṭho hoti sārīrikāhi vedanāhi dukkhāhi tibbāhi kharāhi kaṭukāhi asātāhi amanāpāhi pāṇaharāhi.
segs.e: the suffering or death of a woman or man in such-and-such village or town, nor do they see it themselves, nor does it happen to their own relative or family member, but they themselves are afflicted with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.
They’re moved to act by this,
and strive effectively.

segs.p: Pahitatto kāyena ceva paramasaccaṁ sacchikaroti, paññāya ca ativijjha passati.
segs.e: Applying themselves, they directly realize the ultimate truth, and see it with penetrating wisdom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi so, bhikkhave, bhadro assājānīyo aṭṭhivedhaviddho saṁvijjati saṁvegaṁ āpajjati;
segs.e: This person is like the fine thoroughbred that’s moved to act

segs.p: tathūpamāhaṁ, bhikkhave, imaṁ bhadraṁ purisājānīyaṁ vadāmi.
segs.e: when its bone is struck.

segs.p: Evarūpopi, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhadro purisājānīyo hoti.
segs.e: Some fine thoroughbred people are like that.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho bhadro purisājānīyo santo saṁvijjamāno lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: This is the fourth fine thoroughbred person found in the world.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro bhadrā purisājānīyā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four fine thoroughbred people found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.114
12. With Kesi
A Royal Elephant

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a royal bull elephant with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā ca hoti, hantā ca, khantā ca, gantā ca.
segs.e: A royal bull elephant listens, destroys, endures, and goes fast.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant listen?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo yamenaṁ hatthidammasārathi kāraṇaṁ kāreti—
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens to whatever task the elephant trainer has it do,

segs.p: yadi vā katapubbaṁ yadi vā akatapubbaṁ—
segs.e: whether or not it has done it before.

segs.p: taṁ aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto suṇāti.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo sotā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant listens.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo hantā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant destroy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato hatthimpi hanati, hatthāruhampi hanati, assampi hanati, assāruhampi hanati, rathampi hanati, rathikampi hanati, pattikampi hanati.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle destroys elephants with their riders, horses with their riders, chariots and charioteers, and foot soldiers.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo hantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant destroys.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo khantā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant endure?

segs.p: Idha bhikkhave, rañño nāgo saṅgāmagato khamo hoti sattippahārānaṁ asippahārānaṁ usuppahārānaṁ pharasuppahārānaṁ bheripaṇavasaṅkhatiṇavaninnādasaddānaṁ.
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant in battle endures being struck by spears, swords, arrows, and axes; it endures the thunder of the drums, kettledrums, horns, and cymbals.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo khantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant endures.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo gantā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a royal bull elephant go fast?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo yamenaṁ hatthidammasārathi disaṁ peseti—
segs.e: It’s when a royal bull elephant swiftly goes in whatever direction the elephant trainer sends it,

segs.p: yadi vā gatapubbaṁ yadi vā agatapubbaṁ—
segs.e: whether or not it has been there before.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, rañño nāgo gantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a royal bull elephant goes fast.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño nāgo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A royal bull elephant with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā ca hoti, hantā ca, khantā ca, gantā ca.
segs.e: A mendicant listens, destroys, endures, and goes fast.
And how does a mendicant listen?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye desiyamāne aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasoto dhammaṁ suṇāti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant pays attention, applies the mind, concentrates wholeheartedly, and actively listens when the teaching and training proclaimed by a Realized One is being taught.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sotā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant listens.
And how does a mendicant destroy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti hanati byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti, uppannaṁ byāpādavitakkaṁ …pe… uppannaṁ vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ …pe… uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti hanati byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, dispel them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant destroys.
And how does a mendicant endure?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya, ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ duruttānaṁ durāgatānaṁ vacanapathānaṁ uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant endures cold, heat, hunger, and thirst; the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles; rude and unwelcome criticism; and they put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu khantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant endures.
And how does a mendicant go fast?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāyaṁ disā agatapubbā iminā dīghena addhunā yadidaṁ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbānaṁ, taṁ khippaññeva gantā hoti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant swiftly goes in the direction they’ve never gone before in all this long time; that is, the stilling of all activities, the letting go of all attachments, the ending of craving, fading away, cessation, extinguishment.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu gantā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant goes fast.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.115
12. With Kesi
Things
“Mendicants, there are these four things.
What four?
There is a thing that’s unpleasant to do,
and doing it proves harmful.
There is a thing that’s unpleasant to do,
but doing it proves beneficial.
There is a thing that’s pleasant to do,
but doing it proves harmful.
There is a thing that’s pleasant to do,
and doing it proves beneficial.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṁ ṭhānaṁ amanāpaṁ kātuṁ;
segs.e: Take the thing that’s unpleasant to do,
and doing it proves harmful.

segs.p: idaṁ, bhikkhave, ṭhānaṁ ubhayeneva na kattabbaṁ maññati.
segs.e: This is regarded as a thing that shouldn’t be done on both grounds:
because it’s unpleasant,
and because doing it proves harmful.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, ṭhānaṁ ubhayeneva na kattabbaṁ maññati.
segs.e: This is regarded as a thing that shouldn’t be done on both grounds.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṁ ṭhānaṁ amanāpaṁ kātuṁ;
segs.e: Next, take the thing that’s unpleasant to do,
but doing it proves beneficial.

segs.p: imasmiṁ, bhikkhave, ṭhāne bālo ca paṇḍito ca veditabbo purisathāme purisavīriye purisaparakkame.
segs.e: It is here that you can tell who is foolish and who is astute in regard to human strength, energy, and vigor.
A fool doesn’t reflect:
‘Despite the fact that this thing is unpleasant to do,

segs.p: atha carahidaṁ ṭhānaṁ kayiramānaṁ atthāya saṁvattatī’ti.
segs.e: doing it still proves beneficial.’
They don’t do that thing,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ akayiramānaṁ anatthāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: so that proves harmful.

segs.p: Paṇḍito ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: An astute person does reflect:
‘Even though this thing is unpleasant to do,

segs.p: atha carahidaṁ ṭhānaṁ kayiramānaṁ atthāya saṁvattatī’ti.
segs.e: doing it still proves beneficial.’
They do that thing,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ kayiramānaṁ atthāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: so that proves beneficial.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṁ ṭhānaṁ manāpaṁ kātuṁ;
segs.e: Next, take the thing that’s pleasant to do,
but doing it proves harmful.

segs.p: imasmimpi, bhikkhave, ṭhāne bālo ca paṇḍito ca veditabbo purisathāme purisavīriye purisaparakkame.
segs.e: It is here that you can tell who is foolish and who is astute in regard to human strength, energy, and vigor.
A fool doesn’t reflect:
‘Even though this thing is pleasant to do,

segs.p: atha carahidaṁ ṭhānaṁ kayiramānaṁ anatthāya saṁvattatī’ti.
segs.e: doing it still proves harmful.’
They do that thing,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ kayiramānaṁ anatthāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: and so that proves harmful.

segs.p: Paṇḍito ca kho, bhikkhave, iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: An astute person does reflect:
‘Despite the fact that this thing is pleasant to do,

segs.p: atha carahidaṁ ṭhānaṁ kayiramānaṁ anatthāya saṁvattatī’ti.
segs.e: doing it still proves harmful.’
They don’t do that thing,

segs.p: Tassa taṁ ṭhānaṁ akayiramānaṁ atthāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: so that proves beneficial.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yamidaṁ ṭhānaṁ manāpaṁ kātuṁ, tañca kayiramānaṁ atthāya saṁvattati—
segs.e: Next, take the thing that’s pleasant to do, and doing it proves beneficial.

segs.p: idaṁ, bhikkhave, ṭhānaṁ ubhayeneva kattabbaṁ maññati.
segs.e: This is regarded as a thing that should be done on both grounds:

segs.p: Yampidaṁ ṭhānaṁ manāpaṁ kātuṁ, imināpi naṁ kattabbaṁ maññati;
segs.e: because it’s pleasant,

segs.p: yampidaṁ ṭhānaṁ kayiramānaṁ atthāya saṁvattati, imināpi naṁ kattabbaṁ maññati.
segs.e: and because doing it proves beneficial.

segs.p: Idaṁ, bhikkhave, ṭhānaṁ ubhayeneva kattabbaṁ maññati.
segs.e: This is regarded as a thing that should be done on both grounds.
These are the four things.”
Numbered Discourses 4.116
12. With Kesi
Diligence
“Mendicants, you should be diligent in four situations.
What four?
Give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind; and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind.
Don’t neglect these things.
Give up wrong view; and develop right view.
Don’t neglect this.

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāyaduccaritaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti kāyasucaritaṁ bhāvitaṁ, vacīduccaritaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti vacīsucaritaṁ bhāvitaṁ, manoduccaritaṁ pahīnaṁ hoti manosucaritaṁ bhāvitaṁ, micchādiṭṭhi pahīnā hoti sammādiṭṭhi bhāvitā, so na bhāyati samparāyikassa maraṇassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant who has done these things does not fear death in lives to come.”
Numbered Discourses 4.117
12. With Kesi
Guarding

segs.p: “Catūsu, bhikkhave, ṭhānesu attarūpena appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, in your own way you should practice diligence, mindfulness, and guarding of the mind in four situations.
What four?

segs.p: ‘Mā me rajanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ rajjī’ti attarūpena appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo;
segs.e: ‘May my mind not be aroused by things that arouse greed.’ In your own way you should practice diligence, mindfulness, and guarding of the mind.

segs.p: ‘mā me dosanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ dussī’ti attarūpena appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo;
segs.e: ‘May my mind not be angered by things that provoke hate.’ …

segs.p: ‘mā me mohanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ muyhī’ti attarūpena appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo;
segs.e: ‘May my mind not be deluded by things that promote delusion.’ …

segs.p: ‘mā me madanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ majjī’ti attarūpena appamādo sati cetaso ārakkho karaṇīyo.
segs.e: ‘May my mind not be intoxicated by things that intoxicate.’ …

segs.p: Yato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rajanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ na rajjati vītarāgattā, dosanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ na dussati vītadosattā, mohanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ na muyhati vītamohattā, madanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ na majjati vītamadattā, so na chambhati na kampati na vedhati na santāsaṁ āpajjati, na ca pana samaṇavacanahetupi gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant’s mind is no longer affected by greed, hate, delusion, or intoxication because they’ve got rid of these things, they don’t shake, tremble, quake, or get nervous, nor are they persuaded by the teachings of other ascetics.”
Numbered Discourses 4.118
12. With Kesi
Inspiring

segs.p: “Cattārimāni, bhikkhave, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṁvejanīyāni ṭhānāni.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a faithful gentleman should go to see these four inspiring places.
What four?

segs.p: ‘Idha tathāgato jāto’ti, bhikkhave, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṁ saṁvejanīyaṁ ṭhānaṁ.
segs.e: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One was born!’—that is an inspiring place.

segs.p: ‘Idha tathāgato anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambuddho’ti, bhikkhave, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṁ saṁvejanīyaṁ ṭhānaṁ.
segs.e: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One became awakened as a supreme fully awakened Buddha!’—that is an inspiring place.

segs.p: ‘Idha tathāgato anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavattesī’ti, bhikkhave, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṁ saṁvejanīyaṁ ṭhānaṁ.
segs.e: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One rolled forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma!’—that is an inspiring place.

segs.p: ‘Idha tathāgato anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbuto’ti, bhikkhave, saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyaṁ saṁvejanīyaṁ ṭhānaṁ.
segs.e: Thinking: ‘Here the Realized One was fully quenched in the element of extinguishment, with no residue!’—that is an inspiring place.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri saddhassa kulaputtassa dassanīyāni saṁvejanīyāni ṭhānānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the four inspiring places that a faithful gentleman should go to see.”
Numbered Discourses 4.119
12. With Kesi
Perils (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these four perils.
What four?
The perils of rebirth, old age, sickness, and death.
These are the four perils.”
Numbered Discourses 4.120
12. With Kesi
Perils (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these four perils.
What four?
The perils of fire, water, kings, and bandits.
These are the four perils.”
Numbered Discourses 4.121
13. Fears
Guilt
“Mendicants, there are these four fears.
What four?
The fears of guilt, shame, punishment, and going to a bad place.
And what, mendicants, is the fear of guilt?
It’s when someone reflects:

segs.p: ‘ahañceva kho pana kāyena duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, vācāya duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, manasā duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, kiñca taṁ yaṁ maṁ attā sīlato na upavadeyyā’ti.
segs.e: ‘If I were to do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind, wouldn’t I blame myself for my conduct?’

segs.p: So attānuvādabhayassa bhīto kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti, suddhaṁ attānaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: Being afraid of guilt, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the fear of guilt.
And what, mendicants, is the fear of shame?
It’s when someone reflects:

segs.p: ‘ahañceva kho pana kāyena duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, vācāya duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, manasā duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, kiñca taṁ yaṁ maṁ pare sīlato na upavadeyyun’ti.
segs.e: ‘If I were to do bad things by way of body, speech, and mind, wouldn’t others blame me for my conduct?’

segs.p: So parānuvādabhayassa bhīto kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti, suddhaṁ attānaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: Being afraid of shame, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the fear of shame.
And what, mendicants, is the fear of punishment?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco passati coraṁ āgucāriṁ, rājāno gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārente,
segs.e: It’s when someone sees that the kings have arrested a bandit, a criminal, and subjected them to various punishments—

segs.p: kasāhipi tāḷente, vettehipi tāḷente, addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷente, hatthampi chindante, pādampi chindante, hatthapādampi chindante, kaṇṇampi chindante, nāsampi chindante, kaṇṇanāsampi chindante, bilaṅgathālikampi karonte, saṅkhamuṇḍikampi karonte, rāhumukhampi karonte, jotimālikampi karonte, hatthapajjotikampi karonte, erakavattikampi karonte, cīrakavāsikampi karonte, eṇeyyakampi karonte, balisamaṁsikampi karonte, kahāpaṇakampi karonte, khārāpatacchikampi karonte, palighaparivattikampi karonte, palālapīṭhakampi karonte, tattenapi telena osiñcante, sunakhehipi khādāpente, jīvantampi sūle uttāsente, asināpi sīsaṁ chindante.
segs.e: whipping, caning, and clubbing; cutting off hands or feet, or both; cutting off ears or nose, or both; the ‘porridge pot’, the ‘shell-shave’, the ‘Rāhu’s mouth’, the ‘garland of fire’, the ‘burning hand’, the ‘bulrush twist’, the ‘bark dress’, the ‘antelope’, the ‘meat hook’, the ‘coins’, the ‘caustic pickle’, the ‘twisting bar’, the ‘straw mat’; being splashed with hot oil, being fed to the hounds, being impaled alive, and being beheaded.
They think:

segs.p: ‘yathārūpānaṁ kho pāpakānaṁ kammānaṁ hetu coraṁ āgucāriṁ rājāno gahetvā vividhā kammakāraṇā kārenti, kasāhipi tāḷenti …pe… asināpi sīsaṁ chindanti, ahañceva kho pana evarūpaṁ pāpakammaṁ kareyyaṁ, mampi rājāno gahetvā evarūpā vividhā kammakāraṇā kāreyyuṁ, kasāhipi tāḷeyyuṁ, vettehipi tāḷeyyuṁ, addhadaṇḍakehipi tāḷeyyuṁ, hatthampi chindeyyuṁ, pādampi chindeyyuṁ, hatthapādampi chindeyyuṁ, kaṇṇampi chindeyyuṁ, nāsampi chindeyyuṁ, kaṇṇanāsampi chindeyyuṁ, bilaṅgathālikampi kareyyuṁ, saṅkhamuṇḍikampi kareyyuṁ;
segs.e: ‘If I were to do the same kind of bad deed, the kings would punish me in the same way.’ …

segs.p: rāhumukhampi kareyyuṁ, jotimālikampi kareyyuṁ, hatthapajjotikampi kareyyuṁ, erakavattikampi kareyyuṁ, cīrakavāsikampi kareyyuṁ, eṇeyyakampi kareyyuṁ, balisamaṁsikampi kareyyuṁ, kahāpaṇakampi kareyyuṁ, khārāpatacchikampi kareyyuṁ, palighaparivattikampi kareyyuṁ, palālapīṭhakampi kareyyuṁ, tattenapi telena osiñceyyuṁ, sunakhehipi khādāpeyyuṁ, jīvantampi sūle uttāseyyuṁ, asināpi sīsaṁ chindeyyun’ti.
So daṇḍabhayassa bhīto na paresaṁ pābhataṁ vilumpanto carati.
segs.e: Being afraid of punishment, they don’t steal the belongings of others.
They give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the fear of punishment.
And what, mendicants, is the fear of rebirth in a bad place?
It’s when someone reflects:

segs.p: ‘kāyaduccaritassa kho pāpako vipāko abhisamparāyaṁ, vacīduccaritassa pāpako vipāko abhisamparāyaṁ, manoduccaritassa pāpako vipāko abhisamparāyaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Bad conduct of body, speech, or mind has a bad result in the next life.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana kāyena duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, vācāya duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, manasā duccaritaṁ careyyaṁ, kiñca taṁ yāhaṁ na kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
segs.e: If I were to do such bad things, when my body breaks up, after death, I’d be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’

segs.p: So duggatibhayassa bhīto kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti, vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti, manoduccaritaṁ pahāya manosucaritaṁ bhāveti, suddhaṁ attānaṁ pariharati.
segs.e: Being afraid of rebirth in a bad place, they give up bad conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, and develop good conduct by way of body, speech, and mind, keeping themselves pure.
This is called the fear of rebirth in a bad place.
These are the four fears.”
Numbered Discourses 4.122
13. Fears
The Danger of Waves
“Mendicants, anyone who enters the water should anticipate four dangers.
What four?
The dangers of waves, gharials, whirlpools, and sharks.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri bhayāni udakorohantassa pāṭikaṅkhitabbāni.
segs.e: These are the four dangers that anyone who enters the water should anticipate.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāri bhayāni idhekaccassa kulaputtassa imasmiṁ dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitassa pāṭikaṅkhitabbāni.
segs.e: In the same way, a gentleman gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in this teaching and training should anticipate four dangers.
What four?
The dangers of waves, gharials, whirlpools, and sharks.
And what, mendicants, is the danger of waves?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness, thinking:

segs.p: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto;
segs.e: ‘I’m swamped by rebirth, old age, and death; by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress. I’m swamped by suffering, mired in suffering.

segs.p: appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
segs.e: Hopefully I can make an end to this entire mass of suffering.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ tathā pabbajitaṁ samānaṁ sabrahmacārino ovadanti anusāsanti:
segs.e: When they’ve gone forth, their spiritual companions advise and instruct them:

segs.p: ‘evaṁ te abhikkamitabbaṁ, evaṁ te paṭikkamitabbaṁ, evaṁ te āloketabbaṁ, evaṁ te viloketabbaṁ, evaṁ te samiñjitabbaṁ, evaṁ te pasāritabbaṁ, evaṁ te saṅghāṭipattacīvaraṁ dhāretabban’ti.
segs.e: ‘You should go out like this, and come back like that. You should look to the front like this, and to the side like that. You should contract your limbs like this, and extend them like that. This is how you should bear your outer robe, bowl, and robes.’
They think:

segs.p: ‘mayaṁ kho pubbe agāriyabhūtā samānā aññe ovadāmapi anusāsāmapi.
segs.e: ‘Formerly, as laypeople, we advised and instructed others.

segs.p: Ime panamhākaṁ puttamattā maññe nattamattā maññe ovaditabbaṁ anusāsitabbaṁ maññantī’ti.
segs.e: And now these mendicants—who you’d think were our children or grandchildren—imagine they can advise and instruct us!’

segs.p: So kupito anattamano sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: Angry and upset, they resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ūmibhayassa bhīto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life for fear of the danger of waves.
‘Danger of waves’ is a term for anger and distress.
This is called the danger of waves.
And what, mendicants, is the danger of gharials?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness …

segs.p: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto;
appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.
Tamenaṁ tathā pabbajitaṁ samānaṁ sabrahmacārino ovadanti anusāsanti:
segs.e: When they’ve gone forth, their spiritual companions advise and instruct them:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ te khāditabbaṁ, idaṁ te na khāditabbaṁ, idaṁ te bhuñjitabbaṁ, idaṁ te na bhuñjitabbaṁ, idaṁ te sāyitabbaṁ, idaṁ te na sāyitabbaṁ, idaṁ te pātabbaṁ, idaṁ te na pātabbaṁ, kappiyaṁ te khāditabbaṁ, akappiyaṁ te na khāditabbaṁ, kappiyaṁ te bhuñjitabbaṁ, akappiyaṁ te na bhuñjitabbaṁ, kappiyaṁ te sāyitabbaṁ, akappiyaṁ te na sāyitabbaṁ, kappiyaṁ te pātabbaṁ, akappiyaṁ te na pātabbaṁ, kāle te khāditabbaṁ, vikāle te na khāditabbaṁ, kāle te bhuñjitabbaṁ, vikāle te na bhuñjitabbaṁ, kāle te sāyitabbaṁ, vikāle te na sāyitabbaṁ, kāle te pātabbaṁ, vikāle te na pātabban’ti.
segs.e: ‘You may eat, consume, taste, and drink these things, but not those. You may eat what’s allowable, but not what’s unallowable. You may eat at the right time, but not at the wrong time.’
They think:

segs.p: ‘mayaṁ kho pubbe agāriyabhūtā samānā yaṁ icchāma taṁ khādāma, yaṁ na icchāma na taṁ khādāma;
segs.e: ‘Formerly, as laypeople, we used to eat, consume, taste, and drink what we wanted, not what we didn’t want.

segs.p: yaṁ icchāma taṁ bhuñjāma, yaṁ na icchāma na taṁ bhuñjāma;
yaṁ icchāma taṁ sāyāma, yaṁ na icchāma na taṁ sāyāma;
yaṁ icchāma taṁ pivāma, yaṁ na icchāma na taṁ pivāma;

kappiyampi khādāma akappiyampi khādāma kappiyampi bhuñjāma akappiyampi bhuñjāma kappiyampi sāyāma akappiyampi sāyāma kappiyampi pivāma akappiyampi pivāma, kālepi khādāma vikālepi khādāma kālepi bhuñjāma vikālepi bhuñjāma kālepi sāyāma vikālepi sāyāma kālepi pivāma vikālepi pivāma;
segs.e: We ate and drank both allowable and unallowable things, at the right time and the wrong time.

segs.p: yampi no saddhā gahapatikā divā vikāle paṇītaṁ khādanīyaṁ vā bhojanīyaṁ vā denti, tatrapime mukhāvaraṇaṁ maññe karontī’ti.
segs.e: And these faithful householders give us delicious fresh and cooked foods at the wrong time of day. But these guys imagine they can gag our mouths!’

segs.p: So kupito anattamano sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: Angry and upset, they resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kumbhīlabhayassa bhīto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life for fear of the danger of gharials.
‘Danger of gharials’ is a term for gluttony.
This is called the danger of gharials.
And what, mendicants, is the danger of whirlpools?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness …

segs.p: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi, dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto;
appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.

So evaṁ pabbajito samāno pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya pavisati arakkhiteneva kāyena arakkhitāya vācāya arakkhitena cittena anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā asaṁvutehi indriyehi.
segs.e: When they’ve gone forth, they robe up in the morning and, taking their bowl and robe, enter a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

segs.p: So tattha passati gahapatiṁ vā gahapatiputtaṁ vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitaṁ samaṅgībhūtaṁ paricārayamānaṁ.
segs.e: There they see a householder or their child amusing themselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.
They think:

segs.p: ‘mayaṁ kho pubbe agāriyabhūtā samānā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitā samaṅgībhūtā paricārimhā;
segs.e: ‘Formerly, as laypeople, we amused ourselves, supplied and provided with the five kinds of sensual stimulation.

segs.p: saṁvijjanti kho pana me kule bhogā.
segs.e: And it’s true that my family is wealthy.

segs.p: Sakkā bhoge ca bhuñjituṁ puññāni ca kātuṁ.
segs.e: I can both enjoy my wealth and make merit.

segs.p: Yannūnāhaṁ sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjeyyaṁ puññāni ca kareyyan’ti.
segs.e: Why don’t I resign the training and return to a lesser life, so I can enjoy my wealth and make merit?’
They resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āvaṭṭabhayassa bhīto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life for fear of the danger of whirlpools.

segs.p: Āvaṭṭabhayanti kho, bhikkhave, pañcannetaṁ kāmaguṇānaṁ adhivacanaṁ.
segs.e: ‘Danger of whirlpools’ is a term for the five kinds of sensual stimulation.
This is called the danger of whirlpools.
And what, mendicants, is the danger of sharks?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco kulaputto saddhā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a gentleman has gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness …

segs.p: ‘otiṇṇomhi jātiyā jarāya maraṇena sokehi paridevehi dukkhehi domanassehi upāyāsehi, dukkhotiṇṇo dukkhapareto;
appeva nāma imassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa antakiriyā paññāyethā’ti.

So evaṁ pabbajito samāno pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya gāmaṁ vā nigamaṁ vā piṇḍāya pavisati arakkhiteneva kāyena arakkhitāya vācāya arakkhitena cittena anupaṭṭhitāya satiyā asaṁvutehi indriyehi.
segs.e: When they’ve gone forth, they robe up in the morning and, taking their bowl and robe, enter a village or town for alms without guarding body, speech, and mind, without establishing mindfulness, and without restraining the sense faculties.

segs.p: So tattha passati mātugāmaṁ dunnivatthaṁ vā duppārutaṁ vā.
segs.e: There they see a lady scantily clad, with revealing clothes.

segs.p: Tassa mātugāmaṁ disvā dunnivatthaṁ vā duppārutaṁ vā rāgo cittaṁ anuddhaṁseti.
segs.e: Lust infects their mind,

segs.p: So rāgānuddhaṁsitena cittena sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattati.
segs.e: so they resign the training and return to a lesser life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu susukābhayassa bhīto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvatto.
segs.e: This is called a mendicant who resigns the training and returns to a lesser life because they’re afraid of the danger of sharks.
‘Danger of sharks’ is a term for ladies.
This is called the danger of sharks.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri bhayāni idhekaccassa kulaputtassa imasmiṁ dhammavinaye agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajitassa pāṭikaṅkhitabbānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the four dangers that a gentleman gone forth from the lay life to homelessness in this teaching and training should anticipate.”
Numbered Discourses 4.123
13. Fears
Difference (1st)
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Take an individual who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: Tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno kālaṁ kurumāno brahmakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host.
The lifespan of the gods of the Divinity’s host is one eon.

segs.p: Tattha puthujjano yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā nirayampi gacchati tiracchānayonimpi gacchati pettivisayampi gacchati.
segs.e: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Bhagavato pana sāvako tattha yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā tasmiṁyeva bhave parinibbāyati.
segs.e: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso ayaṁ adhippayāso idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanena, yadidaṁ gatiyā upapattiyā sati.
segs.e: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā ajjhattaṁ sampasādanaṁ cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ avitakkaṁ avicāraṁ samādhijaṁ pītisukhaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take an individual who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, enters and remains in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: Tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno kālaṁ kurumāno ābhassarānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of sublime luminosity.

segs.p: Ābhassarānaṁ, bhikkhave, devānaṁ dve kappā āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of sublime luminosity is two eons.

segs.p: Tattha puthujjano yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā nirayampi gacchati tiracchānayonimpi gacchati pettivisayampi gacchati.
segs.e: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Bhagavato pana sāvako tattha yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā tasmiṁyeva bhave parinibbāyati.
segs.e: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso ayaṁ adhippayāso idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanena, yadidaṁ gatiyā upapattiyā sati.
segs.e: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take an individual who, with the fading away of rapture, enters and remains in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: Tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno, kālaṁ kurumāno subhakiṇhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of universal beauty.

segs.p: Subhakiṇhānaṁ, bhikkhave, devānaṁ cattāro kappā āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of universal beauty is four eons.

segs.p: Tattha puthujjano yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā nirayampi gacchati tiracchānayonimpi gacchati pettivisayampi gacchati.
segs.e: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Bhagavato pana sāvako tattha yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā tasmiṁyeva bhave parinibbāyati.
segs.e: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso ayaṁ adhippayāso idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanena, yadidaṁ gatiyā upapattiyā sati.
segs.e: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take an individual who, with the giving up of pleasure and pain, and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, enters and remains in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: Tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno kālaṁ kurumāno vehapphalānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of abundant fruit.

segs.p: Vehapphalānaṁ, bhikkhave, devānaṁ pañca kappasatāni āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of abundant fruit is five hundred eons.

segs.p: Tattha puthujjano yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā nirayampi gacchati tiracchānayonimpi gacchati pettivisayampi gacchati.
segs.e: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Bhagavato pana sāvako tattha yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā tasmiṁyeva bhave parinibbāyati.
segs.e: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso ayaṁ adhippayāso idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanena, yadidaṁ gatiyā upapattiyā sati.
segs.e: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.124
13. Fears
Difference (2nd)
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Take an individual who, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption …

segs.p: So yadeva tattha hoti rūpagataṁ vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ, te dhamme aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato samanupassati.
segs.e: They contemplate the phenomena there—included in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness—as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā suddhāvāsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the pure abodes.
This rebirth is distinct from that of ordinary people.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, take an individual who, as the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, enters and remains in the second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

segs.p: So yadeva tattha hoti rūpagataṁ vedanāgataṁ saññāgataṁ saṅkhāragataṁ viññāṇagataṁ, te dhamme aniccato dukkhato rogato gaṇḍato sallato aghato ābādhato parato palokato suññato anattato samanupassati.
segs.e: They contemplate the phenomena there—included in form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness—as impermanent, as suffering, as diseased, as a boil, as a dart, as gloom, as an affliction, as alien, as breaking apart, as empty, as not-self.

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā suddhāvāsānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the pure abodes.
This rebirth is distinct from that of ordinary people.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.125
13. Fears
Love (1st)
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: Firstly, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They enjoy this and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: Tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno kālaṁ kurumāno brahmakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the Divinity’s host.
The lifespan of the gods of the Divinity’s host is one eon.

segs.p: Tattha puthujjano yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā nirayampi gacchati tiracchānayonimpi gacchati pettivisayampi gacchati.
segs.e: An ordinary person stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they go to hell or the animal realm or the ghost realm.

segs.p: Bhagavato pana sāvako tattha yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā tasmiṁyeva bhave parinibbāyati.
segs.e: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso ayaṁ adhippayāso idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanena, yadidaṁ gatiyā upapattiyā sati.
segs.e: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo karuṇāsahagatena cetasā …pe…
segs.e: Furthermore, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of compassion … They’re reborn in the company of the gods of sublime luminosity. The lifespan of the gods of sublime luminosity is two eons.
Furthermore, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of rejoicing … They’re reborn in the company of the gods of universal beauty. The lifespan of the gods of universal beauty is four eons.

segs.p: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: Furthermore, an individual meditates spreading a heart full of equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They enjoy this and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: Tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno kālaṁ kurumāno ābhassarānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die

segs.p: Ābhassarānaṁ, bhikkhave, devānaṁ dve kappā āyuppamāṇaṁ …pe… subhakiṇhānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
Subhakiṇhānaṁ, bhikkhave, devānaṁ cattāro kappā āyuppamāṇaṁ …pe… vehapphalānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: they’re reborn in the company of the gods of abundant fruit.

segs.p: Vehapphalānaṁ, bhikkhave, devānaṁ pañca kappasatāni āyuppamāṇaṁ.
segs.e: The lifespan of the gods of abundant fruit is five hundred eons.

segs.p: Tattha puthujjano yāvatāyukaṁ ṭhatvā yāvatakaṁ tesaṁ devānaṁ āyuppamāṇaṁ taṁ sabbaṁ khepetvā nirayampi gacchati tiracchānayonimpi gacchati pettivisayampi gacchati.

segs.e: But a disciple of the Buddha stays there until the lifespan of those gods is spent, then they’re extinguished in that very life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhave, viseso ayaṁ adhippayāso idaṁ nānākaraṇaṁ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā puthujjanena, yadidaṁ gatiyā upapattiyā sati.
segs.e: This is the difference between a learned noble disciple and an unlearned ordinary person, that is, when there is a place of rebirth.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

Numbered Discourses 4.127
13. Fears
Incredible Things About the Realized One (1st)

segs.p: “Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā pātubhavanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, with the appearance of a Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha, four incredible and amazing things appear.
What four?

segs.p: Yadā, bhikkhave, bodhisatto tusitā kāyā cavitvā sato sampajāno mātukucchiṁ okkamati, atha sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: When the being intent on awakening passes away from the host of joyful gods, he’s conceived in his mother’s womb, mindful and aware. And then—in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—an immeasurable, magnificent light appears, surpassing the glory of the gods.

segs.p: Yāpi tā lokantarikā aghā asaṁvutā andhakārā andhakāratimisā yatthapimesaṁ candimasūriyānaṁ evaṁmahiddhikānaṁ evaṁmahānubhāvānaṁ ābhā nānubhonti, tatthapi appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: Even in the boundless gloom of interstellar space—so utterly dark that even the luminosity of the moon and the sun, so mighty and powerful, makes no impression—an immeasurable, magnificent light appears, surpassing the glory of the gods.

segs.p: Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi tenobhāsena aññamaññaṁ sañjānanti:
segs.e: And the sentient beings reborn there recognize each other by that light:
‘So, it seems other sentient beings have been reborn here!’

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the first incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yadā bodhisatto sato sampajāno mātukucchimhā nikkhamati, atha sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the being intent on awakening emerges from his mother’s womb, mindful and aware. And then … an immeasurable, magnificent light appears …

segs.p: Yāpi tā lokantarikā aghā asaṁvutā andhakārā andhakāratimisā yatthapimesaṁ candimasūriyānaṁ evaṁmahiddhikānaṁ evaṁmahānubhāvānaṁ ābhā nānubhonti, tatthapi appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: even in the boundless gloom of interstellar space …

segs.p: Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi tenobhāsena aññamaññaṁ sañjānanti:
Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the second incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yadā tathāgato anuttaraṁ sammāsambodhiṁ abhisambujjhati, atha sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the Realized One awakens to the supreme perfect awakening. And then … an immeasurable, magnificent light appears …

segs.p: Yāpi tā lokantarikā aghā asaṁvutā andhakārā andhakāratimisā yatthapimesaṁ candimasūriyānaṁ evaṁmahiddhikānaṁ evaṁmahānubhāvānaṁ ābhā nānubhonti, tatthapi appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: even in the boundless gloom of interstellar space …

segs.p: Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi tenobhāsena aññamaññaṁ sañjānanti:
Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the third incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, yadā tathāgato anuttaraṁ dhammacakkaṁ pavatteti, atha sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the Realized One rolls forth the supreme Wheel of Dhamma. And then … an immeasurable, magnificent light appears …

segs.p: Yāpi tā lokantarikā aghā asaṁvutā andhakārā andhakāratimisā yatthapimesaṁ candimasūriyānaṁ evaṁmahiddhikānaṁ evaṁmahānubhāvānaṁ ābhā nānubhonti, tatthapi appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso pātubhavati atikkammeva devānaṁ devānubhāvaṁ.
segs.e: even in the boundless gloom of interstellar space …

segs.p: Yepi tattha sattā upapannā tepi tenobhāsena aññamaññaṁ sañjānanti:
Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ catuttho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the fourth incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ime cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā pātubhavantī”ti.
segs.e: With the appearance of a Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, these four incredible and amazing things appear.”
Numbered Discourses 4.128
13. Fears
Incredible Things About the Realized One (2nd)

segs.p: “Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā pātubhavanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, with the appearance of a Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, four incredible and amazing things appear.
What four?
People like clinging, they love it and enjoy it.

segs.p: sā tathāgatena anālaye dhamme desiyamāne sussūsati sotaṁ odahati aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapeti.
segs.e: Yet when a Realized One is teaching the Dhamma of non-clinging, they want to listen, they actively listen, and they try to understand.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ paṭhamo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the first incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.
People like conceit, they love it and enjoy it.

segs.p: Sā tathāgatena mānavinaye dhamme desiyamāne sussūsati sotaṁ odahati aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapeti.
segs.e: Yet when a Realized One is teaching the Dhamma of removing conceit, they want to listen, they actively listen, and they try to understand.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ dutiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the second incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.
People like excitement, they love it and enjoy it.

segs.p: Sā tathāgatena opasamike dhamme desiyamāne sussūsati sotaṁ odahati aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapeti.
segs.e: Yet when a Realized One is teaching the Dhamma of peace, they want to listen, they actively listen, and they try to understand.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ tatiyo acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the third incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.
This population is lost in ignorance, swaddled in their shells.

segs.p: Sā tathāgatena avijjāvinaye dhamme desiyamāne sussūsati sotaṁ odahati aññā cittaṁ upaṭṭhapeti.
segs.e: Yet when a Realized One is teaching the Dhamma of removing ignorance, they want to listen, they actively listen, and they try to understand.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ayaṁ catuttho acchariyo abbhuto dhammo pātubhavati.
segs.e: This is the fourth incredible and amazing thing that appears with the appearance of a Realized One.

segs.p: Tathāgatassa, bhikkhave, arahato sammāsambuddhassa pātubhāvā ime cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā pātubhavantī”ti.
segs.e: With the appearance of a Realized One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha, four incredible and amazing things appear.”
Numbered Discourses 4.129
13. Fears
Incredible Things About Ānanda
“Mendicants, there are these four incredible and amazing things about Ānanda.
What four?

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: If an assembly of monks goes to see Ānanda, they’re uplifted by seeing him

segs.p: Tatra ce ānando dhammaṁ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: and uplifted by hearing him speak.

segs.p: Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti, atha ānando tuṇhī bhavati.
segs.e: And when he falls silent, they’ve never had enough.

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniparisā ānandaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: If an assembly of nuns …

segs.p: Tattha ce ānando dhammaṁ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniparisā hoti, atha ānando tuṇhī bhavati.
Sace, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā ānandaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: laymen …

segs.p: Tatra ce ānando dhammaṁ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā hoti, atha ānando tuṇhī bhavati.
Sace, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā ānandaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: or laywomen goes to see Ānanda, they’re uplifted by seeing him

segs.p: Tatra ce ānando dhammaṁ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: and uplifted by hearing him speak.

segs.p: Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti, atha ānando tuṇhī bhavati.
segs.e: And when he falls silent, they’ve never had enough.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande”ti.
segs.e: These are the four incredible and amazing things about Ānanda.”
Numbered Discourses 4.130
13. Fears

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, acchariyā abbhutā dhammā raññe cakkavattimhi.

segs.p: Atittāva, bhikkhave, khattiyaparisā hoti, atha rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī bhavati.

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇaparisā rājānaṁ cakkavattiṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: If an assembly of brahmins …

segs.p: Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
Atittāva, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇaparisā hoti, atha rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī bhavati.
Sace, bhikkhave, gahapatiparisā rājānaṁ cakkavattiṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: householders …

segs.p: Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
Atittāva, bhikkhave, gahapatiparisā hoti, atha rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī bhavati.
Sace, bhikkhave, samaṇaparisā rājānaṁ cakkavattiṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: or ascetics goes to see a wheel-turning monarch, they’re uplifted by seeing him

segs.p: Tatra ce rājā cakkavattī bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: and uplifted by hearing him speak.

segs.p: Atittāva, bhikkhave, samaṇaparisā hoti, atha rājā cakkavattī tuṇhī bhavati.
segs.e: And when he falls silent, they’ve never had enough.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā raññe cakkavattimhi.
segs.e: These are the four incredible and amazing things about a wheel-turning monarch.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande.
segs.e: In the same way, there are these four incredible and amazing things about Ānanda.
What four?

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā ānandaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: If an assembly of monks goes to see Ānanda, they’re uplifted by seeing him

segs.p: Tatra ce ānando dhammaṁ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: and uplifted by hearing him speak.

segs.p: Atittāva, bhikkhave, bhikkhuparisā hoti, atha ānando tuṇhī bhavati.
segs.e: And when he falls silent, they’ve never had enough.

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniparisā …pe… sace, bhikkhave, upāsakaparisā …pe… sace, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā ānandaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamati, dassanenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: If an assembly of nuns … laymen … or laywomen goes to see Ānanda, they’re uplifted by seeing him

segs.p: Tatra ce ānando dhammaṁ bhāsati, bhāsitenapi sā attamanā hoti.
segs.e: and uplifted by hearing him speak.

segs.p: Atittāva, bhikkhave, upāsikāparisā hoti, atha ānando tuṇhī bhavati.
segs.e: And when he falls silent, they’ve never had enough.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro acchariyā abbhutā dhammā ānande”ti.
segs.e: These are the four incredible and amazing things about Ānanda.”
