14. Individuals
Fetters
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekaccassa puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni honti, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni honti, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni honti.
segs.e: One individual hasn’t given up the lower fetters, the fetters for getting reborn, or the fetters for getting a continued existence.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekaccassa puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni honti, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni honti, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni honti.
segs.e: One individual has given up the lower fetters, but not the fetters for getting reborn, or the fetters for getting a continued existence.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekaccassa puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni honti, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni honti, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni honti.
segs.e: One individual has given up the lower fetters and the fetters for getting reborn, but not the fetters for getting a continued existence.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekaccassa puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni honti, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni honti, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni honti.
segs.e: One individual has given up the lower fetters, the fetters for getting reborn, and the fetters for getting a continued existence.

segs.p: Katamassa, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni?
segs.e: What individual hasn’t given up the lower fetters, the fetters for getting reborn, or the fetters for getting a continued existence?
A once-returner.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni.
segs.e: This is the individual who hasn’t given up the lower fetters, the fetters for getting reborn, or the fetters for getting a continued existence.

segs.p: Katamassa, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni?
segs.e: What individual has given up the lower fetters, but not the fetters for getting reborn, or the fetters for getting a continued existence?
One heading upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni.
Katamassa, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni?
segs.e: What individual has given up the lower fetters and the fetters for getting reborn, but not the fetters for getting a continued existence?
One extinguished between one life and the next.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni.
Katamassa, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni?
segs.e: What individual has given up the lower fetters, the fetters for getting reborn, and the fetters for getting a continued existence?
A perfected one.

segs.p: Imassa kho, bhikkhave, puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, upapattipaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni, bhavapaṭilābhiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

14. Individuals
Eloquence
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One whose elocution is on topic, but not fluent.
One whose elocution is fluent, but not on topic.
One whose elocution is both on topic and fluent.
One whose elocution is neither on topic nor fluent.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

14. Individuals
One Who Understands Immediately
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One who understands immediately, one who understands after detailed explanation, one who needs education, and one who merely learns by rote.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”

14. Individuals
The Fruits of Initiative
“These four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One who lives off the fruit of initiative, but not deeds;
one who lives off the fruit of deeds, but not initiative;
one who lives off the fruit of both deeds and initiative;
one who lives off the fruit of neither initiative nor deeds.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.135
14. Individuals
Blameworthy
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
The blameworthy, the mostly blameworthy, the slightly blameworthy, and the blameless.
And how is an individual blameworthy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sāvajjena kāyakammena samannāgato hoti, sāvajjena vacīkammena samannāgato hoti, sāvajjena manokammena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when an individual does things by way of body, speech, and mind that are blameworthy.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo sāvajjo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is blameworthy.
And how is an individual mostly blameworthy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sāvajjena bahulaṁ kāyakammena samannāgato hoti, appaṁ anavajjena;
segs.e: It’s when an individual does things by way of body, speech, and mind that are mostly blameworthy, but occasionally blameless.

segs.p: sāvajjena bahulaṁ vacīkammena samannāgato hoti, appaṁ anavajjena;
sāvajjena bahulaṁ manokammena samannāgato hoti, appaṁ anavajjena.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo vajjabahulo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is mostly blameworthy.
And how is an individual slightly blameworthy?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo anavajjena bahulaṁ kāyakammena samannāgato hoti, appaṁ sāvajjena;
segs.e: It’s when an individual does things by way of body, speech, and mind that are mostly blameless, but occasionally blameworthy.

segs.p: anavajjena bahulaṁ vacīkammena samannāgato hoti, appaṁ sāvajjena;
anavajjena bahulaṁ manokammena samannāgato hoti, appaṁ sāvajjena.
Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo appavajjo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is slightly blameworthy.
And how is an individual blameless?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo anavajjena kāyakammena samannāgato hoti, anavajjena vacīkammena samannāgato hoti, anavajjena manokammena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: It’s when an individual does things by way of body, speech, and mind that are blameless.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo anavajjo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is blameless.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.136
14. Individuals
Ethics (1st)
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlesu na paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ na paripūrakārī, paññāya na paripūrakārī.
segs.e: One individual has not fulfilled ethics, immersion, or wisdom.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ na paripūrakārī, paññāya na paripūrakārī.
segs.e: One individual has fulfilled ethics, but not immersion or wisdom.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ paripūrakārī, paññāya na paripūrakārī.
segs.e: One individual has fulfilled ethics and immersion, but not wisdom.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlesu paripūrakārī hoti, samādhismiṁ paripūrakārī, paññāya paripūrakārī.
segs.e: One individual has fulfilled ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.137
14. Individuals
Ethics (2nd)
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo na sīlagaru hoti na sīlādhipateyyo, na samādhigaru hoti na samādhādhipateyyo, na paññāgaru hoti na paññādhipateyyo.
segs.e: One individual doesn’t value or submit to ethics, immersion, or wisdom.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlagaru hoti sīlādhipateyyo, na samādhigaru hoti na samādhādhipateyyo, na paññāgaru hoti na paññādhipateyyo.
segs.e: One individual values and submits to ethics, but not to immersion or wisdom.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlagaru hoti sīlādhipateyyo, samādhigaru hoti samādhādhipateyyo, na paññāgaru hoti na paññādhipateyyo.
segs.e: One individual values and submits to ethics and immersion, but not wisdom.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sīlagaru hoti sīlādhipateyyo, samādhigaru hoti samādhādhipateyyo, paññāgaru hoti paññādhipateyyo.
segs.e: One individual values and submits to ethics, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.138
14. Individuals
Retreat
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?
One is on retreat in body, but not mind;
one is on retreat in mind, but not body;
one is on retreat in neither body nor mind; and
one is on retreat in both body and mind.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo nikaṭṭhakāyo hoti anikaṭṭhacitto?
segs.e: And how is an individual on retreat in body, but not mind?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual frequents remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: So tattha kāmavitakkampi vitakketi byāpādavitakkampi vitakketi vihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
segs.e: But they think sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo nikaṭṭhakāyo hoti anikaṭṭhacitto.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is on retreat in body, but not mind.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo anikaṭṭhakāyo hoti nikaṭṭhacitto?
segs.e: And how is an individual on retreat in mind, but not body?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo naheva kho araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: So tattha nekkhammavitakkampi vitakketi abyāpādavitakkampi vitakketi avihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
segs.e: But they think thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo anikaṭṭhakāyo hoti nikaṭṭhacitto.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is on retreat in mind, but not body.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo anikaṭṭhakāyo ca hoti anikaṭṭhacitto ca?
segs.e: And how is an individual on retreat in neither body nor mind?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo naheva kho araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual doesn’t frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: So tattha kāmavitakkampi vitakketi byāpādavitakkampi vitakketi vihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
segs.e: And they think sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo anikaṭṭhakāyo ca hoti anikaṭṭhacitto ca.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is on retreat in neither body nor mind.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo nikaṭṭhakāyo ca hoti nikaṭṭhacitto ca?
segs.e: And how is an individual on retreat in both body and mind?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati.
segs.e: It’s when an individual frequents remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: So tattha nekkhammavitakkampi vitakketi abyāpādavitakkampi vitakketi avihiṁsāvitakkampi vitakketi.
segs.e: And they think thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo nikaṭṭhakāyo ca hoti nikaṭṭhacitto ca.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is on retreat in both body and mind.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.139
14. Individuals
Dhamma Speakers
“Mendicants, there are these four Dhamma speakers.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco dhammakathiko appañca bhāsati asahitañca;
segs.e: One Dhamma speaker speaks little and off topic.

segs.p: parisā cassa na kusalā hoti sahitāsahitassa.
segs.e: And their assembly can’t tell what’s on topic and what’s off topic.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, dhammakathiko evarūpāya parisāya dhammakathikotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Such an assembly regards such a Dhamma speaker simply as a Dhamma speaker.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco dhammakathiko appañca bhāsati sahitañca;
segs.e: One Dhamma speaker speaks little but stays on topic.
And their assembly can tell what’s on topic and what’s off topic.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, dhammakathiko evarūpāya parisāya dhammakathikotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Such an assembly regards such a Dhamma speaker simply as a Dhamma speaker.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco dhammakathiko bahuñca bhāsati asahitañca;
segs.e: One Dhamma speaker speaks much but off topic.

segs.p: parisā cassa na kusalā hoti sahitāsahitassa.
segs.e: And their assembly can’t tell what’s on topic and what’s off topic.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, dhammakathiko evarūpāya parisāya dhammakathikotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Such an assembly regards such a Dhamma speaker simply as a Dhamma speaker.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco dhammakathiko bahuñca bhāsati sahitañca;
segs.e: One Dhamma speaker speaks much and stays on topic.
And their assembly can tell what’s on topic and what’s off topic.

segs.p: Evarūpo, bhikkhave, dhammakathiko evarūpāya parisāya dhammakathikotveva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: Such an assembly regards such a Dhamma speaker simply as a Dhamma speaker.
These are the four Dhamma speakers.”
Numbered Discourses 4.140
14. Individuals
Speaker
“Mendicants, there are these four speakers.
What four?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, vādī atthato pariyādānaṁ gacchati, no byañjanato;
segs.e: There’s a speaker who runs out of meaningful things to say, but not of ways of phrasing things.

segs.p: atthi, bhikkhave, vādī byañjanato pariyādānaṁ gacchati, no atthato;
segs.e: There’s a speaker who runs out of ways of phrasing things, but not of meaningful things to say.

segs.p: atthi, bhikkhave, vādī atthato ca byañjanato ca pariyādānaṁ gacchati;
segs.e: There’s a speaker who runs out of both meaningful things to say, and ways of phrasing things.

segs.p: atthi, bhikkhave, vādī nevatthato no byañjanato pariyādānaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: There’s a speaker who never runs out of meaningful things to say, or ways of phrasing things.
These are the four speakers.

segs.p: Aṭṭhānametaṁ, bhikkhave, anavakāso yaṁ catūhi paṭisambhidāhi samannāgato atthato vā byañjanato vā pariyādānaṁ gaccheyyā”ti.
segs.e: It is impossible, it cannot happen that someone accomplished in the four kinds of textual analysis will ever run out of meaningful things to say, or ways of phrasing things.”
Numbered Discourses 4.141
15. Brightness
Brightness
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of brightness.
What four?
The brightness of the moon, sun, fire, and wisdom.
These are the four kinds of brightness.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ catunnaṁ ābhānaṁ yadidaṁ paññābhā”ti.
segs.e: The best of these four kinds of brightness is the brightness of wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 4.142
15. Brightness
Radiance
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of radiance.
What four?
The radiance of the moon, sun, fire, and wisdom.
These are the four kinds of radiance.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imāsaṁ catunnaṁ pabhānaṁ yadidaṁ paññāpabhā”ti.
segs.e: The best of these four kinds of radiance is the radiance of wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 4.143
15. Brightness
Light
“Mendicants, there are these four lights.
What four?
The lights of the moon, sun, fire, and wisdom.
These are the four lights.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ catunnaṁ ālokānaṁ yadidaṁ paññāloko”ti.
segs.e: The best of these four lights is the light of wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 4.144
15. Brightness
Shining
“Mendicants, there are four kinds of shining.
What four?
The shining of the moon, sun, fire, and wisdom.
These are the four kinds of shining.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ catunnaṁ obhāsānaṁ yadidaṁ paññobhāso”ti.
segs.e: The best of these four kinds of shining is the shining of wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 4.145
15. Brightness
Lamps
“Mendicants, there are these four lamps.
What four?
The lamps of the moon, sun, fire, and wisdom.
These are the four lamps.

segs.p: Etadaggaṁ, bhikkhave, imesaṁ catunnaṁ pajjotānaṁ yadidaṁ paññāpajjoto”ti.
segs.e: The best of these four lamps is the lamp of wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 4.146
15. Brightness
Times (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these four times.
What four?

segs.p: Kālena dhammassavanaṁ, kālena dhammasākacchā, kālena sammasanā, kālena vipassanā—
segs.e: A time for listening to the teaching, a time for discussing the teaching, a time for serenity, and a time for discernment.
These are the four times.”
Numbered Discourses 4.147
15. Brightness
Times (2nd)

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, kālā sammā bhāviyamānā sammā anuparivattiyamānā anupubbena āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpenti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when these four times are rightly developed and reiterated, they gradually lead to the ending of defilements.
What four?

segs.p: Kālena dhammassavanaṁ, kālena dhammasākacchā, kālena sammasanā, kālena vipassanā—
segs.e: A time for listening to the teaching, a time for discussing the teaching, a time for serenity, and a time for discernment.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro kālā sammā bhāviyamānā sammā anuparivattiyamānā anupubbena āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpenti.

Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake deve vassante taṁ udakaṁ yathāninnaṁ pavattamānaṁ pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūreti; pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti; kusobbhā paripūrā mahāsobbhe paripūrenti; mahāsobbhā paripūrā kunnadiyo paripūrenti; kunnadiyo paripūrā mahānadiyo paripūrenti; mahānadiyo paripūrā samuddaṁ paripūrenti.
segs.e: It’s like when the heavens rain heavily on a mountain top, and the water flows downhill to fill the hollows, crevices, and creeks. As they become full, they fill up the pools. The pools fill up the lakes, the lakes fill up the streams, and the streams fill up the rivers. And as the rivers become full, they fill up the ocean.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, ime cattāro kālā sammā bhāviyamānā sammā anuparivattiyamānā anupubbena āsavānaṁ khayaṁ pāpentī”ti.
segs.e: In the same way, when these four times are rightly developed and reiterated, they gradually lead to the ending of defilements.”
Numbered Discourses 4.148
15. Brightness
Bad Conduct
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of bad conduct by way of speech.
What four?

segs.p: Musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo—
segs.e: Speech that’s false, backbiting, harsh, or nonsensical.
These are the four kinds of bad conduct by way of speech.”
Numbered Discourses 4.149
15. Brightness
Good Conduct
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of good conduct by way of speech.
What four?

segs.p: Saccavācā, apisuṇā vācā, saṇhā vācā, mantabhāsā—
segs.e: Speech that’s true, harmonious, gentle, and thoughtful.
These are the four kinds of good conduct by way of speech.”
Numbered Discourses 4.150
15. Brightness
Essentials
“Mendicants, there are these four essentials.
What four?
Ethics, immersion, wisdom, and freedom are essentials.
These are the four essentials.”
Numbered Discourses 4.151
16. Faculties
Faculties
“Mendicants, there are these four faculties.
What four?
The faculties of faith, energy, mindfulness, and immersion.
These are the four faculties.”
Numbered Discourses 4.152
16. Faculties
The Power of Faith
“Mendicants, there are these four powers.
What four?
The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, and immersion.
These are the four powers.”
Numbered Discourses 4.153
16. Faculties
The Power of Wisdom
“Mendicants, there are these four powers.
What four?
The powers of wisdom, energy, blamelessness, and inclusiveness.
These are the four powers.”
Numbered Discourses 4.154
16. Faculties
The Power of Mindfulness
“Mendicants, there are these four powers.
What four?
The powers of mindfulness, immersion, blamelessness, and inclusiveness.
These are the four powers.”
Numbered Discourses 4.155
16. Faculties
The Power of Reflection
“Mendicants, there are these four powers.
What four?
The powers of reflection, development, blamelessness, and inclusiveness.
These are the four powers.”
Numbered Discourses 4.156
16. Faculties
Eons
“Mendicants, an eon contains four uncountable periods.
What four?

segs.p: Yadā, bhikkhave, kappo saṁvaṭṭati, taṁ na sukaraṁ saṅkhātuṁ—
segs.e: When an eon contracts, it’s not easy to calculate

segs.p: ettakāni vassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatānīti vā, ettakāni vassasahassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatasahassānīti vā.
segs.e: how many years, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of years it takes.

segs.p: Yadā, bhikkhave, kappo saṁvaṭṭo tiṭṭhati, taṁ na sukaraṁ saṅkhātuṁ—
segs.e: When an eon remains fully contracted, it’s not easy to calculate

segs.p: ettakāni vassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatānīti vā, ettakāni vassasahassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatasahassānīti vā.
segs.e: how many years, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of years it takes.

segs.p: Yadā, bhikkhave, kappo vivaṭṭati, taṁ na sukaraṁ saṅkhātuṁ—
segs.e: When an eon expands, it’s not easy to calculate

segs.p: ettakāni vassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatānīti vā, ettakāni vassasahassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatasahassānīti vā.
segs.e: how many years, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of years it takes.

segs.p: Yadā, bhikkhave, kappo vivaṭṭo tiṭṭhati, taṁ na sukaraṁ saṅkhātuṁ—
segs.e: When an eon remains fully expanded, it’s not easy to calculate

segs.p: ettakāni vassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatānīti vā, ettakāni vassasahassānīti vā, ettakāni vassasatasahassānīti vā.
segs.e: how many years, how many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands of years it takes.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri kappassa asaṅkhyeyyānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the four uncountable periods of an eon.”
Numbered Discourses 4.157
16. Faculties
Illness
“Mendicants, there are two kinds of illness.
What two?

segs.p: Kāyiko ca rogo cetasiko ca rogo.
segs.e: Mental and physical.

segs.p: Dissanti, bhikkhave, sattā kāyikena rogena ekampi vassaṁ ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, dvepi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, tīṇipi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, cattāripi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, pañcapi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, dasapi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, vīsatipi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, tiṁsampi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, cattārīsampi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, paññāsampi vassāni ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā, vassasatampi, bhiyyopi ārogyaṁ paṭijānamānā.
segs.e: Some sentient beings are seen who can claim to be free of physical illness for a year, or two, or three years … even up to a hundred years or more.

segs.p: Te, bhikkhave, sattā sudullabhā lokasmiṁ ye cetasikena rogena muhuttampi ārogyaṁ paṭijānanti, aññatra khīṇāsavehi.
segs.e: But it’s very hard to find any sentient beings in the world who can claim to be free of mental illness even for an hour, apart from those who have ended the defilements.
There are four kinds of illness for those gone forth.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahiccho hoti vighātavā asantuṭṭho itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena.
segs.e: To start with, a mendicant has many wishes, is frustrated, and is not content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: So mahiccho samāno vighātavā asantuṭṭho itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena pāpikaṁ icchaṁ paṇidahati anavaññappaṭilābhāya lābhasakkārasilokappaṭilābhāya.
segs.e: Because of this, they focus their corrupt wishes on status, and on getting material things, honor, and popularity.

segs.p: So uṭṭhahati ghaṭati vāyamati anavaññappaṭilābhāya lābhasakkārasilokappaṭilābhāya.
segs.e: They try hard, strive, and make an effort to get these things.

segs.p: So saṅkhāya kulāni upasaṅkamati, saṅkhāya nisīdati, saṅkhāya dhammaṁ bhāsati, saṅkhāya uccārapassāvaṁ sandhāreti.
segs.e: They have an ulterior motive when they visit families. They have an ulterior motive when they sit down, when they speak on Dhamma, and even when they hold it in when they need to go to the toilet.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro pabbajitassa rogā.
segs.e: These are the four kinds of illness for those gone forth.
So you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘na mahicchā bhavissāma vighātavanto asantuṭṭhā itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, na pāpikaṁ icchaṁ paṇidahissāma anavaññappaṭilābhāya lābhasakkārasilokappaṭilābhāya, na uṭṭhahissāma na ghaṭessāma na vāyamissāma anavaññappaṭilābhāya lābhasakkārasilokappaṭilābhāya, khamā bhavissāma sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ duruttānaṁ durāgatānaṁ vacanapathānaṁ, uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ adhivāsakajātikā bhavissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘We will not have many wishes or be frustrated. We will be content with any kind of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick. We won’t focus our corrupt wishes on status, and on getting material things, honor, and popularity. We won’t try hard, strive, and make an effort to get these things. We will endure cold, heat, hunger, and thirst. We will endure the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles. We will endure rude and unwelcome criticism. We will put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.’
That’s how you should train.”
Numbered Discourses 4.158
16. Faculties
Decline

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:

segs.p: “Yo hi koci, āvuso, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā cattāro dhamme attani samanupassati, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: “Reverends, any monk or nun who sees four things inside themselves should conclude:
‘My skillful qualities are declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls decline.’
What four?

segs.p: Rāgavepullattaṁ, dosavepullattaṁ, mohavepullattaṁ, gambhīresu kho panassa ṭhānāṭhānesu paññācakkhu na kamati.
segs.e: They have much greed, much hate, and much delusion; and their wisdom eye doesn’t go into the many deep matters.

segs.p: Yo hi koci, āvuso, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā ime cattāro dhamme attani samanupassati, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: Any monk or nun who sees these four things inside themselves should conclude:
‘My skillful qualities are declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls decline.’

segs.p: Yo hi koci, āvuso, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā cattāro dhamme attani samanupassati, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: Any monk or nun who sees four things inside themselves should conclude:
‘My skillful qualities are not declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls non-decline.’
What four?

segs.p: Rāgatanuttaṁ, dosatanuttaṁ, mohatanuttaṁ, gambhīresu kho panassa ṭhānāṭhānesu paññācakkhu kamati.
segs.e: Their greed, hate, and delusion grow less; and their wisdom eye goes into the many deep matters.

segs.p: Yo hi koci, āvuso, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā ime cattāro dhamme attani samanupassati, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: Any monk or nun who sees these four things inside themselves should conclude:
‘My skillful qualities are not declining.
For this is what the Buddha calls non-decline.’”
Numbered Discourses 4.159
16. Faculties
Nun
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho aññatarā bhikkhunī aññataraṁ purisaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: And then a certain nun addressed a man,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, yenayyo ānando tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena ayyassa ānandassa pāde sirasā vanda:
segs.e: “Please, my friend, go to the venerable Ānanda, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:
‘Sir, the nun named so-and-so is sick, suffering, and gravely ill.

segs.p: Sā ayyassa ānandassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti. Evañca vadehi:
segs.e: She bows with her head to your feet.’ And then say:

segs.p: ‘sādhu kira, bhante, ayyo ānando yena bhikkhunupassayo yena sā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, please go to the nuns’ quarters to visit that nun out of sympathy.’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, ayye”ti kho so puriso tassā bhikkhuniyā paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, ma’am,” that man replied. He did as the nun asked.

segs.p: Sā āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandati, evañca vadeti:
‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando yena bhikkhunupassayo yena sā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.

segs.e: Ānanda consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena bhikkhunupassayo yena sā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then Ānanda robed up and went to the nuns’ quarters to visit that nun, taking his bowl and robe.

segs.p: Addasā kho sā bhikkhunī āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: That nun saw Ānanda coming off in the distance.
She wrapped herself up from head to foot and laid down on her cot.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena sā bhikkhunī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā ānando taṁ bhikkhuniṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to her, and sat down on the seat spread out. Then Ānanda said to the nun:
“Sister, this body is produced by food. Relying on food,
you should give up food.

segs.p: Taṇhāsambhūto ayaṁ, bhagini, kāyo taṇhaṁ nissāya.
segs.e: This body is produced by craving. Relying on craving,
you should give up craving.

segs.p: Mānasambhūto ayaṁ, bhagini, kāyo mānaṁ nissāya.
segs.e: This body is produced by conceit. Relying on conceit,
you should give up conceit.
This body is produced by sex.
The Buddha spoke of breaking off everything to do with sex.
‘This body is produced by food. Relying on food,

segs.p: Āhāro pahātabbo’ti, iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ.
segs.e: you should give up food.’ This is what I said,
but why did I say it?

segs.p: Idha, bhagini, bhikkhu paṭisaṅkhā yoniso āhāraṁ āhāreti:
segs.e: Take a mendicant who reflects rationally on the food that they eat:

segs.p: ‘neva davāya na madāya na maṇḍanāya na vibhūsanāya, yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya vihiṁsūparatiyā brahmacariyānuggahāya. Iti purāṇañca vedanaṁ paṭihaṅkhāmi, navañca vedanaṁ na uppādessāmi. Yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro cā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Not for fun, indulgence, adornment, or decoration, but only to sustain this body, to avoid harm, and to support spiritual practice. In this way, I shall put an end to old discomfort and not give rise to new discomfort, and I will have the means to keep going, blamelessness, and a comfortable abiding.’

segs.p: So aparena samayena āhāraṁ nissāya āhāraṁ pajahati.
segs.e: After some time, relying on food, they give up food.

segs.p: ‘Āhārasambhūto ayaṁ, bhagini, kāyo āhāraṁ nissāya āhāro pahātabbo’ti,
iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s why I said what I said.
‘This body is produced by craving. Relying on craving,

segs.p: Taṇhā pahātabbā’ti, iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ.
segs.e: you should give up craving.’ This is what I said,
but why did I say it?
Take a mendicant who hears this:

segs.p: ‘itthannāmo kira bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
They think:

segs.p: ‘kudāssu nāma ahampi āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Oh, when will I too realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …’

segs.p: So aparena samayena taṇhaṁ nissāya taṇhaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: After some time, relying on craving, they give up craving.

segs.p: ‘Taṇhāsambhūto ayaṁ, bhagini, kāyo taṇhaṁ nissāya taṇhā pahātabbā’ti,
iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s why I said what I said.
‘This body is produced by conceit. Relying on conceit,

segs.p: Māno pahātabbo’ti, iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ.
segs.e: you should give up conceit.’ This is what I said,
but why did I say it?
Take a mendicant who hears this:

segs.p: ‘itthannāmo kira bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharatī’ti.
segs.e: ‘They say that the mendicant named so-and-so has realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.’
They think:

segs.p: ‘so hi nāma āyasmā āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati;
segs.e: ‘Well, that venerable can realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom … in this very life …
Why can’t I?’

segs.p: So aparena samayena mānaṁ nissāya mānaṁ pajahati.
segs.e: After some time, relying on conceit, they give up conceit.

segs.p: ‘Mānasambhūto ayaṁ, bhagini, kāyo, mānaṁ nissāya māno pahātabbo’ti,
iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s why I said what I said.
‘This body is produced by sex.
The Buddha spoke of breaking off everything to do with sex.’”

segs.p: Atha kho sā bhikkhunī mañcakā vuṭṭhahitvā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā āyasmato ānandassa pādesu sirasā nipatitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then that nun rose from her cot, placed her robe over one shoulder, bowed with her head to Ānanda’s feet, and said,

segs.p: “accayo maṁ, bhante, accagamā, yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yāhaṁ evamakāsiṁ.
segs.e: “I made a mistake, sir. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of me to act in that way.

segs.p: Tassā me, bhante, ayyo ānando accayaṁ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu, āyatiṁ saṁvarāyā”ti.
segs.e: Please, sir, accept my mistake for what it is, so I can restrain myself in future.”

segs.p: “Taggha taṁ, bhagini, accayo accagamā, yathābālaṁ yathāmūḷhaṁ yathāakusalaṁ, yā tvaṁ evamakāsi.
segs.e: “Indeed, sister, you made a mistake. It was foolish, stupid, and unskillful of you to act in that way.

segs.p: Yato ca kho tvaṁ, bhagini, accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikarosi, taṁ te mayaṁ paṭiggaṇhāma.
segs.e: But since you have recognized your mistake for what it is, and have dealt with it properly, I accept it.

segs.p: Vuddhi hesā, bhagini, ariyassa vinaye yo accayaṁ accayato disvā yathādhammaṁ paṭikaroti āyatiṁ saṁvaraṁ āpajjatī”ti.
segs.e: For it is growth in the training of the Noble One to recognize a mistake for what it is, deal with it properly, and commit to restraint in the future.”
Numbered Discourses 4.160
16. Faculties
The Training of a Holy One

segs.p: “Sugato vā, bhikkhave, loke tiṭṭhamāno sugatavinayo vā tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a Holy One or a Holy One’s training remain in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
And who is a Holy One?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā.
segs.e: It’s when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.
This is a Holy One.
And what is the training of a Holy One?

segs.p: So dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.
This is the training of a Holy One.

segs.p: Evaṁ sugato vā, bhikkhave, loke tiṭṭhamāno sugatavinayo vā tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānanti.
segs.e: This is how a Holy One or a Holy One’s training remain in the world for the welfare and happiness of the people, out of sympathy for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

segs.p: Cattārome, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These four things lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū duggahitaṁ suttantaṁ pariyāpuṇanti dunnikkhittehi padabyañjanehi.
segs.e: Firstly, the mendicants memorize discourses that they learned incorrectly, with misplaced words and phrases.

segs.p: Dunnikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi dunnayo hoti.
segs.e: When the words and phrases are misplaced, the meaning is misinterpreted.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū dubbacā honti dovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā akkhamā appadakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants are hard to admonish, having qualities that make them hard to admonish. They’re impatient, and don’t take instruction respectfully.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te na sakkaccaṁ suttantaṁ paraṁ vācenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—don’t carefully make others recite the discourses.

segs.p: Tesaṁ accayena chinnamūlako suttanto hoti appaṭisaraṇo.
segs.e: When they pass away, the discourses are cut off at the root, with no one to preserve them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, therā bhikkhū bāhulikā honti sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: Furthermore, the senior mendicants are indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
Those who come after them follow their example.

segs.p: Sāpi hoti bāhulikā sāthalikā, okkamane pubbaṅgamā, paviveke nikkhittadhurā, na vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: They too become indulgent and slack, leaders in backsliding, neglecting seclusion, not rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing that leads to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā saddhammassa sammosāya antaradhānāya saṁvattantīti.
segs.e: These are four things that lead to the decline and disappearance of the true teaching.

segs.p: Cattārome, bhikkhave, dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: These four things lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhū suggahitaṁ suttantaṁ pariyāpuṇanti sunikkhittehi padabyañjanehi.
segs.e: Firstly, the mendicants memorize discourses that have been learned correctly, with well placed words and phrases.

segs.p: Sunikkhittassa, bhikkhave, padabyañjanassa atthopi sunayo hoti.
segs.e: When the words and phrases are well placed, the meaning is interpreted correctly.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the first thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhū suvacā honti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgatā khamā padakkhiṇaggāhino anusāsaniṁ.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants are easy to admonish, having qualities that make them easy to admonish. They’re patient, and take instruction respectfully.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the second thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ye te bhikkhū bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā, te sakkaccaṁ suttantaṁ paraṁ vācenti.
segs.e: Furthermore, the mendicants who are very learned—inheritors of the heritage, who have memorized the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines—carefully make others recite the discourses.

segs.p: Tesaṁ accayena nacchinnamūlako suttanto hoti sappaṭisaraṇo.
segs.e: When they pass away, the discourses aren’t cut off at the root, and they have someone to preserve them.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, tatiyo dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the third thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, therā bhikkhū na bāhulikā honti na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā, paviveke pubbaṅgamā, vīriyaṁ ārabhanti appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: Furthermore, the senior mendicants are not indulgent or slack, nor are they backsliders; instead, they take the lead in seclusion, rousing energy for attaining the unattained, achieving the unachieved, and realizing the unrealized.
Those who come after them follow their example.

segs.p: Sāpi hoti na bāhulikā na sāthalikā, okkamane nikkhittadhurā, paviveke pubbaṅgamā, vīriyaṁ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: They too aren’t indulgent or slack …

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, catuttho dhammo saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: This is the fourth thing that leads to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā saddhammassa ṭhitiyā asammosāya anantaradhānāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These are four things that lead to the continuation, persistence, and enduring of the true teaching.”

17. Practice
In Detail
“Mendicants, there are four ways of practice.
What four?
Painful practice with slow insight,
painful practice with swift insight,
pleasant practice with slow insight, and
pleasant practice with swift insight.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā?
segs.e: And what’s the painful practice with slow insight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pakatiyāpi tibbarāgajātiko hoti, abhikkhaṇaṁ rāgajaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
segs.e: It’s when someone is ordinarily full of acute greed, hate, and delusion. They often feel the pain and sadness that greed, hate, and delusion bring.

segs.p: Pakatiyāpi tibbadosajātiko hoti, abhikkhaṇaṁ dosajaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.
Pakatiyāpi tibbamohajātiko hoti, abhikkhaṇaṁ mohajaṁ dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvedeti.

segs.e: These five faculties manifest in them weakly:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ muduttā dandhaṁ ānantariyaṁ pāpuṇāti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: Because of this, they only slowly attain the conditions for ending the defilements in the present life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā.
segs.e: This is called the painful practice with slow insight.

segs.e: And what’s the painful practice with swift insight?

17. Practice
Ugly
“Mendicants, there are four ways of practice.
What four?
Painful practice with slow insight,
painful practice with swift insight,
pleasant practice with slow insight, and
pleasant practice with swift insight.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā?
segs.e: And what’s the painful practice with slow insight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asubhānupassī kāye viharati, āhāre paṭikūlasaññī, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññī, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions,

segs.p: maraṇasaññā kho panassa ajjhattaṁ sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: and has well established the perception of their own death.

segs.p: So imāni pañca sekhabalāni upanissāya viharati—
segs.e: They rely on these five powers of a trainee:
faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
But these five faculties manifest in them weakly:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ muduttā dandhaṁ ānantariyaṁ pāpuṇāti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: Because of this, they only slowly attain the conditions for ending the defilements in the present life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā.
segs.e: This is called the painful practice with slow insight.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, dukkhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā?
segs.e: And what’s the painful practice with swift insight?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asubhānupassī kāye viharati, āhāre paṭikūlasaññī, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññī, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī;

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā.
segs.e: This is called the painful practice with swift insight.

segs.p: Katamā ca, bhikkhave, sukhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā?
segs.e: And what’s the pleasant practice with slow insight?

segs.p: Idha bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṁ savicāraṁ vivekajaṁ pītisukhaṁ paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of seclusion, while placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā ajjhattaṁ sampasādanaṁ cetaso ekodibhāvaṁ avitakkaṁ avicāraṁ samādhijaṁ pītisukhaṁ dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption, which has the rapture and bliss born of immersion, with internal clarity and mind at one, without placing the mind and keeping it connected.

segs.p: pītiyā ca virāgā upekkhako ca viharati sato ca sampajāno sukhañca kāyena paṭisaṁvedeti yaṁ taṁ ariyā ācikkhanti: ‘upekkhako satimā sukhavihārī’ti tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: And with the fading away of rapture, they enter and remain in the third absorption, where they meditate with equanimity, mindful and aware, experiencing for themselves the bliss of which the noble ones declare, ‘Equanimous and mindful, one meditates in bliss.’

segs.p: sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṁ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṁ catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: With the giving up of pleasure and pain and the disappearance of former happiness and sadness, they enter and remain in the fourth absorption, without pleasure or pain, with pure equanimity and mindfulness.

segs.p: So imāni pañca sekhabalāni upanissāya viharati—
segs.e: They rely on these five powers of a trainee:
faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
But these five faculties manifest in them weakly:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ muduttā dandhaṁ ānantariyaṁ pāpuṇāti āsavānaṁ khayāya.

segs.e: It’s when a mendicant … enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

segs.p: So imāni pañca sekhabalāni upanissāya viharati—
segs.e: They rely on these five powers of a trainee:
faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
And these five faculties manifest in them strongly:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ adhimattattā khippaṁ ānantariyaṁ pāpuṇāti āsavānaṁ khayāya.
segs.e: Because of this, they swiftly attain the conditions for ending the defilements in the present life.

segs.p: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā.
segs.e: This is called the pleasant practice with swift insight.
These are the four ways of practice.”

17. Practice
Patient (1st)
“Mendicants, there are four ways of practice.
What four?

segs.p: Akkhamā paṭipadā, khamā paṭipadā, damā paṭipadā, samā paṭipadā.
segs.e: Impatient practice, patient practice, taming practice, and calming practice.
And what’s the impatient practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco akkosantaṁ paccakkosati, rosantaṁ paṭirosati, bhaṇḍantaṁ paṭibhaṇḍati.
segs.e: It’s when someone abuses, annoys, or argues with you, and you abuse, annoy, or argue right back at them.
This is called the impatient practice.
And what’s the patient practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco akkosantaṁ na paccakkosati, rosantaṁ na paṭirosati, bhaṇḍantaṁ na paṭibhaṇḍati.
segs.e: It’s when someone abuses, annoys, or argues with you, and you don’t abuse, annoy, or argue back at them.
This is called the patient practice.
And what’s the taming practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī;
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ cakkhundriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati cakkhundriyaṁ; cakkhundriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of sight were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of sight, and achieving its restraint.
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī;
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati manindriyaṁ; manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.
This is called the taming practice.
And what’s the calming practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti sameti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti; uppannaṁ byāpādavitakkaṁ …pe… uppannaṁ vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ … uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti sameti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, dispel them, calm them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.
This is called the calming practice.
These are the four ways of practice.”
Numbered Discourses 4.165
17. Practice
Patience (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are four ways of practice.
What four?

segs.p: Akkhamā paṭipadā, khamā paṭipadā, damā paṭipadā, samā paṭipadā.
segs.e: Impatient practice, patient practice, taming practice, and calming practice.
And what’s the impatient practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco akkhamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya, ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ duruttānaṁ durāgatānaṁ vacanapathānaṁ uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ anadhivāsakajātiko hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone cannot endure cold, heat, hunger, and thirst. They cannot endure the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles. They cannot endure rude and unwelcome criticism. And they cannot put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.
This is called the impatient practice.
And what’s the patient practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco khamo hoti sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya, ḍaṁsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṁ duruttānaṁ durāgatānaṁ vacanapathānaṁ uppannānaṁ sārīrikānaṁ vedanānaṁ dukkhānaṁ tibbānaṁ kharānaṁ kaṭukānaṁ asātānaṁ amanāpānaṁ pāṇaharānaṁ adhivāsakajātiko hoti.
segs.e: It’s when someone endures cold, heat, hunger, and thirst. They endure the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles. They endure rude and unwelcome criticism. And they put up with physical pain—sharp, severe, acute, unpleasant, disagreeable, and life-threatening.
This is called the patient practice.
And what’s the taming practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā na nimittaggāhī hoti …pe…
segs.e: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, they don’t get caught up in the features and details. …
When they hear a sound with their ears …
When they smell an odor with their nose …
When they taste a flavor with their tongue …
When they feel a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya na nimittaggāhī hoti nānubyañjanaggāhī;
segs.e: When they know an idea with their mind, they don’t get caught up in the features and details.

segs.p: yatvādhikaraṇamenaṁ manindriyaṁ asaṁvutaṁ viharantaṁ abhijjhādomanassā pāpakā akusalā dhammā anvāssaveyyuṁ, tassa saṁvarāya paṭipajjati; rakkhati manindriyaṁ; manindriye saṁvaraṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: If the faculty of mind were left unrestrained, bad unskillful qualities of covetousness and displeasure would become overwhelming. For this reason, they practice restraint, protecting the faculty of mind, and achieving its restraint.
This is called the taming practice.
And what’s the calming practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu uppannaṁ kāmavitakkaṁ nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti sameti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti, uppannaṁ byāpādavitakkaṁ …pe… uppannaṁ vihiṁsāvitakkaṁ … uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti sameti byantīkaroti anabhāvaṁ gameti.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t tolerate a sensual, malicious, or cruel thought. They don’t tolerate any bad, unskillful qualities that have arisen, but give them up, dispel them, calm them, eliminate them, and obliterate them.
This is called the calming practice.
These are the four ways of practice.”
Numbered Discourses 4.166
17. Practice
Both
“Mendicants, there are four ways of practice.
What four?
Painful practice with slow insight,
painful practice with swift insight,
pleasant practice with slow insight, and
pleasant practice with swift insight.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā dukkhā dandhābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva hīnā akkhāyati. Yampāyaṁ paṭipadā dukkhā, imināpāyaṁ hīnā akkhāyati; yampāyaṁ paṭipadā dandhā, imināpāyaṁ hīnā akkhāyati.
segs.e: Of these, the painful practice with slow insight is said to be inferior in both ways: because it’s painful and because it’s slow.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva hīnā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This practice is said to be inferior in both ways.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā dukkhā khippābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā dukkhattā hīnā akkhāyati.
segs.e: The painful practice with swift insight is said to be inferior because it’s painful.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā sukhā dandhābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā dandhattā hīnā akkhāyati.
segs.e: The pleasant practice with slow insight is said to be inferior because it’s slow.

segs.p: Tatra, bhikkhave, yāyaṁ paṭipadā sukhā khippābhiññā, ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva paṇītā akkhāyati. Yampāyaṁ paṭipadā sukhā, imināpāyaṁ paṇītā akkhāyati; yampāyaṁ paṭipadā khippā, imināpāyaṁ paṇītā akkhāyati.
segs.e: The pleasant practice with swift insight is said to be superior in both ways: because it’s pleasant, and because it’s swift.

segs.p: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭipadā ubhayeneva paṇītā akkhāyati.
segs.e: This practice is said to be superior in both ways.
These are the four ways of practice.”
Numbered Discourses 4.167
17. Practice
Moggallāna’s Practice

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahāmoggallānena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta went up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Sāriputta sat down to one side and said to Mahāmoggallāna:
“Reverend Moggallāna, there are four ways of practice.
What four?
Painful practice with slow insight,
painful practice with swift insight,
pleasant practice with slow insight, and
pleasant practice with swift insight.
These are the four ways of practice.

segs.p: Imāsaṁ, āvuso, catunnaṁ paṭipadānaṁ katamaṁ te paṭipadaṁ āgamma anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuttan”ti?
segs.e: Which one of these four ways of practice did you rely on to free your mind from defilements by not grasping?”
“Reverend Sāriputta …

segs.p: Dukkhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā, dukkhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā, sukhā paṭipadā dandhābhiññā, sukhā paṭipadā khippābhiññā.
Imāsaṁ, āvuso, catunnaṁ paṭipadānaṁ yāyaṁ paṭipadā dukkhā khippābhiññā, imaṁ me paṭipadaṁ āgamma anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuttan”ti.
segs.e: I relied on the painful practice with swift insight to free my mind from defilements by not grasping.”
Numbered Discourses 4.168

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahāmoggallāna went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.e: Which one of these four ways of practice did you rely on to free your mind from defilements by not grasping?”
“Reverend Moggallāna …

Numbered Discourses 4.169
17. Practice
Extra Effort
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo diṭṭheva dhamme sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: One individual is fully extinguished in this very life by making extra effort.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo kāyassa bhedā sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: One individual is fully extinguished when the body breaks up by making extra effort.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo diṭṭheva dhamme asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: One individual is fully extinguished in this very life without making extra effort.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo kāyassa bhedā asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: One individual is fully extinguished when the body breaks up without making extra effort.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo diṭṭheva dhamme sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti?
segs.e: And how is an individual fully extinguished in this very life by making extra effort?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asubhānupassī kāye viharati, āhāre paṭikūlasaññī, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññī, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions,

segs.p: Maraṇasaññā kho panassa ajjhattaṁ sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: and has well established the perception of their own death.

segs.p: So imāni pañca sekhabalāni upanissāya viharati—
segs.e: They rely on these five powers of a trainee:
faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
And these five faculties manifest in them strongly:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ adhimattattā diṭṭheva dhamme sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: Because of the strength of the five faculties, they are fully extinguished in this very life by making extra effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo diṭṭheva dhamme sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is fully extinguished in this very life by making extra effort.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo kāyassa bhedā sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti?
segs.e: How is an individual fully extinguished when the body breaks up by making extra effort?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asubhānupassī kāye viharati, āhāre paṭikūlasaññī, sabbaloke anabhiratisaññī, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant meditates observing the ugliness of the body, perceives the repulsiveness of food, perceives dissatisfaction with the whole world, observes the impermanence of all conditions,

segs.p: Maraṇasaññā kho panassa ajjhattaṁ sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: and has well established the perception of their own death.

segs.p: So imāni pañca sekhabalāni upanissāya viharati—
segs.e: They rely on these five powers of a trainee:
faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
But these five faculties manifest in them weakly:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ muduttā kāyassa bhedā sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: Because of the weakness of the five faculties, they are fully extinguished when the body breaks up by making extra effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo kāyassa bhedā sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is fully extinguished when the body breaks up by making extra effort.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo diṭṭheva dhamme asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti?
segs.e: And how is an individual fully extinguished in this very life without making extra effort?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant … enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

segs.p: So imāni pañca sekhabalāni upanissāya viharati—
segs.e: They rely on these five powers of a trainee:
faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
And these five faculties manifest in them strongly:
faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ adhimattattā diṭṭheva dhamme asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: Because of the strength of the five faculties, they are fully extinguished in this very life without making extra effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo diṭṭheva dhamme asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is fully extinguished in this very life without making extra effort.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, puggalo kāyassa bhedā asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti?
segs.e: And how is an individual fully extinguished when the body breaks up without making extra effort?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant … enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

segs.p: So imāni pañca sekhabalāni upanissāya viharati—
segs.e: They rely on these five powers of a trainee:
faith, conscience, prudence, energy, and wisdom.
But these five faculties manifest in them weakly: faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: So imesaṁ pañcannaṁ indriyānaṁ muduttā kāyassa bhedā asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: Because of the weakness of the five faculties, they are fully extinguished when the body breaks up without making extra effort.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo kāyassa bhedā asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is fully extinguished when the body breaks up without making extra effort.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
