17. Practice
In Conjunction
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā ānando bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Ānanda addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Ānanda said this:

segs.p: “Yo hi koci, āvuso, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā mama santike arahattappattiṁ byākaroti, sabbo so catūhi maggehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: “Reverends, all of the monks and nuns who declare in my presence that they have attained perfection, did so by one or other of four paths.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, āvuso, bhikkhu samathapubbaṅgamaṁ vipassanaṁ bhāveti.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who develops serenity before discernment.

segs.p: Tassa samathapubbaṅgamaṁ vipassanaṁ bhāvayato maggo sañjāyati.
segs.e: As they do so, the path is born in them.

segs.p: So taṁ maggaṁ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti.
segs.e: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ maggaṁ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saṁyojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.
segs.e: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṁ samathaṁ bhāveti.
segs.e: Another mendicant develops discernment before serenity.

segs.p: Tassa vipassanāpubbaṅgamaṁ samathaṁ bhāvayato maggo sañjāyati.
segs.e: As they do so, the path is born in them.

segs.p: So taṁ maggaṁ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti.
segs.e: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ maggaṁ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saṁyojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.
segs.e: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu samathavipassanaṁ yuganaddhaṁ bhāveti.
segs.e: Another mendicant develops serenity and discernment in conjunction.

segs.p: Tassa samathavipassanaṁ yuganaddhaṁ bhāvayato maggo sañjāyati.
segs.e: As they do so, the path is born in them.

segs.p: So taṁ maggaṁ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti.
segs.e: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ maggaṁ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saṁyojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.
segs.e: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhuno dhammuddhaccaviggahitaṁ mānasaṁ hoti.
segs.e: Another mendicant’s heart is seized by restlessness to realize the teaching.

segs.p: Hoti so, āvuso, samayo yaṁ taṁ cittaṁ ajjhattameva santiṭṭhati sannisīdati ekodi hoti samādhiyati.
segs.e: But there comes a time when their mind is stilled internally; it settles, unifies, and becomes immersed in samādhi.
The path is born in them.

segs.p: So taṁ maggaṁ āsevati bhāveti bahulīkaroti.
segs.e: They cultivate, develop, and make much of it.

segs.p: Tassa taṁ maggaṁ āsevato bhāvayato bahulīkaroto saṁyojanāni pahīyanti, anusayā byantīhonti.
segs.e: By doing so, they give up the fetters and eliminate the underlying tendencies.

segs.p: Yo hi koci, āvuso, bhikkhu vā bhikkhunī vā mama santike arahattappattiṁ byākaroti, sabbo so imehi catūhi maggehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarenā”ti.
segs.e: All of the monks and nuns who declare in my presence that they have attained perfection, did so by one or other of these four paths.”
Numbered Discourses 4.171
18. Intention
Intention

segs.p: “Kāye vā, bhikkhave, sati kāyasañcetanāhetu uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, as long as there’s a body, the intention that gives rise to bodily action causes pleasure and pain to arise in oneself.

segs.p: Vācāya vā, bhikkhave, sati vacīsañcetanāhetu uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: As long as there’s a voice, the intention that gives rise to verbal action causes pleasure and pain to arise in oneself.

segs.p: Mane vā, bhikkhave, sati manosañcetanāhetu uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ avijjāpaccayāva.
segs.e: As long as there’s a mind, the intention that gives rise to mental action causes pleasure and pain to arise in oneself. But this is only when dependent on ignorance.

segs.p: Sāmaṁ vā taṁ, bhikkhave, kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: By oneself one instigates the choice that gives rise to bodily, verbal, and mental action, conditioned by which that pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

segs.p: Pare vāssa taṁ, bhikkhave, kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharonti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: Or else others instigate the choice …

segs.p: Sampajāno vā taṁ, bhikkhave, kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: One instigates the choice after deliberation …

segs.p: Asampajāno vā taṁ, bhikkhave, kāyasaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
segs.e: Or else one instigates the choice without deliberation …

segs.p: Sāmaṁ vā taṁ, bhikkhave, vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ;
pare vāssa taṁ, bhikkhave, vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharonti;
sampajāno vā taṁ, bhikkhave, vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ;
asampajāno vā taṁ, bhikkhave, vacīsaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.
Sāmaṁ vā taṁ, bhikkhave, manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ;
pare vāssa taṁ, bhikkhave, manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharonti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ;
sampajāno vā taṁ, bhikkhave, manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ;
asampajāno vā taṁ, bhikkhave, manosaṅkhāraṁ abhisaṅkharoti, yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ.

segs.e: Ignorance is included in all these things.

segs.p: avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā so kāyo na hoti yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ, sā vācā na hoti yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ, so mano na hoti yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhaṁ,
segs.e: But when ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, that body, that voice, and that mind no longer exist dependent on which that pleasure and pain arise in oneself.

segs.p: khettaṁ taṁ na hoti …pe… vatthu taṁ na hoti …pe… āyatanaṁ taṁ na hoti …pe… adhikaraṇaṁ taṁ na hoti yaṁpaccayāssa taṁ uppajjati ajjhattaṁ sukhadukkhanti.
segs.e: That field does not exist, that ground does not exist, that dimension does not exist, that foundation does not exist, dependent on which that pleasure and pain arise in oneself.”
“Mendicants, there are four kinds of incarnation.
What four?

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe attasañcetanā kamati, no parasañcetanā.
segs.e: There is incarnation where one’s own intention is effective, not that of others.

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe parasañcetanā kamati, no attasañcetanā.
segs.e: There is incarnation where the intention of others is effective, not one’s own.

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe attasañcetanā ca kamati parasañcetanā ca.
segs.e: There is incarnation where both one’s own and others’ intentions are effective.

segs.p: Atthi, bhikkhave, attabhāvapaṭilābho, yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe nevattasañcetanā kamati, no parasañcetanā.
segs.e: There is incarnation where neither one’s own nor others’ intentions are effective.
These are the four kinds of incarnation.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Venerable Sāriputta said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “imassa kho ahaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmi:
segs.e: “Sir, this is how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.

segs.p: ‘tatra, bhante, yāyaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābho yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe attasañcetanā kamati no parasañcetanā, attasañcetanāhetu tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhā kāyā cuti hoti.
segs.e: Take the case of the incarnation where one’s own intention is effective, not that of others. Those sentient beings pass away from that realm due to their own intention.

segs.p: Tatra, bhante, yāyaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābho yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe parasañcetanā kamati no attasañcetanā, parasañcetanāhetu tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhā kāyā cuti hoti.
segs.e: Take the case of the incarnation where the intention of others is effective, not one’s own. Those sentient beings pass away from that realm due to the intention of others.

segs.p: Tatra, bhante, yāyaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābho yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe attasañcetanā ca kamati parasañcetanā ca, attasañcetanā ca parasañcetanā ca hetu tesaṁ sattānaṁ tamhā kāyā cuti hoti.
segs.e: Take the case of the incarnation where both one’s own and others’ intentions are effective. Those sentient beings pass away from that realm due to both their own and others’ intentions.

segs.p: Tatra, bhante, yāyaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābho yasmiṁ attabhāvapaṭilābhe neva attasañcetanā kamati no parasañcetanā, katame tena devā daṭṭhabbā’”ti?
segs.e: But sir, in the case of the incarnation where neither one’s own nor others’ intentions are effective, what kind of gods does this refer to?”
“Sāriputta, it refers to the gods reborn in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.”

segs.p: “Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā tamhā kāyā cutā āgāmino honti āgantāro itthattaṁ?
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why some sentient beings pass away from that realm as returners who come back to this place,

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā tamhā kāyā cutā anāgāmino honti anāgantāro itthattan”ti?
segs.e: while others are non-returners who don’t come back?”

segs.p: “Idha, sāriputta, ekaccassa puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni appahīnāni honti, so diṭṭheva dhamme nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: “Sāriputta, take an individual who hasn’t given up the lower fetters. In this very life they enter and abide in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati;
segs.e: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno kālaṁ kurumāno nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: So tato cuto āgāmī hoti āgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: When they pass away from there, they’re a returner, who comes back to this place.

segs.p: Idha pana, sāriputta, ekaccassa puggalassa orambhāgiyāni saṁyojanāni pahīnāni honti, so diṭṭheva dhamme nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Sāriputta, take an individual who has given up the lower fetters. In this very life they enter and abide in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: So tadassādeti, taṁ nikāmeti, tena ca vittiṁ āpajjati;
segs.e: They enjoy it and like it and find it rewarding.

segs.p: tattha ṭhito tadadhimutto tabbahulavihārī aparihīno kālaṁ kurumāno nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: If they abide in that, are committed to it, and meditate on it often without losing it, when they die they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: So tato cuto anāgāmī hoti anāgantā itthattaṁ.
segs.e: When they pass away from there, they’re a non-returner, not coming back to this place.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā tamhā kāyā cutā āgāmino honti āgantāro itthattaṁ.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why some sentient beings pass away from that realm as returners who come back to this place,

segs.p: Ayaṁ pana, sāriputta, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā tamhā kāyā cutā anāgāmino honti anāgantāro itthattan”ti.
segs.e: while others are non-returners who don’t come back.”
Numbered Discourses 4.172
18. Intention
Sāriputta’s Attainment of Textual Analysis

segs.p: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, mendicants!”

segs.p: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Reverend,” they replied.
Sāriputta said this:

segs.p: “Addhamāsūpasampannena me, āvuso, atthapaṭisambhidā sacchikatā odhiso byañjanaso.
segs.e: “Reverends, I realized the textual analysis of the meaning—piece by piece and expression by expression—a fortnight after I ordained.

segs.p: Tamahaṁ anekapariyāyena ācikkhāmi desemi paññāpemi paṭṭhapemi vivarāmi vibhajāmi uttānīkaromi.
segs.e: In many ways I explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, and reveal it.

segs.p: Yassa kho panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā, so maṁ pañhena.
segs.e: Whoever has any doubt or uncertainty, let them ask me,

segs.p: Ahaṁ veyyākaraṇena sammukhībhūto no satthā yo no dhammānaṁ sukusalo.
segs.e: I will answer. Our teacher is present, he who is so very skilled in our teachings.

segs.p: Addhamāsūpasampannena me, āvuso, dhammapaṭisambhidā sacchikatā odhiso byañjanaso.
segs.e: I realized the textual analysis of the text—piece by piece and expression by expression—a fortnight after I ordained. …

segs.p: Tamahaṁ anekapariyāyena ācikkhāmi desemi paññāpemi paṭṭhapemi vivarāmi vibhajāmi uttānīkaromi.
Yassa kho panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā, so maṁ pañhena.
Ahaṁ veyyākaraṇena sammukhībhūto no satthā yo no dhammānaṁ sukusalo.
Addhamāsūpasampannena me, āvuso, niruttipaṭisambhidā sacchikatā odhiso byañjanaso.
segs.e: I realized the textual analysis of definition—piece by piece and expression by expression—a fortnight after I ordained. …

segs.p: Tamahaṁ anekapariyāyena ācikkhāmi desemi paññāpemi paṭṭhapemi vivarāmi vibhajāmi uttānīkaromi.
Yassa kho panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā, so maṁ pañhena.
Ahaṁ veyyākaraṇena sammukhībhūto no satthā yo no dhammānaṁ sukusalo.
Addhamāsūpasampannena me, āvuso, paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā sacchikatā odhiso byañjanaso.
segs.e: I realized the textual analysis of eloquence—piece by piece and expression by expression—a fortnight after I ordained.

segs.p: Tamahaṁ anekapariyāyena ācikkhāmi desemi paññāpemi paṭṭhapemi vivarāmi vibhajāmi uttānīkaromi.
segs.e: In many ways I explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, and reveal it.

segs.p: Yassa kho panassa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā, so maṁ pañhena.
segs.e: If anyone has any doubt or uncertainty, let them ask me,

segs.p: Ahaṁ veyyākaraṇena sammukhībhūto no satthā yo no dhammānaṁ sukusalo”ti.
segs.e: I will answer. Our teacher is present, he who is so very skilled in our teachings.”
Numbered Discourses 4.173
18. Intention
With Mahākoṭṭhita

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Mahākoṭṭhita went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mahākoṭṭhiko āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Mahākoṭṭhita sat down to one side, and said to Sāriputta:
“Reverend, when the six fields of contact have faded away and ceased with no residue left behind, does something else still exist?”
“Don’t put it like that, reverend.”
“Does something else no longer exist?”
“Don’t put it like that, reverend.”

segs.p: “Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthi ca natthi ca aññaṁ kiñcī”ti?
segs.e: “Does something else both still exist and no longer exist?”
“Don’t put it like that, reverend.”

segs.p: “Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā nevatthi no natthaññaṁ kiñcī”ti?
segs.e: “Does something else neither still exist nor no longer exist?”
“Don’t put it like that, reverend.”

segs.p: “‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno ‘mā hevaṁ, āvuso’ti vadesi.
segs.e: “Reverend, when asked whether—when the six fields of contact have faded away and ceased with no residue left behind—something else still exists, you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

segs.p: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
segs.e: When asked whether something else no longer exists,
you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

segs.p: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthi ca natthi ca aññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
segs.e: When asked whether something else both still exists and no longer exists,
you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

segs.p: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā nevatthi no natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
segs.e: When asked whether something else neither still exists nor no longer exists,
you say ‘don’t put it like that’.

segs.p: Yathā kathaṁ pana, āvuso, imassa bhāsitassa attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?
segs.e: How then should we see the meaning of this statement?”

segs.p: “‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
segs.e: “In saying that, ‘When the six fields of contact have faded away and ceased with no residue left behind, something else still exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

segs.p: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
segs.e: In saying that, ‘something else no longer exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

segs.p: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā atthi ca natthi ca aññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
segs.e: In saying that, ‘something else both still exists and no longer exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

segs.p: ‘Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā nevatthi no natthaññaṁ kiñcī’ti, iti vadaṁ appapañcaṁ papañceti.
segs.e: In saying that, ‘something else neither still exists nor no longer exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

segs.p: Yāvatā, āvuso, channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ gati tāvatā papañcassa gati;
segs.e: The scope of proliferation extends as far as the scope of the six fields of contact.

segs.p: yāvatā papañcassa gati tāvatā channaṁ phassāyatanānaṁ gati.
segs.e: The scope of the six fields of contact extends as far as the scope of proliferation.

segs.p: Channaṁ, āvuso, phassāyatanānaṁ asesavirāganirodhā papañcanirodho papañcavūpasamo”ti.
segs.e: When the six fields of contact fade away and cease with no residue left behind, proliferation stops and is stilled.”
Numbered Discourses 4.174
18. Intention
With Ānanda

segs.e: In saying that, ‘something else no longer exists’, you’re proliferating the unproliferated.

Numbered Discourses 4.175
18. Intention
With Upavāṇa

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā upavāṇo yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Upavāṇa went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā upavāṇo āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Upavāṇa sat down to one side, and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, vijjāyantakaro hotī”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, do you become a terminator because of knowledge?”
“That’s not it, reverend.”
“Do you become a terminator because of conduct?”
“That’s not it, reverend.”
“Do you become a terminator because of both knowledge and conduct?”
“That’s not it, reverend.”
“Do you become a terminator for some reason other than knowledge and conduct?”
“That’s not it, reverend.”

segs.p: “‘Kiṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, vijjāyantakaro hotī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
segs.e: “Reverend Sāriputta, when asked whether you become a terminator because of knowledge or conduct or knowledge and conduct, or for some other reason,
you say ‘that’s not it’.

segs.p: ‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, caraṇenantakaro hotī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, vijjācaraṇenantakaro hotī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:
‘Kiṁ panāvuso sāriputta, aññatra vijjācaraṇenantakaro hotī’ti, iti puṭṭho samāno:

segs.e: How then do you become a terminator?”

segs.p: “Vijjāya ce, āvuso, antakaro abhavissa, saupādānova samāno antakaro abhavissa.
segs.e: “Reverend, if you became a terminator because of knowledge, then even someone who still grasps fuel could be a terminator.

segs.p: Caraṇena ce, āvuso, antakaro abhavissa, saupādānova samāno antakaro abhavissa.
segs.e: If you became a terminator because of conduct, then even someone who still grasps fuel could be a terminator.

segs.p: Vijjācaraṇena ce, āvuso, antakaro abhavissa, saupādānova samāno antakaro abhavissa.
segs.e: If you became a terminator because of both knowledge and conduct, then even someone who still grasps fuel could be a terminator.

segs.p: Aññatra vijjācaraṇena ce, āvuso, antakaro abhavissa, puthujjano antakaro abhavissa.
segs.e: If you became a terminator for some reason other than knowledge and conduct, then even an ordinary person could be a terminator.
For an ordinary person lacks knowledge and conduct.

segs.p: Caraṇavipanno kho, āvuso, yathābhūtaṁ na jānāti na passati.
segs.e: Reverend, someone lacking good conduct does not know and see things as they are.
Someone accomplished in good conduct knows and sees things as they are.
Knowing and seeing things as they are, one is a terminator.”
Numbered Discourses 4.176
18. Intention
Aspiration

segs.p: “Saddho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ sammā āyācamāno āyāceyya:
segs.e: “Mendicants, a faithful monk would rightly aspire:
‘May I be like Sāriputta and Moggallāna!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvakānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ, yadidaṁ sāriputtamoggallānā.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my monk disciples, that is, Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

segs.p: Saddhā, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī evaṁ sammā āyācamānā āyāceyya:
segs.e: A faithful nun would rightly aspire:

segs.p: ‘tādisā homi yādisā khemā ca bhikkhunī uppalavaṇṇā cā’ti.
segs.e: ‘May I be like the nuns Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvikānaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ, yadidaṁ khemā ca bhikkhunī uppalavaṇṇā ca.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my nun disciples, that is, the nuns Khemā and Uppalavaṇṇā.

segs.p: Saddho, bhikkhave, upāsako evaṁ sammā āyācamāno āyāceyya:
segs.e: A faithful layman would rightly aspire:

segs.p: ‘tādiso homi yādiso citto ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako’ti.
segs.e: ‘May I be like the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvakānaṁ upāsakānaṁ, yadidaṁ citto ca gahapati hatthako ca āḷavako.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my male lay disciples, that is, the householder Citta and Hatthaka of Āḷavī.

segs.p: Saddhā, bhikkhave, upāsikā evaṁ sammā āyācamānā āyāceyya:
segs.e: A faithful laywoman would rightly aspire:

segs.p: ‘tādisā homi yādisā khujjuttarā ca upāsikā veḷukaṇḍakiyā ca nandamātā’ti.
segs.e: ‘May I be like the laywomen Khujjuttarā and Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother!’

segs.p: Esā, bhikkhave, tulā etaṁ pamāṇaṁ mama sāvikānaṁ upāsikānaṁ, yadidaṁ khujjuttarā ca upāsikā veḷukaṇḍakiyā ca nandamātā”ti.
segs.e: These are a standard and a measure for my female lay disciples, that is, the laywomen Khujjuttarā and Veḷukaṇṭakī, Nanda’s mother.”
Numbered Discourses 4.177
18. Intention
With Rāhula

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā rāhulo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ rāhulaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Rāhula went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Yā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā pathavīdhātu yā ca bāhirā pathavīdhātu, pathavīdhāturevesā.
segs.e: “Rāhula, the interior earth element and the exterior earth element are just the earth element.

segs.p: ‘Taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā pathavīdhātuyā nibbindati, pathavīdhātuyā cittaṁ virājeti.
segs.e: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the earth element, detaching the mind from the earth element.

segs.p: Yā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā āpodhātu yā ca bāhirā āpodhātu, āpodhāturevesā.
segs.e: The interior water element and the exterior water element are just the water element.

segs.p: ‘Taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā āpodhātuyā nibbindati, āpodhātuyā cittaṁ virājeti.
segs.e: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the water element, detaching the mind from the water element.

segs.p: Yā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā tejodhātu yā ca bāhirā tejodhātu, tejodhāturevesā.
segs.e: The interior fire element and the exterior fire element are just the fire element.

segs.p: ‘Taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā tejodhātuyā nibbindati, tejodhātuyā cittaṁ virājeti.
segs.e: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the fire element, detaching the mind from the fire element.

segs.p: Yā ca, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu yā ca bāhirā vāyodhātu, vāyodhāturevesā.
segs.e: The interior air element and the exterior air element are just the air element.

segs.p: ‘Taṁ netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti, evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya daṭṭhabbaṁ.
segs.e: This should be truly seen with right understanding like this: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya disvā vāyodhātuyā nibbindati, vāyodhātuyā cittaṁ virājeti.
segs.e: When you truly see with right understanding, you grow disillusioned with the air element, detaching the mind from the air element.

segs.p: Yato kho, rāhula, bhikkhu imāsu catūsu dhātūsu nevattānaṁ na attaniyaṁ samanupassati, ayaṁ vuccati, rāhula, bhikkhu acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant sees these four elements as neither self nor belonging to self, they’re called a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”
Numbered Discourses 4.178
18. Intention
Billabong
“Mendicants, these four individuals are found in the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who enters and remains in a peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on the cessation of substantial reality,

segs.p: Tassa sakkāyanirodhaṁ manasi karoto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati nādhimuccati.
segs.e: but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno na sakkāyanirodho pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You wouldn’t expect that mendicant to realize the cessation of substantial reality.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso lepagatena hatthena sākhaṁ gaṇheyya, tassa so hattho sajjeyyapi gaṇheyyapi bajjheyyapi;
segs.e: Suppose a person were to grab a branch with a glue-smeared hand. Their hand would stick, hold, and bind to it.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who enters and remains in a peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on the cessation of substantial reality,

segs.p: Tassa sakkāyanirodhaṁ manasi karoto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati nādhimuccati.
segs.e: but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno na sakkāyanirodho pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You wouldn’t expect that mendicant to realize the cessation of substantial reality.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Next, take a mendicant who enters and remains in a peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on the cessation of substantial reality,

segs.p: Tassa sakkāyanirodhaṁ manasi karoto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati.
segs.e: and on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sakkāyanirodho pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You would expect that mendicant to realize the cessation of substantial reality.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso suddhena hatthena sākhaṁ gaṇheyya, tassa so hattho neva sajjeyya na gaṇheyya na bajjheyya;
segs.e: Suppose a person were to grab a branch with a clean hand. Their hand wouldn’t stick, hold, or bind to it.

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who enters and remains in a peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on the cessation of substantial reality,

segs.p: Tassa sakkāyanirodhaṁ manasi karoto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati.
segs.e: and on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sakkāyanirodho pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You would expect that mendicant to realize the cessation of substantial reality.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Next, take a mendicant who enters and remains in a peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on smashing ignorance,

segs.p: Tassa avijjāppabhedaṁ manasi karoto avijjāppabhede cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati nādhimuccati.
segs.e: but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno na avijjāppabhedo pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You wouldn’t expect that mendicant to smash ignorance.
Suppose there was a billabong that had been stagnant for many years.

segs.p: Tassā puriso yāni ceva āyamukhāni tāni pidaheyya, yāni ca apāyamukhāni tāni vivareyya, devo ca na sammā dhāraṁ anuppaveccheyya.
segs.e: And someone was to close off the inlets and open up the drains, and the heavens didn’t provide enough rain.

segs.p: Evañhi tassā, bhikkhave, jambāliyā na āḷippabhedo pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You wouldn’t expect that billabong to break its banks.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who enters and remains in a certain peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on smashing ignorance,

segs.p: Tassa avijjāppabhedaṁ manasi karoto avijjāppabhede cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati nādhimuccati.
segs.e: but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno na avijjāppabhedo pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You wouldn’t expect that mendicant to smash ignorance.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Next, take a mendicant who enters and remains in a peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on smashing ignorance,

segs.p: Tassa avijjāppabhedaṁ manasi karoto avijjāppabhede cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati.
segs.e: and on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno avijjāppabhedo pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You would expect that mendicant to smash ignorance.
Suppose there was a billabong that had been stagnant for many years.

segs.p: Tassā puriso yāni ceva āyamukhāni tāni vivareyya, yāni ca apāyamukhāni tāni pidaheyya, devo ca sammā dhāraṁ anuppaveccheyya.
segs.e: And someone was to open up the inlets and close off the drains, and the heavens provided plenty of rain.

segs.p: Evañhi tassā, bhikkhave, jambāliyā āḷippabhedo pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You would expect that billabong to break its banks.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who enters and remains in a certain peaceful release of the heart.
They focus on smashing ignorance,

segs.p: Tassa avijjāppabhedaṁ manasi karoto avijjāppabhede cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati adhimuccati.
segs.e: and on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

segs.p: Tassa kho evaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno avijjāppabhedo pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: You would expect that mendicant to smash ignorance.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puggalā santo saṁvijjamānā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals found in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.179
18. Intention
Extinguishment

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to Venerable Sāriputta, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, Ānanda sat down to one side, and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, hetu ko paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme na parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, Reverend Sāriputta, what is the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life?”

segs.p: “Idhāvuso ānanda, sattā imā hānabhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, imā ṭhitibhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, imā visesabhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti, imā nibbedhabhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānanti.
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, it’s because some sentient beings don’t really understand which perceptions make things worse, which keep things steady, which lead to distinction, and which lead to penetration.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso ānanda, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme na parinibbāyantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are not fully extinguished in this very life.”

segs.p: “Ko panāvuso sāriputta, hetu ko paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti?
segs.e: “What is the cause, Reverend Sāriputta, what is the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life?”

segs.p: “Idhāvuso ānanda, sattā imā hānabhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, imā ṭhitibhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, imā visesabhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti, imā nibbedhabhāgiyā saññāti yathābhūtaṁ pajānanti.
segs.e: “Reverend Ānanda, it’s because some sentient beings truly understand which perceptions make things worse, which keep things steady, which lead to distinction, and which lead to penetration.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, āvuso ānanda, hetu ayaṁ paccayo, yena m’idhekacce sattā diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyantī”ti.
segs.e: That’s the cause, that’s the reason why some sentient beings are fully extinguished in this very life.”
Numbered Discourses 4.180
18. Intention
The Four Great References

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bhoganagare viharati ānandacetiye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near the Bhoga City, at the Ānanda Shrine.
There the Buddha addressed the mendicants,
“Mendicants!”
“Venerable sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, I will teach you the four great references.

segs.p: taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“Mendicants, what are the four great references?
Take a mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
segs.e: ‘Reverend, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ayaṁ dhammo, ayaṁ vinayo, idaṁ satthusāsanan’ti.
segs.e: this is the teaching, this is the training, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

segs.p: Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṁ neva abhinanditabbaṁ nappaṭikkositabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should neither approve nor reject that mendicant’s statement.

segs.p: Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṁ uggahetvā sutte otāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni.
segs.e: Instead, having carefully memorized those words and phrases, you should make sure they fit in the discourse and are exhibited in the training.

segs.p: Tāni ce sutte otāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte otaranti na vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: If they do not fit in the discourse and are not exhibited in the training, you should draw the conclusion:

segs.p: ‘addhā idaṁ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassa;
segs.e: ‘Clearly this is not the word of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.
It has been incorrectly memorized by that mendicant.’
And so you should discard it.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
segs.e: ‘Reverend, I have heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ayaṁ dhammo, ayaṁ vinayo, idaṁ satthusāsanan’ti.
segs.e: this is the teaching, this is the training, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

segs.p: Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṁ neva abhinanditabbaṁ nappaṭikkositabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should neither approve nor reject that mendicant’s statement.

segs.p: Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṁ uggahetvā sutte otāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni.
segs.e: Instead, having carefully memorized those words and phrases, you should make sure they fit in the discourse and are exhibited in the training.

segs.p: Tāni ce sutte otāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva otaranti vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: If they fit in the discourse and are exhibited in the training, you should draw the conclusion:

segs.p: ‘addhā idaṁ tassa bhagavato vacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassa;
segs.e: ‘Clearly this is the word of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.
It has been correctly memorized by that mendicant.’
You should remember it. This is the first great reference.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘asukasmiṁ nāma āvāse saṅgho viharati sathero sapāmokkho.
segs.e: ‘In such-and-such monastery lives a Saṅgha with seniors and leaders.

segs.p: Tassa me saṅghassa sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
segs.e: I’ve heard and learned this in the presence of that Saṅgha:

segs.p: ayaṁ dhammo, ayaṁ vinayo, idaṁ satthusāsanan’ti.
segs.e: this is the teaching, this is the training, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

segs.p: Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṁ neva abhinanditabbaṁ nappaṭikkositabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should neither approve nor reject that mendicant’s statement.

segs.p: Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṁ uggahetvā sutte otāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni.
segs.e: Instead, having carefully memorized those words and phrases, you should make sure they fit in the discourse and are exhibited in the training.

segs.p: Tāni ce sutte otāriyamānāni vinaye sandassiyamānāni na ceva sutte otaranti na vinaye sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: If they do not fit in the discourse and are not exhibited in the training, you should draw the conclusion:

segs.p: ‘addhā idaṁ na ceva tassa bhagavato vacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassa;
segs.e: ‘Clearly this is not the word of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.
It has been incorrectly memorized by that Saṅgha.’
And so you should discard it.

segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘asukasmiṁ nāma āvāse saṅgho viharati sathero sapāmokkho.
segs.e: ‘In such-and-such monastery lives a Saṅgha with seniors and leaders.

segs.p: Tassa me saṅghassa sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
segs.e: I’ve heard and learned this in the presence of that Saṅgha:

segs.p: ayaṁ dhammo, ayaṁ vinayo, idaṁ satthusāsanan’ti.
segs.e: this is the teaching, this is the training, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

segs.p: Tassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhāsitaṁ neva abhinanditabbaṁ nappaṭikkositabbaṁ.
segs.e: You should neither approve nor reject that mendicant’s statement.

segs.p: Anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā tāni padabyañjanāni sādhukaṁ uggahetvā sutte otāretabbāni, vinaye sandassetabbāni.
segs.e: Instead, having carefully memorized those words and phrases, you should make sure they fit in the discourse and are exhibited in the training.

segs.p: Tāni ce sutte otāriyamānāni, vinaye sandassiyamānāni sutte ceva otaranti vinaye ca sandissanti, niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṁ:
segs.e: If they fit in the discourse and are exhibited in the training, you should draw the conclusion:

segs.p: ‘addhā idaṁ tassa bhagavato vacanaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassa;
segs.e: ‘Clearly this is the word of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.
It has been correctly memorized by that Saṅgha.’
You should remember it. This is the second great reference.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Take another mendicant who says:

segs.p: ‘asukasmiṁ nāma āvāse sambahulā therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā vinayadharā mātikādharā.
segs.e: ‘In such-and-such monastery there are several senior mendicants who are very learned, inheritors of the heritage, who remember the teachings, the monastic law, and the outlines.

segs.p: Tesaṁ me therānaṁ sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ—
segs.e: I’ve heard and learned this in the presence of those senior mendicants:

segs.p: ayaṁ dhammo, ayaṁ vinayo, idaṁ satthusāsanan’ti.
segs.e: this is the teaching, this is the training, this is the Teacher’s instruction.’

Numbered Discourses 4.181
19. Brahmins
A Warrior

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato yodhājīvo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a warrior with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, yodhājīvo ṭhānakusalo ca hoti, dūrepātī ca, akkhaṇavedhī ca, mahato ca kāyassa padāletā.
segs.e: He’s skilled in the basics, a long-distance shooter, a marksman, one who shatters large objects.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi aṅgehi samannāgato yodhājīvo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A warrior with these four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ṭhānakusalo ca hoti, dūrepātī ca, akkhaṇavedhī ca, mahato ca kāyassa padāletā.
segs.e: He’s skilled in the basics, a long-distance shooter, a marksman, one who shatters large objects.
And how is a mendicant skilled in the basics?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ṭhānakusalo hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is skilled in the basics.
And how is a mendicant a long-distance shooter?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ rūpaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant truly sees any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
They truly see any kind of feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dūrepātī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is a long-distance shooter.
And how is a mendicant a marksman?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkhaṇavedhī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is a marksman.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahato kāyassa padāletā hoti?
segs.e: And how does a mendicant shatter large objects?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahantaṁ avijjākkhandhaṁ padāletā.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant shatters the great mass of ignorance.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mahato kāyassa padāletā hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant shatters large objects.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.182
19. Brahmins
Guarantee
“There are four things that no one can guarantee—

segs.p: samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṁ.
segs.e: not an ascetic, a brahmin, a god, a Māra, a divinity, or anyone in the world.
What four?
No one can guarantee that someone liable to old age will not grow old.

segs.p: samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṁ;

segs.e: No one can guarantee that someone liable to sickness will not get sick.

segs.p: samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṁ;

segs.e: No one can guarantee that someone liable to death will not die.

segs.p: samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṁ;
‘yāni kho pana tāni pubbe attanā katāni pāpakāni kammāni saṅkilesikāni ponobhavikāni sadarāni dukkhavipākāni āyatiṁ jātijarāmaraṇikāni, tesaṁ vipāko mā nibbattī’ti natthi koci pāṭibhogo—
segs.e: No one can guarantee that the bad deeds done in past lives—corrupting, leading to future lives, hurtful, resulting in suffering and future rebirth, old age, and death—will not produce their result.

segs.p: samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmiṁ.
Imesaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catunnaṁ dhammānaṁ natthi koci pāṭibhogo—
segs.e: These are the four things that no one can guarantee—

segs.p: samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā koci vā lokasmin”ti.
segs.e: not an ascetic, a brahmin, a god, a Māra, a divinity, or anyone in the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.183
19. Brahmins
Vassakāra on What is Heard

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Vassakāra the brahmin, a chief minister of Magadha, went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:
“Worthy Gotama, this is my doctrine and view:
There’s nothing wrong with talking about what you’ve seen, saying:

segs.p: evaṁ me diṭṭhanti, natthi tato doso;
segs.e: ‘So I have seen.’
There’s nothing wrong with talking about what you’ve heard, saying:

segs.p: evaṁ me sutanti, natthi tato doso;
segs.e: ‘So I have heard.’
There’s nothing wrong with talking about what you’ve thought, saying:

segs.p: evaṁ me mutanti, natthi tato doso;
segs.e: ‘So I have thought.’
There’s nothing wrong with talking about what you’ve known, saying:

segs.p: evaṁ me viññātanti, natthi tato doso’”ti.
segs.e: ‘So I have known.’”
“Brahmin, I don’t say you should talk about everything you see, hear, think, and know.

segs.p: na panāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sabbaṁ diṭṭhaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi;
segs.e: But I also don’t say you should talk about nothing you see, hear, think, and know.

segs.p: nāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sabbaṁ sutaṁ bhāsitabbanti vadāmi;
na panāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sabbaṁ sutaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi;
nāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sabbaṁ mutaṁ bhāsitabbanti vadāmi;
na panāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sabbaṁ mutaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi;
nāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sabbaṁ viññātaṁ bhāsitabbanti vadāmi;
na panāhaṁ, brāhmaṇa, sabbaṁ viññātaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
Yañhi, brāhmaṇa, diṭṭhaṁ bhāsato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṁ diṭṭhaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When talking about certain things you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known, unskillful qualities grow while skillful qualities decline. I say that you shouldn’t talk about those things.

segs.p: Yañca khvassa, brāhmaṇa, diṭṭhaṁ abhāsato kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṁ diṭṭhaṁ bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
segs.e: When talking about other things you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known, unskillful qualities decline while skillful qualities grow. I say that you should talk about those things.”

segs.p: Yañhi, brāhmaṇa, sutaṁ bhāsato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṁ sutaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
Yañca khvassa, brāhmaṇa, sutaṁ abhāsato kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṁ sutaṁ bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
Yañhi, brāhmaṇa, mutaṁ bhāsato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṁ mutaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
Yañca khvassa, brāhmaṇa, mutaṁ abhāsato kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṁ mutaṁ bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
Yañhi, brāhmaṇa, viññātaṁ bhāsato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, evarūpaṁ viññātaṁ na bhāsitabbanti vadāmi.
Yañca khvassa, brāhmaṇa, viññātaṁ abhāsato kusalā dhammā parihāyanti, akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, evarūpaṁ viññātaṁ bhāsitabbanti vadāmī”ti.
Atha kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti.
segs.e: Then Vassakāra the brahmin, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, rose from his seat and left.
Numbered Discourses 4.184
19. Brahmins
Fearless

segs.p: Atha kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Jānussoṇi went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:
“Worthy Gotama, this is my doctrine and view:

segs.p: ‘natthi yo maraṇadhammo samāno na bhāyati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘All those liable to death are frightened and terrified of death.’”

segs.p: “Atthi, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno bhāyati, santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa;
segs.e: “Brahmin, some of those liable to death are frightened and terrified of death.

segs.p: atthi pana, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno na bhāyati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: But some of those liable to death are not frightened and terrified of death.

segs.p: Katamo ca, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno bhāyati, santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa?
segs.e: Who are those frightened of death?

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho.
segs.e: It’s someone who isn’t free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they think:

segs.p: ‘piyā vata maṁ kāmā jahissanti, piye cāhaṁ kāme jahissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The sensual pleasures that I love so much will leave me, and I’ll leave them.’

segs.p: So socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno bhāyati, santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This is someone who is frightened of death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco kāye avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s someone who isn’t free of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for the body.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they think:

segs.p: ‘piyo vata maṁ kāyo jahissati, piyañcāhaṁ kāyaṁ jahissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘This body that I love so much will leave me, and I’ll leave it.’

segs.p: So socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno bhāyati, santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This, too, is someone who is frightened of death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco akatakalyāṇo hoti akatakusalo akatabhīruttāṇo katapāpo kataluddo katakibbiso.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s someone who hasn’t done good and skillful things that keep them safe, but has done bad things, violence and sin.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they think:

segs.p: ‘akataṁ vata me kalyāṇaṁ, akataṁ kusalaṁ, akataṁ bhīruttāṇaṁ;
segs.e: ‘Well, I haven’t done good and skillful things that keep me safe.

segs.p: kataṁ pāpaṁ, kataṁ luddaṁ, kataṁ kibbisaṁ.
segs.e: And I have done bad things, violence and sin.

segs.p: Yāvatā, bho, akatakalyāṇānaṁ akatakusalānaṁ akatabhīruttāṇānaṁ katapāpānaṁ kataluddānaṁ katakibbisānaṁ gati taṁ gatiṁ pecca gacchāmī’ti.
segs.e: When I depart, I’ll go to the place where people who’ve done such things go.’

segs.p: So socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno bhāyati, santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This, too, is someone who is frightened of death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco kaṅkhī hoti vicikicchī aniṭṭhaṅgato saddhamme.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s someone who’s doubtful, uncertain, and undecided about the true teaching.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they think:
‘I’m doubtful, uncertain, and undecided about the true teaching.’

segs.p: So socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno bhāyati, santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This, too, is someone who is frightened of death.

segs.p: Ime kho, brāhmaṇa, cattāro maraṇadhammā samānā bhāyanti, santāsaṁ āpajjanti maraṇassa.
segs.e: These are the four individuals liable to death who are frightened and terrified of death.

segs.p: Katamo ca, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno na bhāyati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa?
segs.e: Who are those not frightened of death?

segs.p: Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco kāmesu vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho.
segs.e: It’s someone who is rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for sensual pleasures.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa na evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they don’t think:

segs.p: ‘piyā vata maṁ kāmā jahissanti, piye cāhaṁ kāme jahissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The sensual pleasures that I love so much will leave me, and I’ll leave them.’

segs.p: So na socati na kilamati na paridevati, na urattāḷiṁ kandati, na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They don’t sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno na bhāyati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This is someone who’s not frightened of death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco kāye vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s someone who is rid of greed, desire, fondness, thirst, passion, and craving for the body.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa na evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they don’t think:

segs.p: ‘piyo vata maṁ kāyo jahissati, piyañcāhaṁ kāyaṁ jahissāmī’ti.
segs.e: ‘This body that I love so much will leave me, and I’ll leave it.’

segs.p: So na socati na kilamati na paridevati, na urattāḷiṁ kandati, na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They don’t sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno na bhāyati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This, too, is someone who’s not frightened of death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco akatapāpo hoti akataluddo akatakibbiso katakalyāṇo katakusalo katabhīruttāṇo.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s someone who hasn’t done bad things, violence and sin, but has done good and skillful deeds that keep them safe.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they think:

segs.p: ‘akataṁ vata me pāpaṁ, akataṁ luddaṁ, akataṁ kibbisaṁ;
segs.e: ‘Well, I haven’t done bad things, violence and sin.

segs.p: kataṁ kalyāṇaṁ, kataṁ kusalaṁ, kataṁ bhīruttāṇaṁ.
segs.e: And I have done good and skillful deeds that keep me safe.

segs.p: Yāvatā, bho, akatapāpānaṁ akataluddānaṁ akatakibbisānaṁ katakalyāṇānaṁ katakusalānaṁ katabhīruttāṇānaṁ gati taṁ gatiṁ pecca gacchāmī’ti.
segs.e: When I depart, I’ll go to the place where people who’ve done such things go.’

segs.p: So na socati na kilamati na paridevati, na urattāḷiṁ kandati, na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They don’t sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno na bhāyati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This, too, is someone who’s not frightened of death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, brāhmaṇa, idhekacco akaṅkhī hoti avicikicchī niṭṭhaṅgato saddhamme.
segs.e: Furthermore, it’s someone who’s not doubtful, uncertain, or undecided about the true teaching.
When they fall seriously ill,

segs.p: Tassa aññatarena gāḷhena rogātaṅkena phuṭṭhassa evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: they think:
‘I’m not doubtful, uncertain, or undecided about the true teaching.’

segs.p: So na socati na kilamati na paridevati, na urattāḷiṁ kandati, na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They don’t sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, brāhmaṇa, maraṇadhammo samāno na bhāyati, na santāsaṁ āpajjati maraṇassa.
segs.e: This, too, is someone who’s not frightened of death.

segs.p: Ime kho, brāhmaṇa, cattāro maraṇadhammā samānā na bhāyanti, na santāsaṁ āpajjanti maraṇassā”ti.
segs.e: These are the four individuals liable to death who are not frightened and terrified of death.”

segs.p: “Abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṁ, bho gotama …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: “Excellent, worthy Gotama! … From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 4.185
19. Brahmins
Truths of the Brahmins

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: Once the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā paribbājakā sippinikātīre paribbājakārāme paṭivasanti, seyyathidaṁ annabhāro varadharo sakuludāyī ca paribbājako aññe ca abhiññātā abhiññātā paribbājakā.
segs.e: Now at that time several very well-known wanderers were residing in their monastery on the bank of the Serpentine River. They included Annabhāra, Varadhara, Sakuludāyī, and other very well-known wanderers.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena sippinikātīre paribbājakārāmo tenupasaṅkami.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the monastery for the wanderers on the bank of the Serpentine River.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena tesaṁ aññatitthiyānaṁ paribbājakānaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarā kathā udapādi:
segs.e: Now at that time this discussion came up while those wanderers of other religions were sitting together,
“The truths of the brahmins are like this; the truths of the brahmins are like that.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā yena te paribbājakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā te paribbājake etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha went up to those wanderers, sat down on the seat spread out, and said to them,

segs.p: “Kāya nuttha, paribbājakā, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti?
segs.e: “Wanderers, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”

segs.p: “Idha, bho gotama, amhākaṁ sannisinnānaṁ sannipatitānaṁ ayamantarākathā udapādi:
segs.e: “Well, worthy Gotama, this discussion came up among us while we were sitting together:
‘The truths of the brahmins are like this; the truths of the brahmins are like that.’”

segs.p: “Cattārimāni, paribbājakā, brāhmaṇasaccāni mayā sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditāni.
segs.e: “Wanderers, I declare these four truths of the brahmins, having realized them with my own insight.
What four?
Take a brahmin who says:
‘No sentient beings should be killed.’

segs.p: Iti vadaṁ brāhmaṇo saccaṁ āha, no musā.
segs.e: In speaking like this, a brahmin speaks the truth, not lies.

segs.p: So tena na samaṇoti maññati, na brāhmaṇoti maññati, na seyyohamasmīti maññati, na sadisohamasmīti maññati, na hīnohamasmīti maññati.
segs.e: But they don’t think of themselves as an ‘ascetic’ or ‘brahmin’ because of that. Nor do they think ‘I’m better’ or ‘I’m equal’ or ‘I’m worse’.

segs.p: Api ca yadeva tattha saccaṁ tadabhiññāya pāṇānaṁyeva anuddayāya anukampāya paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: Rather, they simply practice out of kindness and sympathy for living creatures, having had insight into the truth of that.
Take another brahmin who says:
‘All sensual pleasures are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.’

segs.p: Iti vadaṁ brāhmaṇo saccamāha, no musā.
segs.e: Saying this, a brahmin speaks the truth, not lies.

segs.p: So tena na samaṇoti maññati, na brāhmaṇoti maññati, na seyyohamasmīti maññati, na sadisohamasmīti maññati, na hīnohamasmīti maññati.
segs.e: But they don’t think of themselves as an ‘ascetic’ or ‘brahmin’ because of that. Nor do they think ‘I’m better’ or ‘I’m equal’ or ‘I’m worse’.

segs.p: Api ca yadeva tattha saccaṁ tadabhiññāya kāmānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: Rather, they simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding sensual pleasures, having had insight into the truth of that.
Take another brahmin who says:

segs.p: ‘sabbe bhavā aniccā …pe… tadabhiññāya bhavānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: ‘All states of existence are impermanent, suffering, and perishable.’ … They simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding future lives, having had insight into the truth of that.
Take another brahmin who says:

segs.p: ‘nāhaṁ kvacani kassaci kiñcanatasmiṁ na ca mama kvacani katthaci kiñcanatatthī’ti.
segs.e: ‘I don’t belong to anyone anywhere. And nothing belongs to me anywhere.’

segs.p: Iti vadaṁ brāhmaṇo saccaṁ āha, no musā.
segs.e: In speaking like this, a brahmin speaks the truth, not lies.

segs.p: So tena na samaṇoti maññati, na brāhmaṇoti maññati, na seyyohamasmīti maññati, na sadisohamasmīti maññati, na hīnohamasmīti maññati.
segs.e: But they don’t think of themselves as an ‘ascetic’ or ‘brahmin’ because of that. Nor do they think ‘I’m better’ or ‘I’m equal’ or ‘I’m worse’.

segs.p: Api ca yadeva tattha saccaṁ tadabhiññāya ākiñcaññaṁyeva paṭipadaṁ paṭipanno hoti.
segs.e: Rather, they simply practice the path of nothingness, having had insight into the truth of that.

segs.p: Imāni kho, paribbājakā, cattāri brāhmaṇasaccāni mayā sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā paveditānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the four truths of the brahmins that I declare, having realized them with my own insight.”
Numbered Discourses 4.186
19. Brahmins
Approach

segs.p: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then one of the mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “kena nu kho, bhante, loko nīyati, kena loko parikassati, kassa ca uppannassa vasaṁ gacchatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what leads the world on? What drags it around? What arises and takes control?”
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Bhaddako kho te, bhikkhu, ummaggo, bhaddakaṁ paṭibhānaṁ, kalyāṇī paripucchā.
segs.e: Your approach and eloquence are excellent, and it’s a good question.
For you asked:

segs.p: ‘kena nu kho, bhante, loko nīyati, kena loko parikassati, kassa ca uppannassa vasaṁ gacchatī’”ti?
segs.e: ‘What leads the world on? What drags it around? What arises and takes control?’”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Cittena kho, bhikkhu, loko nīyati, cittena parikassati, cittassa uppannassa vasaṁ gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: “Mendicant, the mind leads the world on. The mind drags it around. When the mind arises, it takes control.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṁ uttari pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir”, that monk approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. Then he asked another question:
“Sir, they speak of ‘a learned memorizer of the teaching’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bahussuto dhammadharo hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is a learned memorizer of the teaching defined?”
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Bhaddako kho te, bhikkhu ummaggo, bhaddakaṁ paṭibhānaṁ, kalyāṇī paripucchā.
segs.e: Your approach and eloquence are excellent, and it’s a good question. …

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, bahussuto dhammadharo hotī’”ti?

segs.e: I have taught many teachings:

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthā, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Catuppadāya cepi, bhikkhu, gāthāya atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti bahussuto dhammadharoti alaṁvacanāyā”ti.
segs.e: But if anyone understands the meaning and the text of even a four-line verse, and if they practice in line with that teaching, they’re qualified to be called a ‘learned memorizer of the teaching’.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṁ uttari pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir”, that monk approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. Then he asked another question:
“Sir, they speak of ‘a learned person with penetrating wisdom’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sutavā nibbedhikapañño hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is a learned person with penetrating wisdom defined?”
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Bhaddako kho te, bhikkhu, ummaggo, bhaddakaṁ paṭibhānaṁ, kalyāṇī paripucchā.
segs.e: Your approach and eloquence are excellent, and it’s a good question. …

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, sutavā nibbedhikapañño hotī’”ti?
“Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhuno ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti sutaṁ hoti, paññāya cassa atthaṁ ativijjha passati;
segs.e: Take a mendicant who has heard: ‘This is suffering.’ They see what it means with penetrating wisdom.

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ dukkhasamudayo’ti sutaṁ hoti, paññāya cassa atthaṁ ativijjha passati;
segs.e: They’ve heard: ‘This is the origin of suffering’ …

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodho’ti sutaṁ hoti, paññāya cassa atthaṁ ativijjha passati;
segs.e: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ …

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti sutaṁ hoti, paññāya cassa atthaṁ ativijjha passati.
segs.e: ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering.’ They see what it means with penetrating wisdom.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, sutavā nibbedhikapañño hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is learned, with penetrating wisdom.”

segs.p: “Sādhu, bhante”ti kho so bhikkhu bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā bhagavantaṁ uttari pañhaṁ apucchi:
segs.e: Saying “Good, sir”, that monk approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. Then he asked another question:
“Sir, they speak of ‘an astute person with great wisdom’.

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, paṇḍito mahāpañño hotī”ti?
segs.e: How is an astute person with great wisdom defined?”
“Good, good, mendicant!

segs.p: Bhaddako kho te, bhikkhu, ummaggo, bhaddakaṁ paṭibhānaṁ, kalyāṇī paripucchā.
segs.e: Your approach and eloquence are excellent, and it’s a good question. …

segs.p: Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, paṇḍito mahāpañño hotī’”ti?
“Idha, bhikkhu, paṇḍito mahāpañño nevattabyābādhāya ceteti na parabyābādhāya ceteti na ubhayabyābādhāya ceteti attahitaparahitaubhayahitasabbalokahitameva cintayamāno cinteti.
segs.e: An astute person with great wisdom is one who has no intention to hurt themselves, or to hurt others, or to hurt both. When they think, they only think of the benefit for themselves, for others, for both, and for the whole world.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhu, paṇḍito mahāpañño hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how an individual is astute, with great wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 4.187
19. Brahmins
With Vassakāra

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Atha kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then Vassakāra the brahmin, a chief minister of Magadha, went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “Jāneyya nu kho, bho gotama, asappuriso asappurisaṁ:
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, could an untrue person know of an untrue person:
‘This worthy one is an untrue person’?”

segs.p: “Aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, brāhmaṇa, anavakāso yaṁ asappuriso asappurisaṁ jāneyya:
segs.e: “That’s impossible, brahmin, it can’t happen.”
“Could an untrue person know of a true person:
‘This worthy one is a true person’?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṁ anavakāso yaṁ asappuriso sappurisaṁ jāneyya:
segs.e: “That too is impossible, it can’t happen.”

segs.p: “Jāneyya nu kho, bho gotama, sappuriso sappurisaṁ:
segs.e: “Worthy Gotama, could a true person know of a true person:
‘This worthy one is a true person’?”

segs.p: “Ṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vijjati yaṁ sappuriso sappurisaṁ jāneyya:
segs.e: “That, brahmin, is possible.”
“Could a true person know of an untrue person:
‘This worthy one is an untrue person’?”

segs.p: “Etampi kho, brāhmaṇa, ṭhānaṁ vijjati yaṁ sappuriso asappurisaṁ jāneyya:
segs.e: “That too is possible.”
“It’s incredible, worthy Gotama, it’s amazing,
how well said this was by the worthy Gotama:

segs.p: ‘aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, brāhmaṇa, anavakāso yaṁ asappuriso asappurisaṁ jāneyya—
segs.e: ‘It’s impossible, it can’t happen, that an untrue person could know …

segs.p: Etampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṁ anavakāso yaṁ asappuriso sappurisaṁ jāneyya—
Ṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vijjati yaṁ sappuriso sappurisaṁ jāneyya—
segs.e: But it is possible that a true person could know …’

segs.p: Etampi kho, brāhmaṇa, ṭhānaṁ vijjati yaṁ sappuriso asappurisaṁ jāneyya—
Ekamidaṁ, bho gotama, samayaṁ todeyyassa brāhmaṇassa parisati parūpārambhaṁ vattenti:
segs.e: Once, members of the brahmin Todeyya’s assembly were going on complaining about others:

segs.p: ‘bālo ayaṁ rājā eḷeyyo samaṇe rāmaputte abhippasanno, samaṇe ca pana rāmaputte evarūpaṁ paramanipaccakāraṁ karoti, yadidaṁ abhivādanaṁ paccuṭṭhānaṁ añjalikammaṁ sāmīcikammanti.
segs.e: ‘This King Eḷeyya is a fool to be so devoted to the ascetic Rāmaputta. He even shows him the utmost deference by bowing down to him, rising up for him, greeting him with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for him.
And these king’s men are fools too—

segs.p: yamako moggallo uggo nāvindakī gandhabbo aggivesso, ye samaṇe rāmaputte abhippasannā, samaṇe ca pana rāmaputte evarūpaṁ paramanipaccakāraṁ karonti, yadidaṁ abhivādanaṁ paccuṭṭhānaṁ añjalikammaṁ sāmīcikamman’ti.
segs.e: Yamaka, Moggalla, Ugga, Nāvindakī, Gandhabba, and Aggivessa—for they show the same kind of deference to Rāmaputta.’

segs.p: Tyāssudaṁ todeyyo brāhmaṇo iminā nayena neti.
segs.e: Then the brahmin Todeyya reasoned with them like this:
‘What do the good fellows think?

segs.p: paṇḍito rājā eḷeyyo karaṇīyādhikaraṇīyesu vacanīyādhivacanīyesu alamatthadasatarehi alamatthadasataro’ti?
segs.e: When it comes to the various duties and speeches, isn’t King Eḷeyya astute, even better than the experts?’

segs.p: ‘Evaṁ, bho, paṇḍito rājā eḷeyyo karaṇīyādhikaraṇīyesu vacanīyādhivacanīyesu alamatthadasatarehi alamatthadasataroti.
segs.e: ‘That’s true, worthy sir.’

segs.p: Yasmā ca kho, bho, samaṇo rāmaputto raññā eḷeyyena paṇḍitena paṇḍitataro karaṇīyādhikaraṇīyesu vacanīyādhivacanīyesu alamatthadasatarena alamatthadasataro, tasmā rājā eḷeyyo samaṇe rāmaputte abhippasanno, samaṇe ca pana rāmaputte evarūpaṁ paramanipaccakāraṁ karoti, yadidaṁ abhivādanaṁ paccuṭṭhānaṁ añjalikammaṁ sāmīcikammaṁ’.
segs.e: ‘It’s because the ascetic Rāmaputta is even more astute and expert than King Eḷeyya that the king is so devoted to him. That’s why he even shows Rāmaputta the utmost deference by bowing down to him, rising up for him, greeting him with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for him.
‘What do the good fellows think?

segs.p: yamako moggallo uggo nāvindakī gandhabbo aggivesso, karaṇīyādhikaraṇīyesu vacanīyādhivacanīyesu alamatthadasatarehi alamatthadasatarā’ti?
segs.e: When it comes to the various duties and speeches, aren’t the king’s men—Yamaka, Moggalla, Ugga, Nāvindakī, Gandhabba, and Aggivessa—astute, even better than the experts?’
‘That’s true, worthy sir.’

segs.p: yamako moggallo uggo nāvindakī gandhabbo aggivesso, karaṇīyādhikaraṇīyesu vacanīyādhivacanīyesu alamatthadasatarehi alamatthadasatarāti.

Yasmā ca kho, bho, samaṇo rāmaputto rañño eḷeyyassa parihārakehi paṇḍitehi paṇḍitataro karaṇīyādhikaraṇīyesu vacanīyādhivacanīyesu alamatthadasatarehi alamatthadasataro, tasmā rañño eḷeyyassa parihārakā samaṇe rāmaputte abhippasannā;
segs.e: ‘It’s because Rāmaputta is even more astute and expert than the king’s men that they have such devotion to him. …

segs.p: samaṇe ca pana rāmaputte evarūpaṁ paramanipaccakāraṁ karonti, yadidaṁ abhivādanaṁ paccuṭṭhānaṁ añjalikammaṁ sāmīcikamman’ti.
segs.e: It’s because Rāmaputta is even more astute and expert than King Eḷeyya that the king is so devoted to him. That’s why he even shows Rāmaputta the utmost deference by bowing down to him, rising up for him, greeting him with cupped palms, and observing proper etiquette for him.’

segs.p: Acchariyaṁ, bho gotama, abbhutaṁ, bho gotama.
segs.e: It’s incredible, worthy Gotama, it’s amazing,
how well said this was by the worthy Gotama:

segs.p: ‘aṭṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, brāhmaṇa, anavakāso yaṁ asappuriso asappurisaṁ jāneyya—
segs.e: ‘It’s impossible, it can’t happen, that an untrue person could know …

segs.p: Etampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṁ anavakāso yaṁ asappuriso sappurisaṁ jāneyya—
Ṭhānaṁ kho etaṁ, brāhmaṇa, vijjati yaṁ sappuriso sappurisaṁ jāneyya—
segs.e: But it is possible that a true person could know …’

segs.p: Etampi kho, brāhmaṇa, ṭhānaṁ vijjati yaṁ sappuriso asappurisaṁ jāneyya—
Handa ca dāni mayaṁ, bho gotama, gacchāma.
segs.e: Well, now, worthy Gotama, I must go.
I have many duties, and much to do.”
“Please, brahmin, go at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho vassakāro brāhmaṇo magadhamahāmatto bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmīti.
segs.e: Then Vassakāra the brahmin, having approved and agreed with what the Buddha said, rose from his seat and left.
Numbered Discourses 4.188
19. Brahmins
With Upaka

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate.
segs.e: Once the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha, on the Vulture’s Peak Mountain.

segs.p: Atha kho upako maṇḍikāputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho upako maṇḍikāputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Upaka the son of Maṇḍikā went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, this is my doctrine and view:

segs.p: ‘yo koci parūpārambhaṁ vatteti, parūpārambhaṁ vattento sabbo so na upapādeti.
segs.e: ‘Whoever goes on complaining about others without giving any reasons
is reprehensible and at fault.’”

segs.p: “Parūpārambhañce, upaka, vatteti parūpārambhaṁ vattento na upapādeti, anupapādento gārayho hoti upavajjo.
segs.e: “Upaka, if someone goes on complaining about others without giving a reason, they’re reprehensible and at fault.

segs.p: Tvaṁ kho, upaka, parūpārambhaṁ vattesi, parūpārambhaṁ vattento na upapādesi, anupapādento gārayho hosi upavajjo”ti.
segs.e: But that’s what you do, so you’re reprehensible and at fault!”
“Sir, like a fish caught in a big trap just as it rises,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, ummujjamānakoyeva bhagavatā mahatā vādapāsena baddho”ti.
segs.e: so the Buddha caught me in a big trap of words just as I rose up.”
“Upaka, I’ve declared: ‘This is unskillful.’

segs.p: Tattha aparimāṇā padā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā tathāgatassa dhammadesanā—
segs.e: And for that there are limitless words, phrasings, and teachings of the Realized One:
‘This is another way of saying that this is unskillful.’

segs.p: Taṁ kho panidaṁ akusalaṁ pahātabbanti kho, upaka, mayā paññattaṁ.
segs.e: I’ve declared: ‘The unskillful should be given up.’

segs.p: Tattha aparimāṇā padā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā tathāgatassa dhammadesanā—
