segs.e: And for that there are limitless words, phrasings, and teachings of the Realized One:
‘This is another way of saying that the unskillful should be given up.’

segs.p: Idaṁ kusalanti kho, upaka, mayā paññattaṁ.
segs.e: I’ve declared that: ‘This is skillful.’

segs.p: Tattha aparimāṇā padā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā tathāgatassa dhammadesanā—
segs.e: And for that there are limitless words, phrasings, and teachings of the Realized One:
‘This is another way of saying that this is skillful.’

segs.p: Taṁ kho panidaṁ kusalaṁ bhāvetabbanti kho, upaka, mayā paññattaṁ.
segs.e: I’ve declared: ‘The skillful should be developed.’

segs.p: Tattha aparimāṇā padā aparimāṇā byañjanā aparimāṇā tathāgatassa dhammadesanā—
segs.e: And for that there are limitless words, phrasings, and teachings of the Realized One:
‘This is another way of saying that the skillful should be developed.’”

segs.p: Atha kho upako maṇḍikāputto bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā yena rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā yāvatako ahosi bhagavatā saddhiṁ kathāsallāpo taṁ sabbaṁ rañño māgadhassa ajātasattussa vedehiputtassa ārocesi.
segs.e: And then Upaka son of Maṇḍikā approved and agreed with what the Buddha said. He got up from his seat, bowed and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right. Then he went up to King Ajātasattu of Magadha, son of the princess of Videha. He told the King of all they had discussed.

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, rājā māgadho ajātasattu vedehiputto kupito anattamano upakaṁ maṇḍikāputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: But Ajātasattu became angry and upset, and said to Upaka,

segs.p: “yāva dhaṁsī vatāyaṁ loṇakāradārako yāva mukharo yāva pagabbo yatra hi nāma taṁ bhagavantaṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ āsādetabbaṁ maññissati;
segs.e: “How rude of this salt-maker’s boy! How scurrilous and impudent of him to imagine he could attack the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha!

segs.p: apehi tvaṁ, upaka, vinassa, mā taṁ addasan”ti.
segs.e: Get out, Upaka, go away! Don’t let me see you again.”
Numbered Discourses 4.189
19. Brahmins
Things to be Realized
“Mendicants, these four things should be realized.
What four?
There are things to be realized with direct meditative experience.
There are things to be realized with recollection.
There are things to be realized with vision.
There are things to be realized with wisdom.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā kāyena sacchikaraṇīyā?
segs.e: What things are to be realized with direct meditative experience?
The eight liberations.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā satiyā sacchikaraṇīyā?
segs.e: What things are to be realized with recollection?
Past lives.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā cakkhunā sacchikaraṇīyā?
segs.e: What things are to be realized with vision?
The passing away and rebirth of sentient beings.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā paññāya sacchikaraṇīyā?
segs.e: What things are to be realized with wisdom?
The ending of defilements.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro sacchikaraṇīyā dhammā”ti.
segs.e: These are the four things to be realized.”
Numbered Discourses 4.190
19. Brahmins
Sabbath

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisinno hoti.
segs.e: Now, at that time it was the sabbath, and the Buddha was sitting surrounded by the Saṅgha of monks.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā tuṇhībhūtaṁ tuṇhībhūtaṁ bhikkhusaṅghaṁ anuviloketvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha looked around the Saṅgha of monks, who were so very silent. He addressed them:

segs.p: “Apalāpāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā nippalāpāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā suddhā sāre patiṭṭhitā.
segs.e: “This assembly has no chaff, monks, it is free of chaff, pure, and consolidated in the core.

segs.p: Tathārūpo ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho, tathārūpāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā.
segs.e: Such is this Saṅgha of monks, such is this assembly!

segs.p: Yathārūpā parisā dullabhā dassanāyapi lokasmiṁ, tathārūpo ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho, tathārūpāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā.
segs.e: An assembly such as this is rarely seen in the world.

segs.p: Yathārūpā parisā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa, tathārūpo ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho, tathārūpāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā.
segs.e: An assembly such as this is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya parisāya appaṁ dinnaṁ bahu hoti bahu dinnaṁ bahutaraṁ, tathārūpo ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho, tathārūpāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā.
segs.e: For an assembly such as this, giving little becomes much, while giving much becomes even more.

segs.p: Yathārūpaṁ parisaṁ alaṁ yojanagaṇanānipi dassanāya gantuṁ api puṭosenāpi, tathārūpo ayaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhusaṅgho, tathārūpāyaṁ, bhikkhave, parisā.
segs.e: An assembly such as this is worth traveling many leagues to see, even if you have to carry your own provisions in a knapsack.

segs.p: Santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe devappattā viharanti;
segs.e: There are mendicants staying in this Saṅgha who have attained to the gods.

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe brahmappattā viharanti;
segs.e: There are mendicants staying in this Saṅgha who have attained to divinity.

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe āneñjappattā viharanti;
segs.e: There are mendicants staying in this Saṅgha who have attained to the imperturbable.

segs.p: santi, bhikkhave, bhikkhū imasmiṁ bhikkhusaṅghe ariyappattā viharanti.
segs.e: There are mendicants staying in this Saṅgha who have attained to nobility.
And how has a mendicant attained to the gods?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption …

segs.p: vitakkavicārānaṁ vūpasamā …pe… dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: As the placing of the mind and keeping it connected are stilled, they enter and remain in the second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu devappatto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has attained to the gods.
And how has a mendicant attained to divinity?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant meditates spreading a heart full of love to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of love to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.
Furthermore, a mendicant meditates spreading a heart full of compassion …
rejoicing …

segs.p: upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṁ disaṁ pharitvā viharati, tathā dutiyaṁ tathā tatiyaṁ tathā catutthaṁ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṁ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṁ lokaṁ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.
segs.e: equanimity to one direction, and to the second, and to the third, and to the fourth. In the same way above, below, across, everywhere, all around, they spread a heart full of equanimity to the whole world—abundant, expansive, limitless, free of enmity and ill will.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu brahmappatto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has attained to divinity.
And how has a mendicant attained to the imperturbable?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabbaso rūpasaññānaṁ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṁ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṁ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, going totally beyond perceptions of form, with the ending of perceptions of impingement, not focusing on perceptions of diversity, aware that ‘space is infinite’, enters and remains in the dimension of infinite space.

segs.p: Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘anantaṁ viññāṇan’ti viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite’, he enters and remains in the dimension of infinite consciousness.

segs.p: Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṁ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of infinite consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing at all’, he enters and remains in the dimension of nothingness.

segs.p: Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṁ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: Going totally beyond the dimension of nothingness, he enters and remains in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āneñjappatto hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has attained to the imperturbable.
And how has a mendicant attained to nobility?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ariyappatto hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant has attained to nobility.”
Numbered Discourses 4.191
20. The Great Chapter
Followed by Ear

segs.p: “Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ cattāro ānisaṁsā pāṭikaṅkhā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, you can expect four benefits when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well penetrated theoretically.
What four?
Take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: They’ve followed those teachings by ear, consolidated them by voice, examined them by the mind, and well penetrated them theoretically.

segs.p: So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods.
Being happy there, passages of the teaching come back to them.
Memory comes up slowly,

segs.p: atha so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
segs.e: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

segs.p: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ayaṁ paṭhamo ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: This is the first benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well penetrated theoretically.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: They’ve followed those teachings by ear, consolidated them by voice, examined them by the mind, and well penetrated them theoretically.

segs.p: So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

segs.p: Tassa tattha na heva kho sukhino dhammapadā plavanti;
segs.e: Though they’re happy there, passages of the teaching don’t come back to them.

segs.p: api ca kho bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: However, a mendicant with psychic powers, who has achieved mastery of the mind, teaches Dhamma to the assembly of gods.
They think:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ vā so dhammavinayo, yatthāhaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarin’ti.
segs.e: ‘I used to lead the spiritual life in this same teaching and training.’
Memory comes up slowly,

segs.p: atha so satto khippameva visesagāmī hoti.
segs.e: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.
Suppose a person was skilled in the sound of drums.
While traveling along a road they hear the sound of drums.

segs.p: Tassa na heva kho assa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā:
segs.e: They wouldn’t have any doubts or uncertainties about whether

segs.p: ‘bherisaddo nu kho, na nu kho bherisaddo’ti.
segs.e: that was the sound of drums or not.
They’d just conclude, ‘That’s the sound of drums.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods. …

segs.p: Tassa tattha na heva kho sukhino dhammapadā plavanti;
api ca kho bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
‘ayaṁ vā so dhammavinayo, yatthāhaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarin’ti.

segs.e: Memory comes up slowly,

segs.p: atha so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
segs.e: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

segs.p: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ayaṁ dutiyo ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: This is the second benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well penetrated theoretically.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: They’ve followed those teachings by ear, consolidated them by voice, examined them by the mind, and well penetrated them theoretically.

segs.p: So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

segs.p: Tassa tattha na heva kho sukhino dhammapadā plavanti, napi bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti;
segs.e: But passages of the teaching don’t come back to them when they’re happy, nor does a mendicant with psychic powers … teach Dhamma to the assembly of gods.

segs.p: api ca kho devaputto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
segs.e: However, a godling teaches Dhamma to the assembly of gods.
They think:

segs.p: ‘ayaṁ vā so dhammavinayo, yatthāhaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarin’ti.
segs.e: ‘I used to lead the spiritual life in this same teaching and training.’
Memory comes up slowly,

segs.p: atha so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
segs.e: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.
Suppose a person was skilled in the sound of horns.
While traveling along a road they hear the sound of horns.

segs.p: Tassa na heva kho assa kaṅkhā vā vimati vā:
segs.e: They wouldn’t have any doubt about whether

segs.p: ‘saṅkhasaddo nu kho, na nu kho saṅkhasaddo’ti.
segs.e: that was the sound of horns or not.
They’d just conclude, ‘That’s the sound of horns.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods. …

segs.p: Tassa tattha na heva kho sukhino dhammapadā plavanti, napi bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti;
api ca kho devaputto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti.
‘ayaṁ vā so dhammavinayo, yatthāhaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarin’ti.

segs.e: Memory comes up slowly,

segs.p: atha so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
segs.e: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

segs.p: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ayaṁ tatiyo ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: This is the third benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well penetrated theoretically.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: Furthermore, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching—

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
segs.e: statements, mixed prose & verse, discussions, verses, inspired exclamations, legends, stories of past lives, amazing stories, and elaborations.

segs.p: Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
segs.e: They’ve followed those teachings by ear, consolidated them by voice, examined them by the mind, and well penetrated them theoretically.

segs.p: So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

segs.p: Tassa tattha na heva kho sukhino dhammapadā plavanti, napi bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti, napi devaputto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti;
segs.e: But passages of the teaching don’t come back to them when they’re happy, and neither a mendicant with psychic powers … nor a godling teaches Dhamma to the assembly of gods.

segs.p: api ca kho opapātiko opapātikaṁ sāreti:
segs.e: But a being who has been reborn spontaneously reminds another such being:

segs.p: ‘sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, yattha mayaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarimhā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Do you remember, good fellow? Do you remember where we used to lead the spiritual life?’
He says:
‘I remember, good fellow, I remember!’
Memory comes up slowly,

segs.p: atha so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
segs.e: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.
Suppose there were two friends who had played together in the sand.
Some time or other they’d meet.

segs.p: Añño pana sahāyako sahāyakaṁ evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: And one friend would say to the other:
‘Do you remember this, my dear? Do you remember that, my dear?’
They’d say:
‘I remember, my dear, I remember!’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammaṁ pariyāpuṇāti—
segs.e: In the same way, take a mendicant who memorizes the teaching …

segs.p: suttaṁ, geyyaṁ, veyyākaraṇaṁ, gāthaṁ, udānaṁ, itivuttakaṁ, jātakaṁ, abbhutadhammaṁ, vedallaṁ.
Tassa te dhammā sotānugatā honti, vacasā paricitā, manasānupekkhitā, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā.
So muṭṭhassati kālaṁ kurumāno aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: But they die unmindful and are reborn in one of the orders of gods. …

segs.p: Tassa tattha na heva kho sukhino dhammapadā plavanti, napi bhikkhu iddhimā cetovasippatto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti, napi devaputto devaparisāyaṁ dhammaṁ deseti;
api ca kho opapātiko opapātikaṁ sāreti:
‘sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, sarasi tvaṁ, mārisa, yattha mayaṁ pubbe brahmacariyaṁ acarimhā’ti.

segs.e: Memory comes up slowly,

segs.p: atha kho so satto khippaṁyeva visesagāmī hoti.
segs.e: but then that being quickly reaches distinction.

segs.p: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ, diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ayaṁ catuttho ānisaṁso pāṭikaṅkho.
segs.e: This is the fourth benefit you can expect when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well penetrated theoretically.

segs.p: Sotānugatānaṁ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṁ, vacasā paricitānaṁ, manasānupekkhitānaṁ diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhānaṁ ime cattāro ānisaṁsā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: You can expect these four benefits when the teachings have been followed by ear, consolidated by voice, examined by the mind, and well penetrated theoretically.”
Numbered Discourses 4.192
20. The Great Chapter
Facts
“Mendicants, these four things can be known in four situations.
What four?

segs.p: Saṁvāsena, bhikkhave, sīlaṁ veditabbaṁ, tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena.
segs.e: You can get to know a person’s ethics by living with them. But only after a long time, not casually; only when attentive, not when inattentive; and only by the wise, not the witless.

segs.p: Saṁvohārena, bhikkhave, soceyyaṁ veditabbaṁ, tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena.
segs.e: You can get to know a person’s purity by dealing with them. …

segs.p: Āpadāsu, bhikkhave, thāmo veditabbo, so ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññena.
segs.e: You can get to know a person’s resilience in times of trouble. …

segs.p: Sākacchāya, bhikkhave, paññā veditabbā, sā ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenāti.
segs.e: You can get to know a person’s wisdom by discussion. But only after a long time, not casually; only when attentive, not when inattentive; and only by the wise, not the witless.

segs.p: ‘Saṁvāsena, bhikkhave, sīlaṁ veditabbaṁ, tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti,
segs.e: ‘You can get to know a person’s ethics by living with them. But only after a long time, not casually; only when attentive, not when inattentive; and only by the wise, not the witless.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ saṁvasamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Take an individual who’s living with someone else. They come to know:

segs.p: ‘dīgharattaṁ kho ayamāyasmā khaṇḍakārī chiddakārī sabalakārī kammāsakārī, na santatakārī na santatavutti;
segs.e: ‘For a long time this venerable’s deeds have been broken, tainted, spotty, and marred. Their deeds and behavior are inconsistent.
This venerable is unethical, not ethical.’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ saṁvasamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Take another individual who’s living with someone else. They come to know:

segs.p: ‘dīgharattaṁ kho ayamāyasmā akhaṇḍakārī acchiddakārī asabalakārī akammāsakārī santatakārī santatavutti;
segs.e: ‘For a long time this venerable’s deeds have been intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred. Their deeds and behavior are consistent.
This venerable is ethical, not unethical.’

segs.p: ‘Saṁvāsena, bhikkhave, sīlaṁ veditabbaṁ, tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti, iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s why I said that you can get to know a person’s ethics by living with them. But only after a long time, not a short time; only when attentive, not when inattentive; and only by the wise, not the witless.

segs.p: ‘Saṁvohārena, bhikkhave, soceyyaṁ veditabbaṁ, tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti,
segs.e: ‘You can get to know a person’s purity by dealing with them. …’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ saṁvoharamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Take an individual who has dealings with someone else. They come to know:

segs.p: ‘aññathā kho ayamāyasmā ekena eko voharati, aññathā dvīhi, aññathā tīhi, aññathā sambahulehi;
segs.e: ‘This venerable deals with one person in one way. Then they deal with two, three, or many people each in different ways.
They’re not consistent from one deal to the next.
This venerable’s dealings are impure, not pure.’

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ saṁvoharamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Take another individual who has dealings with someone else. They come to know:

segs.p: ‘yatheva kho ayamāyasmā ekena eko voharati, tathā dvīhi, tathā tīhi, tathā sambahulehi.
segs.e: ‘This venerable deals with one person in one way. Then they deal with two, three, or many people each in the same way.
They’re consistent from one deal to the next.
This venerable’s dealings are pure, not impure.’

segs.p: ‘Saṁvohārena, bhikkhave, soceyyaṁ veditabbaṁ, tañca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti, iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s why I said that you can get to know a person’s purity by dealing with them. …

segs.p: ‘Āpadāsu, bhikkhave, thāmo veditabbo, so ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti,
segs.e: ‘You can get to know a person’s resilience in times of trouble. …’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno, bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno, rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno na iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Take someone who experiences loss of family, wealth, or health. But they don’t reflect:

segs.p: ‘tathābhūto kho ayaṁ lokasannivāso tathābhūto ayaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābho yathābhūte lokasannivāse yathābhūte attabhāvapaṭilābhe aṭṭha lokadhammā lokaṁ anuparivattanti loko ca aṭṭha lokadhamme anuparivattati—
segs.e: ‘Worldly life is like that. Incarnation is like that. That’s why the eight worldly conditions revolve around the world, and the world revolves around the eight worldly conditions:

segs.p: lābho ca, alābho ca, yaso ca, ayaso ca, nindā ca, pasaṁsā ca, sukhañca, dukkhañcā’ti.
segs.e: gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.’

segs.p: So ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno socati kilamati paridevati, urattāḷiṁ kandati, sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They sorrow and wail and lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Take someone else who experiences loss of family, wealth, or health. But they reflect:

segs.p: ‘tathābhūto kho ayaṁ lokasannivāso tathābhūto ayaṁ attabhāvapaṭilābho yathābhūte lokasannivāse yathābhūte attabhāvapaṭilābhe aṭṭha lokadhammā lokaṁ anuparivattanti loko ca aṭṭha lokadhamme anuparivattati—
segs.e: ‘Worldly life is like that. Incarnation is like that. That’s why the eight worldly conditions revolve around the world, and the world revolves around the eight worldly conditions:

segs.p: lābho ca, alābho ca, yaso ca, ayaso ca, nindā ca, pasaṁsā ca, sukhañca, dukkhañcā’ti.
segs.e: gain and loss, fame and disgrace, blame and praise, pleasure and pain.’

segs.p: So ñātibyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno bhogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno rogabyasanena vā phuṭṭho samāno na socati na kilamati na paridevati, na urattāḷiṁ kandati, na sammohaṁ āpajjati.
segs.e: They don’t sorrow or wail or lament, beating their breast and falling into confusion.

segs.p: ‘Āpadāsu, bhikkhave, thāmo veditabbo, so ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti,
segs.e: That’s why I said that you can get to know a person’s resilience in times of trouble. …

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
‘Sākacchāya, bhikkhave, paññā veditabbā, sā ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti,
segs.e: ‘You can get to know a person’s wisdom by discussion. But only after a long time, not casually; only when attentive, not when inattentive; and only by the wise, not the witless.’

segs.p: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
segs.e: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ sākacchāyamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Take an individual who is discussing with someone else. They come to know:

segs.p: ‘yathā kho imassa āyasmato ummaggo yathā ca abhinīhāro yathā ca pañhāsamudāhāro, duppañño ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā paññavā.
segs.e: ‘Judging by this venerable’s approach, by what they’re getting at, and by how they discuss a question, they’re witless, not wise.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathā hi ayamāyasmā na ceva gambhīraṁ atthapadaṁ udāharati santaṁ paṇītaṁ atakkāvacaraṁ nipuṇaṁ paṇḍitavedanīyaṁ.
segs.e: This venerable does not bring up a deep and meaningful saying that is peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, comprehensible to the astute.

segs.p: Yañca ayamāyasmā dhammaṁ bhāsati tassa ca nappaṭibalo saṅkhittena vā vitthārena vā atthaṁ ācikkhituṁ desetuṁ paññāpetuṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ vivarituṁ vibhajituṁ uttānīkātuṁ.
segs.e: When this venerable speaks on Dhamma they’re not able to explain the meaning, either briefly or in detail. They can’t teach it, assert it, establish it, clarify it, analyze it, or reveal it.
This venerable is witless, not wise.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, cakkhumā puriso udakarahadassa tīre ṭhito passeyya parittaṁ macchaṁ ummujjamānaṁ.
segs.e: Suppose a person with clear eyes was standing on the bank of a lake. They’d see a little fish rising,
and think:

segs.p: ‘yathā kho imassa macchassa ummaggo yathā ca ūmighāto yathā ca vegāyitattaṁ, paritto ayaṁ maccho, nāyaṁ maccho mahanto’ti.
segs.e: ‘Judging by this fish’s approach, by the ripples it makes, and by its force, it’s a little fish, not a big one.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ sākacchāyamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: In the same way, an individual who is discussing with someone else would come to know:

segs.p: ‘yathā kho imassa āyasmato ummaggo yathā ca abhinīhāro yathā ca pañhāsamudāhāro, duppañño ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā paññavā.
segs.e: ‘Judging by this venerable’s approach, by what they’re getting at, and by how they discuss a question, they’re witless, not wise. …’

segs.p: Tathā hi ayamāyasmā na ceva gambhīraṁ atthapadaṁ udāharati santaṁ paṇītaṁ atakkāvacaraṁ nipuṇaṁ paṇḍitavedanīyaṁ.
Yañca ayamāyasmā dhammaṁ bhāsati, tassa ca na paṭibalo saṅkhittena vā vitthārena vā atthaṁ ācikkhituṁ desetuṁ paññāpetuṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ vivarituṁ vibhajituṁ uttānīkātuṁ.
Idha pana, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ sākacchāyamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: Take another individual who is discussing with someone else. They come to know:

segs.p: ‘yathā kho imassa āyasmato ummaggo yathā ca abhinīhāro yathā ca pañhāsamudāhāro, paññavā ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā duppañño.
segs.e: ‘Judging by this venerable’s approach, by what they’re getting at, and by how they discuss a question, they’re wise, not witless.
Why is that?

segs.p: Tathā hi ayamāyasmā gambhīrañceva atthapadaṁ udāharati santaṁ paṇītaṁ atakkāvacaraṁ nipuṇaṁ paṇḍitavedanīyaṁ.
segs.e: This venerable brings up a deep and meaningful saying that is peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of logic, subtle, comprehensible to the astute.

segs.p: Yañca ayamāyasmā dhammaṁ bhāsati, tassa ca paṭibalo saṅkhittena vā vitthārena vā atthaṁ ācikkhituṁ desetuṁ paññāpetuṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ vivarituṁ vibhajituṁ uttānīkātuṁ.
segs.e: When this venerable speaks on Dhamma they’re able to explain the meaning, either briefly or in detail. They teach it, assert it, establish it, clarify it, analyze it, and reveal it.
This venerable is wise, not witless.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, cakkhumā puriso udakarahadassa tīre ṭhito passeyya mahantaṁ macchaṁ ummujjamānaṁ.
segs.e: Suppose a man with clear eyes was standing on the bank of a lake. He’d see a big fish rising,
and think:

segs.p: ‘yathā kho imassa macchassa ummaggo yathā ca ūmighāto yathā ca vegāyitattaṁ, mahanto ayaṁ maccho, nāyaṁ maccho paritto’ti.
segs.e: ‘Judging by this fish’s approach, by the ripples it makes, and by its force, it’s a big fish, not a little one.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, puggalo puggalena saddhiṁ sākacchāyamāno evaṁ jānāti:
segs.e: In the same way, an individual who is discussing with someone else would come to know:

segs.p: ‘yathā kho imassa āyasmato ummaggo yathā ca abhinīhāro yathā ca pañhāsamudāhāro, paññavā ayamāyasmā, nāyamāyasmā duppañño.
segs.e: ‘Judging by this venerable’s approach, by what they’re getting at, and by how they articulate a question, they’re wise, not witless. …’

segs.p: Tathā hi ayamāyasmā gambhīrañceva atthapadaṁ udāharati santaṁ paṇītaṁ atakkāvacaraṁ nipuṇaṁ paṇḍitavedanīyaṁ.
Yañca ayamāyasmā dhammaṁ bhāsati, tassa ca paṭibalo saṅkhittena vā vitthārena vā atthaṁ ācikkhituṁ desetuṁ paññāpetuṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ vivarituṁ vibhajituṁ uttānīkātuṁ.
‘Sākacchāya, bhikkhave, paññā veditabbā, sā ca kho dīghena addhunā, na ittaraṁ; manasikarotā, no amanasikarotā; paññavatā, no duppaññenā’ti, iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s why I said that you can get to know a person’s wisdom by discussion. But only after a long time, not casually; only when attentive, not when inattentive; and only by the wise, not the witless.

segs.p: Imāni kho, bhikkhave, cattāri ṭhānāni imehi catūhi ṭhānehi veditabbānī”ti.
segs.e: These are the four things that can be known in four situations.”
Numbered Discourses 4.193
20. The Great Chapter
With Bhaddiya

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho bhaddiyo licchavi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho bhaddiyo licchavi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Bhaddiya the Licchavi went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, I have heard this:

segs.p: ‘māyāvī samaṇo gotamo āvaṭṭaniṁ māyaṁ jānāti yāya aññatitthiyānaṁ sāvake āvaṭṭetī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The ascetic Gotama is deceitful. He knows a conversion trick, and uses it to convert the disciples of those of other religions.’

segs.p: ‘māyāvī samaṇo gotamo āvaṭṭaniṁ māyaṁ jānāti yāya aññatitthiyānaṁ sāvake āvaṭṭetī’ti, kacci te, bhante, bhagavato vuttavādino, na ca bhagavantaṁ abhūtena abbhācikkhanti, dhammassa ca anudhammaṁ byākaronti, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānupāto gārayhaṁ ṭhānaṁ āgacchati, anabbhakkhātukāmā hi mayaṁ, bhante, bhagavantan”ti?
segs.e: I trust those who say this repeat what the Buddha has said, and do not misrepresent him with an untruth? Is their explanation in line with the teaching? Are there any legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism?”

segs.p: “Etha tumhe, bhaddiya, mā anussavena, mā paramparāya, mā itikirāya, mā piṭakasampadānena, mā takkahetu, mā nayahetu, mā ākāraparivitakkena, mā diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā, mā bhabbarūpatāya, mā ‘samaṇo no garū’ti.
segs.e: “Please, Bhaddiya, don’t go by oral transmission, don’t go by lineage, don’t go by testament, don’t go by canonical authority, don’t rely on logic, don’t rely on inference, don’t go by reasoned train of thought, don’t go by the acceptance of a view after deliberation, don’t go by the appearance of competence, and don’t think ‘The ascetic is our respected teacher.’
But when you know for yourselves:

segs.p: ‘ime dhammā akusalā, ime dhammā sāvajjā, ime dhammā viññugarahitā, ime dhammā samattā samādinnā ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattantī’ti, atha tumhe, bhaddiya, pajaheyyātha.
segs.e: ‘These things are unskillful, blameworthy, criticized by sensible people, and when you undertake them, they lead to harm and suffering’, then you should give them up.
What do you think, Bhaddiya?

segs.p: lobho purisassa ajjhattaṁ uppajjamāno uppajjati hitāya vā ahitāya vā”ti?
segs.e: Does greed come up in a person for their welfare or harm?”
“Harm, sir.”

segs.p: “Luddho panāyaṁ, bhaddiya, purisapuggalo lobhena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto pāṇampi hanati, adinnampi ādiyati, paradārampi gacchati, musāpi bhaṇati, parampi tathattāya samādapeti yaṁsa hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāyā”ti.
segs.e: “A greedy individual, overcome by greed, kills living creatures, steals, commits adultery, lies, and encourages others to do the same. Is that for their lasting harm and suffering?”
“Yes, sir.”
“What do you think, Bhaddiya?

segs.p: doso purisassa …pe… moho purisassa …pe… sārambho purisassa ajjhattaṁ uppajjamāno uppajjati hitāya vā ahitāya vā”ti?
segs.e: Does hate … or delusion … or aggression come up in a person for their welfare or harm?”
“Harm, sir.”

segs.p: “Sāraddho panāyaṁ, bhaddiya, purisapuggalo sārambhena abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto pāṇampi hanati, adinnampi ādiyati, paradārampi gacchati, musāpi bhaṇati, parampi tathattāya samādapeti yaṁsa hoti dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāyā”ti.
segs.e: “An aggressive individual kills living creatures, steals, commits adultery, lies, and encourages others to do the same. Is that for their lasting harm and suffering?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhaddiya, ime dhammā kusalā vā akusalā vā”ti?
segs.e: “What do you think, Bhaddiya, are these things skillful or unskillful?”
“Unskillful, sir.”
“Blameworthy or blameless?”
“Blameworthy, sir.”
“Criticized or praised by sensible people?”
“Criticized by sensible people, sir.”

segs.p: “Samattā samādinnā ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti, no vā?
segs.e: “When you undertake them, do they lead to harm and suffering, or not?
Or how do you see this?”
“When you undertake them, they lead to harm and suffering.
That’s how we see it.”

segs.p: “Iti kho, bhaddiya, yaṁ taṁ te avocumhā—
segs.e: “So, Bhaddiya, when we said:

segs.p: etha tumhe, bhaddiya, mā anussavena, mā paramparāya, mā itikirāya, mā piṭakasampadānena, mā takkahetu, mā nayahetu, mā ākāraparivitakkena, mā diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā, mā bhabbarūpatāya, mā ‘samaṇo no garū’ti.
segs.e: ‘Please, Bhaddiya, don’t go by oral transmission, don’t go by lineage, don’t go by testament, don’t go by canonical authority, don’t rely on logic, don’t rely on inference, don’t go by reasoned train of thought, don’t go by the acceptance of a view after deliberation, don’t go by the appearance of competence, and don’t think “The ascetic is our respected teacher.”
But when you know for yourselves:

segs.p: ‘ime dhammā akusalā, ime dhammā sāvajjā, ime dhammā viññugarahitā, ime dhammā samattā samādinnā ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattantīti, atha tumhe, bhaddiya, pajaheyyāthā’ti,
segs.e: “These things are unskillful, blameworthy, criticized by sensible people, and when you undertake them, they lead to harm and suffering”, then you should give them up.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Etha tumhe, bhaddiya, mā anussavena, mā paramparāya, mā itikirāya, mā piṭakasampadānena, mā takkahetu, mā nayahetu, mā ākāraparivitakkena, mā diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā, mā bhabbarūpatāya, mā ‘samaṇo no garū’ti.
segs.e: Please, Bhaddiya, don’t rely on oral transmission …
But when you know for yourselves:

segs.p: ‘ime dhammā kusalā, ime dhammā anavajjā, ime dhammā viññuppasatthā, ime dhammā samattā samādinnā hitāya sukhāya saṁvattantī’ti, atha tumhe, bhaddiya, upasampajja vihareyyāthāti.
segs.e: ‘These things are skillful, blameless, praised by sensible people, and when you undertake them, they lead to welfare and happiness’, then you should acquire them and keep them.
What do you think, Bhaddiya?

segs.p: alobho purisassa ajjhattaṁ uppajjamāno uppajjati hitāya vā ahitāya vā”ti?
segs.e: Does contentment … love … understanding … benevolence come up in a person for their welfare or harm?”

segs.p: “Aluddho panāyaṁ, bhaddiya, purisapuggalo lobhena anabhibhūto apariyādinnacitto neva pāṇaṁ hanati, na adinnaṁ ādiyati, na paradāraṁ gacchati, na musā bhaṇati, parampi tathattāya na samādapeti yaṁsa hoti dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
“Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhaddiya, adoso purisassa …pe… amoho purisassa …pe… asārambho purisassa ajjhattaṁ uppajjamāno uppajjati hitāya vā ahitāya vā”ti?

segs.e: “Welfare, sir.”

segs.p: “Asāraddho panāyaṁ, bhaddiya, purisapuggalo sārambhena anabhibhūto apariyādinnacitto neva pāṇaṁ hanati, na adinnaṁ ādiyati, na paradāraṁ gacchati, na musā bhaṇati, parampi tathattāya na samādapeti yaṁsa hoti dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: “An individual who is benevolent—not overcome by aggression—doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit adultery, lie, or encourage others to do the same. Is that for their lasting welfare and happiness?”
“Yes, sir.”

segs.p: “Taṁ kiṁ maññatha, bhaddiya, ime dhammā kusalā vā akusalā vā”ti?
segs.e: “What do you think, Bhaddiya, are these things skillful or unskillful?”
“Skillful, sir.”
“Blameworthy or blameless?”
“Blameless, sir.”
“Criticized or praised by sensible people?”
“Praised by sensible people, sir.”

segs.p: “Samattā samādinnā hitāya sukhāya saṁvattanti no vā?
segs.e: “When you undertake them, do they lead to welfare and happiness, or not?
Or how do you see this?”
“When you undertake them, they lead to welfare and happiness.
That’s how we see it.”

segs.p: “Iti kho, bhaddiya, yaṁ taṁ te avocumhā—
segs.e: “So, Bhaddiya, when we said:

segs.p: etha tumhe, bhaddiya, mā anussavena, mā paramparāya, mā itikirāya, mā piṭakasampadānena, mā takkahetu, mā nayahetu, mā ākāraparivitakkena, mā diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā, mā bhabbarūpatāya, mā ‘samaṇo no garū’ti.
segs.e: ‘Please, Bhaddiya, don’t go by oral transmission, don’t go by lineage, don’t go by testament, don’t go by canonical authority, don’t rely on logic, don’t rely on inference, don’t go by reasoned train of thought, don’t go by the acceptance of a view after deliberation, don’t go by the appearance of competence, and don’t think “The ascetic is our respected teacher.”
But when you know for yourselves:

segs.p: ‘ime dhammā kusalā, ime dhammā anavajjā, ime dhammā viññuppasatthā, ime dhammā samattā samādinnā hitāya sukhāya saṁvattantīti, atha tumhe, bhaddiya, upasampajja vihareyyāthā’ti,
segs.e: “These things are skillful, blameless, praised by sensible people, and when you undertake them, they lead to welfare and happiness”, then you should acquire them and keep them.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.

segs.p: Ye kho te, bhaddiya, loke santo sappurisā te sāvakaṁ evaṁ samādapenti:
segs.e: The good and true persons in the world encourage their disciples:

segs.p: ‘ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, lobhaṁ vineyya viharāhi.
segs.e: ‘Please, my man, live rid of greed.

segs.p: Lobhaṁ vineyya viharanto na lobhajaṁ kammaṁ karissasi kāyena vācāya manasā.
segs.e: Then you won’t act out of greed by way of body, speech, or mind.
Live rid of hate … delusion … aggression.

segs.p: Dosaṁ vineyya viharanto na dosajaṁ kammaṁ karissasi kāyena vācāya manasā.
segs.e: Then you won’t act out of hate … delusion … aggression by way of body, speech, or mind.”

segs.p: Mohaṁ vineyya viharanto na mohajaṁ kammaṁ karissasi kāyena vācāya manasā.
Sārambhaṁ vineyya viharanto na sārambhajaṁ kammaṁ karissasi kāyena vācāya manasā’”ti.
Evaṁ vutte, bhaddiyo licchavi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Bhaddiya the Licchavi said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: “Excellent, sir! … From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
“Well, Bhaddiya, did I say to you:
‘Please, Bhaddiya, be my disciple,
and I will be your teacher’?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁvādiṁ kho maṁ, bhaddiya, evamakkhāyiṁ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhanti:
segs.e: “Though I state and assert this, certain ascetics and brahmins misrepresent me with the incorrect, hollow, false, untruthful claim:

segs.p: ‘māyāvī samaṇo gotamo āvaṭṭaniṁ māyaṁ jānāti yāya aññatitthiyānaṁ sāvake āvaṭṭetī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘The ascetic Gotama is deceitful. He knows a conversion trick, and uses it to convert the disciples of those of other religions.’”
“Sir, this conversion trick is excellent.
This conversion trick is lovely!

segs.p: Piyā me, bhante, ñātisālohitā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṁ, piyānampi me assa ñātisālohitānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: If my loved ones—relatives and kin—were to be converted by this, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Sabbe cepi, bhante, khattiyā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṁ, sabbesampissa khattiyānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: If all the aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials were to be converted by this, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.”

segs.p: Sabbe cepi, bhante, brāhmaṇā … vessā … suddā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṁ, sabbesampissa suddānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.

segs.e: “That’s so true, Bhaddiya! That’s so true, Bhaddiya!

segs.p: Sabbe cepi, bhaddiya, khattiyā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṁ akusaladhammappahānāya kusaladhammūpasampadāya, sabbesampissa khattiyānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: If all the aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials were to be converted by this, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Sabbe cepi, bhaddiya, brāhmaṇā … vessā … suddā āvaṭṭeyyuṁ akusaladhammappahānāya kusaladhammūpasampadāya, sabbesampissa suddānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.

Sadevako cepi, bhaddiya, loko samārako sabrahmako sassamaṇabrāhmaṇī pajā sadevamanussā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṁ akusaladhammappahānāya kusaladhammūpasampadāya, sadevakassapissa lokassa samārakassa sabrahmakassa sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya.
segs.e: If the whole world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—were to be converted by this, for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness.

segs.p: Ime cepi, bhaddiya, mahāsālā imāya āvaṭṭaniyā āvaṭṭeyyuṁ akusaladhammappahānāya kusaladhammūpasampadāya, imesampissa mahāsālānaṁ dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya (…).
segs.e: If these great sal trees were to be converted by this, for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities, it would be for their lasting welfare and happiness—if they were sentient.
How much more then a human being!”
Numbered Discourses 4.194
20. The Great Chapter
At Sāpūga

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ānando koliyesu viharati sāmugaṁ nāma koliyānaṁ nigamo.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Ānanda was staying in the land of the Koliyans, where they have a town named Sāpūga.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā sāmugiyā koliyaputtā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinne kho te sāmugiye koliyaputte āyasmā ānando etadavoca:
segs.e: Then several Koliyans from Sāpūga went up to Ānanda, bowed, and sat down to one side. Then Venerable Ānanda said to them:

segs.p: “Cattārimāni, byagghapajjā, pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgāni tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātāni sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāya.
segs.e: “Byagghapajjas, these four factors of trying to be pure have been rightly explained by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.
What four?
The factors of trying to be pure in ethics, mind, view, and freedom.
And what is the factor of trying to be pure in ethics?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajjā, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.
This is called purity of ethics.

segs.p: Iti evarūpiṁ sīlapārisuddhiṁ aparipūraṁ vā paripūressāmi paripūraṁ vā tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmīti, yo tattha chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca, idaṁ vuccati, byagghapajjā, sīlapārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ.
segs.e: They think: ‘I will fulfill such purity of ethics, or, if it’s already fulfilled, I’ll support it in every situation by wisdom.’ Their enthusiasm for that—their effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness—is called the factor of trying to be pure in ethics.
And what is the factor of trying to be pure in mind?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajjā, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.
This is called purity of mind.

segs.p: Iti evarūpiṁ cittapārisuddhiṁ aparipūraṁ vā paripūressāmi paripūraṁ vā tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmīti, yo tattha chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca, idaṁ vuccati, byagghapajjā, cittapārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ.
segs.e: They think: ‘I will fulfill such purity of mind, or, if it’s already fulfilled, I’ll support it in every situation by wisdom.’ Their enthusiasm for that—their effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness—is called the factor of trying to be pure in mind.
And what is the factor of trying to be pure in view?

segs.p: Idha, byagghapajjā, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: Take a mendicant who truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.
This is called purity of view.

segs.p: Iti evarūpiṁ diṭṭhipārisuddhiṁ aparipūraṁ vā …pe… tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmīti, yo tattha chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca, idaṁ vuccati, byagghapajjā, diṭṭhipārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ.
segs.e: They think: ‘I will fulfill such purity of view, or, if it’s already fulfilled, I’ll support it in every situation by wisdom.’ Their enthusiasm for that—their effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness—is called the factor of trying to be pure in view.
And what is the factor of trying to be pure in freedom?

segs.p: Sa kho so, byagghapajjā, ariyasāvako iminā ca sīlapārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgena samannāgato iminā ca cittapārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgena samannāgato iminā ca diṭṭhipārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgena samannāgato rajanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ virājeti, vimocanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ vimoceti.
segs.e: That noble disciple—who has these factors of trying to be pure in ethics, mind, and view—detaches their mind from things that arouse greed, and frees their mind from things that it should be freed from.

segs.p: So rajanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ virājetvā, vimocanīyesu dhammesu cittaṁ vimocetvā sammāvimuttiṁ phusati.
segs.e: Doing so, they experience perfect freedom.
This is called purity of freedom.

segs.p: Iti evarūpiṁ vimuttipārisuddhiṁ aparipūraṁ vā paripūressāmi paripūraṁ vā tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmīti, yo tattha chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca, idaṁ vuccati, byagghapajjā, vimuttipārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgaṁ.
segs.e: They think: ‘I will fulfill such purity of freedom, or, if it’s already fulfilled, I’ll support it in every situation by wisdom.’ Their enthusiasm for that—their effort, zeal, vigor, perseverance, mindfulness, and situational awareness—is called the factor of trying to be pure in freedom.

segs.p: Imāni kho, byagghapajjā, cattāri pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgāni tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sammadakkhātāni sattānaṁ visuddhiyā sokaparidevānaṁ samatikkamāya dukkhadomanassānaṁ atthaṅgamāya ñāyassa adhigamāya nibbānassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
segs.e: These four factors of trying to be pure have been rightly explained by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha. They are in order to purify sentient beings, to get past sorrow and crying, to make an end of pain and sadness, to discover the system, and to realize extinguishment.”
Numbered Discourses 4.195
20. The Great Chapter
With Vappa

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho vappo sakko nigaṇṭhasāvako yenāyasmā mahāmoggallāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho vappaṁ sakkaṁ nigaṇṭhasāvakaṁ āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Vappa of the Sakyans, a disciple of the Jains, went up to Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, bowed, and sat down to one side. Mahāmoggallāna said to him:

segs.p: “Idhassa, vappa, kāyena saṁvuto vācāya saṁvuto manasā saṁvuto avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā.
segs.e: “Vappa, take an individual who, due to the fading away of ignorance and the arising of knowledge, is restrained in body, speech, and mind.

segs.p: Passasi no tvaṁ, vappa, taṁ ṭhānaṁ yatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan”ti?
segs.e: Do you see any reason why defilements giving rise to painful feelings would defile that person in the next life?”
“Sir, I do see such a case.

segs.p: Idhassa, bhante, pubbe pāpakammaṁ kataṁ avipakkavipākaṁ.
segs.e: Take someone who did bad deeds in a past life. But the result of that has not yet ripened.

segs.p: Tatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan”ti.
segs.e: For this reason defilements giving rise to painful feelings would defile that person in the next life.”

segs.p: Ayañceva kho pana āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa vappena sakkena nigaṇṭhasāvakena saddhiṁ antarākathā vippakatā hoti.
segs.e: But this conversation between Mahāmoggallāna and Vappa was left unfinished.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ mahāmoggallānaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to the assembly hall. He sat down on the seat spread out, and said to Mahāmoggallāna,

segs.p: “Kāya nuttha, moggallāna, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā; kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti?
segs.e: “Moggallāna, what were you sitting talking about just now? What conversation was left unfinished?”
Moggallāna repeated the entire conversation to the Buddha, and concluded:

segs.p: ‘idhassa, vappa, kāyena saṁvuto vācāya saṁvuto manasā saṁvuto avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā.
Passasi no tvaṁ, vappa, taṁ ṭhānaṁ yatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan’ti?
Evaṁ vutte, bhante, vappo sakko nigaṇṭhasāvako maṁ etadavoca:
Idhassa, bhante, pubbe pāpakammaṁ kataṁ avipakkavipākaṁ.
Tatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan’ti.
Ayaṁ kho no, bhante, vappena sakkena nigaṇṭhasāvakena saddhiṁ antarākathā vippakatā; atha bhagavā anuppatto”ti.
segs.e: “This was my conversation with Vappa that was unfinished when the Buddha arrived.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā vappaṁ sakkaṁ nigaṇṭhasāvakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha said to Vappa,

segs.p: “sace me tvaṁ, vappa, anuññeyyañceva anujāneyyāsi, paṭikkositabbañca paṭikkoseyyāsi, yassa ca me bhāsitassa atthaṁ na jāneyyāsi mamevettha uttari paṭipuccheyyāsi:
segs.e: “Vappa, we can discuss this. But only if you grant what should be granted, and reject what should be rejected. And if you ask me the meaning of anything you don’t understand, saying:

segs.p: ‘idaṁ, bhante, kathaṁ, imassa ko attho’ti, siyā no ettha kathāsallāpo”ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, why is this? What’s the meaning of that?’”

segs.p: “Anuññeyyañcevāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavato anujānissāmi, paṭikkositabbañca paṭikkosissāmi, yassa cāhaṁ bhagavato bhāsitassa atthaṁ na jānissāmi bhagavantaṁyevettha uttari paṭipucchissāmi:
segs.e: “Sir, let us discuss this. I will do as you say.”
“What do you think, Vappa?

segs.p: ye kāyasamārambhapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, kāyasamārambhā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: There are distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of instigating bodily activity. These don’t occur in someone who refrains from such bodily activity.

segs.p: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti, sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little. This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Passasi no tvaṁ, vappa, taṁ ṭhānaṁ yatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan”ti?
segs.e: Do you see any reason why defilements giving rise to painful feelings would defile that person in the next life?”
“No, sir.”
“What do you think, Vappa?

segs.p: ye vacīsamārambhapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, vacīsamārambhā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: There are distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of instigating verbal activity. These don’t occur in someone who refrains from such verbal activity.

segs.p: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti.
segs.e: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Passasi no tvaṁ, vappa, taṁ ṭhānaṁ yatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan”ti?
segs.e: Do you see any reason why defilements giving rise to painful feelings would defile that person in the next life?”
“No, sir.”
“What do you think, Vappa?

segs.p: ye manosamārambhapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, manosamārambhā paṭiviratassa evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: There are distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of instigating mental activity. These don’t occur in someone who refrains from such mental activity.

segs.p: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti.
segs.e: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Passasi no tvaṁ, vappa, taṁ ṭhānaṁ yatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan”ti?
segs.e: Do you see any reason why defilements giving rise to painful feelings would defile that person in the next life?”
“No, sir.”
“What do you think, Vappa?

segs.p: ye avijjāpaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, avijjāvirāgā vijjuppādā evaṁsa te āsavā vighātapariḷāhā na honti.
segs.e: There are distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of ignorance. These don’t occur when ignorance fades away and knowledge arises.

segs.p: So navañca kammaṁ na karoti, purāṇañca kammaṁ phussa phussa byantīkaroti.
segs.e: They don’t perform any new deeds, and old deeds are eliminated by experiencing their results little by little.

segs.p: Sandiṭṭhikā nijjarā akālikā ehipassikā opaneyyikā paccattaṁ veditabbā viññūhi.
segs.e: This wearing away is apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.

segs.p: Passasi no tvaṁ, vappa, taṁ ṭhānaṁ yatonidānaṁ purisaṁ dukkhavedaniyā āsavā assaveyyuṁ abhisamparāyan”ti?
segs.e: Do you see any reason why defilements giving rise to painful feelings would defile that person in the next life?”
“No, sir.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ sammā vimuttacittassa kho, vappa, bhikkhuno cha satatavihārā adhigatā honti.
segs.e: “A mendicant whose mind is rightly freed like this has achieved six consistent responses.

segs.p: So cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano; upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
segs.e: Seeing a sight with their eyes, they’re neither happy nor sad, but remain equanimous, mindful and aware.
Hearing a sound with their ears …
Smelling an odor with their nose …
Tasting a flavor with their tongue …
Encountering a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano; upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
segs.e: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad, but remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

segs.p: So kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyamāno ‘kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyāmī’ti pajānāti; jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyamāno ‘jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyāmī’ti pajānāti;
segs.e: Feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

segs.p: ‘kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītī bhavissantī’ti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life has come to an end, everything that’s felt, being no longer relished, will become cool right here.’

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, vappa, thūṇaṁ paṭicca chāyā paññāyati.
segs.e: Suppose there was a shadow cast by a post.
Then along comes a person with a spade and basket.
They cut down the post at its base,
dig it up,
and pull it out by its roots, right down to the fibers and stems.
Then they split it apart,
cut up the parts,
and chop them into splinters.
Next they dry the splinters in the wind and sun,
burn them with fire,
and reduce them to ashes.

segs.p: Masiṁ karitvā mahāvāte vā ophuṇeyya nadiyā vā sīghasotāya pavāheyya.
segs.e: Then they whisk away the ashes in a strong wind, or glide them down a swift stream.

segs.p: Evaṁ hissa, vappa, yā thūṇaṁ paṭicca chāyā sā ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā.
segs.e: And so the shadow cast by the post is cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, vappa, evaṁ sammā vimuttacittassa bhikkhuno cha satatavihārā adhigatā honti.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant whose mind is rightly freed like this has achieved six consistent responses.

segs.p: So cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano; upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
segs.e: Seeing a sight with their eyes, they’re neither happy nor sad, but remain equanimous, mindful and aware.
Hearing a sound with their ears …
Smelling an odor with their nose …
Tasting a flavor with their tongue …
Encountering a touch with their body …

segs.p: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano; upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno.
segs.e: Knowing an idea with their mind, they’re neither happy nor sad, but remain equanimous, mindful and aware.

segs.p: So kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyamāno ‘kāyapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyāmī’ti pajānāti; jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyamāno ‘jīvitapariyantikaṁ vedanaṁ vediyāmī’ti pajānāti;
segs.e: Feeling the end of the body draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of the body draw close.’ Feeling the end of life draw close, they understand: ‘I feel the end of life draw close.’

segs.p: ‘kāyassa bhedā uddhaṁ jīvitapariyādānā idheva sabbavedayitāni anabhinanditāni sītī bhavissantī’ti pajānāti”.
segs.e: They understand: ‘When my body breaks up and my life has come to an end, everything that’s felt, being no longer relished, will become cool right here.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, vappo sakko nigaṇṭhasāvako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he said this, Vappa the Sakyan, the disciple of the Jains, said to the Buddha:
“Sir, suppose there was a man who raised commercial horses for profit.

segs.p: So udayañceva nādhigaccheyya, uttariñca kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assa.
segs.e: But he never made any profit, and instead just got weary and frustrated.

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho ahaṁ, bhante, udayatthiko bāle nigaṇṭhe payirupāsiṁ.
segs.e: In the same way, I paid homage to those Jain fools for profit.

segs.p: Svāhaṁ udayañceva nādhigacchiṁ, uttariñca kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī ahosiṁ.
segs.e: But I never made any profit, and instead just got weary and frustrated.

segs.p: Esāhaṁ, bhante, ajjatagge yo me bālesu nigaṇṭhesu pasādo taṁ mahāvāte vā ophuṇāmi nadiyā vā sīghasotāya pavāhemi.
segs.e: From this day forth, any confidence I had in those Jain fools I whisk away as in a strong wind, or glide away as down a swift stream.

segs.p: Abhikkantaṁ, bhante …pe… upāsakaṁ maṁ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṁ saraṇaṁ gatan”ti.
segs.e: Excellent, sir! … From this day forth, may the Buddha remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
Numbered Discourses 4.196
20. The Great Chapter
With Sāḷha

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho sāḷho ca licchavi abhayo ca licchavi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho sāḷho licchavi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sāḷha and Abhaya the Licchavis went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Santi, bhante, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā dvayena oghassa nittharaṇaṁ paññapenti—
segs.e: “There are, sir, some ascetics and brahmins who advocate crossing the flood by means of two things:
purification of ethics, and mortification in disgust of sin.
What does the Buddha say about this?”

segs.p: “Sīlavisuddhiṁ kho ahaṁ, sāḷha, aññataraṁ sāmaññaṅganti vadāmi.
segs.e: “Sāḷha, purification of ethics is one of the factors of the ascetic life, I say.

segs.p: Ye te, sāḷha, samaṇabrāhmaṇā tapojigucchāvādā tapojigucchāsārā tapojigucchāallīnā viharanti, abhabbā te oghassa nittharaṇāya.
segs.e: But those ascetics and brahmins who teach fervent mortification in disgust of sin—regarding it as essential and sticking to it—are incapable of crossing the flood.

segs.p: Yepi te, sāḷha, samaṇabrāhmaṇā aparisuddhakāyasamācārā aparisuddhavacīsamācārā aparisuddhamanosamācārā aparisuddhājīvā, abhabbā te ñāṇadassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.
segs.e: And those ascetics and brahmins whose livelihood and behavior by way of body, speech, and mind, is not pure are also incapable of knowing and seeing, of supreme awakening.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, sāḷha, puriso nadiṁ taritukāmo tiṇhaṁ kuṭhāriṁ ādāya vanaṁ paviseyya.
segs.e: Suppose a man who wanted to cross a river took a sharp axe into a wood.

segs.p: So tattha passeyya mahatiṁ sālalaṭṭhiṁ ujuṁ navaṁ akukkuccakajātaṁ.
segs.e: There he’d see a large green sal tree, straight and young and grown unskewed.
He’d cut it down at the base,
cut off the top,
and completely strip off the branches and foliage.
Then he’d trim it with axes and
machetes,
plane it,
and sand it with a rock.
Finally, he’d launch out on the river.
What do you think, Sāḷha?

segs.p: bhabbo nu kho so puriso nadiṁ taritun”ti?
segs.e: Is that man capable of crossing the river?”
“No, sir.
Why not?

segs.p: “Asu hi, bhante, sālalaṭṭhi bahiddhā suparikammakatā anto avisuddhā.
segs.e: Because that green sal tree is well worked on the outside, but inside it’s still not cleared out.

segs.p: Tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—sālalaṭṭhi saṁsīdissati, puriso anayabyasanaṁ āpajjissatī”ti.
segs.e: I’d expect that green sal tree to sink, and the man to come to ruin.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho, sāḷha, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā tapojigucchāvādā tapojigucchāsārā tapojigucchāallīnā viharanti, abhabbā te oghassa nittharaṇāya.
segs.e: “In the same way, Sāḷha, those ascetics and brahmins who teach fervent mortification in disgust of sin—regarding it as essential and sticking to it—are incapable of crossing the flood.

segs.p: Yepi te, sāḷha, samaṇabrāhmaṇā aparisuddhakāyasamācārā aparisuddhavacīsamācārā aparisuddhamanosamācārā aparisuddhājīvā, abhabbā te ñāṇadassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.
segs.e: And those ascetics and brahmins whose livelihood and behavior by way of body, speech, and mind is not pure are also incapable of knowing and seeing, of supreme awakening.

segs.p: Ye ca kho te, sāḷha, samaṇabrāhmaṇā na tapojigucchāvādā na tapojigucchāsārā na tapojigucchāallīnā viharanti, bhabbā te oghassa nittharaṇāya.
segs.e: But those ascetics and brahmins who don’t teach mortification in disgust of sin—not regarding it as essential or sticking to it—are capable of crossing the flood.

segs.p: Yepi te, sāḷha, samaṇabrāhmaṇā parisuddhakāyasamācārā parisuddhavacīsamācārā parisuddhamanosamācārā parisuddhājīvā, bhabbā te ñāṇadassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.
segs.e: And those ascetics and brahmins whose behavior by way of body, speech, and mind is pure are also capable of knowing and seeing, of supreme awakening.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, sāḷha, puriso nadiṁ taritukāmo tiṇhaṁ kuṭhāriṁ ādāya vanaṁ paviseyya.
segs.e: Suppose a man who wanted to cross a river took a sharp axe into a wood.

segs.p: So tattha passeyya mahatiṁ sālalaṭṭhiṁ ujuṁ navaṁ akukkuccakajātaṁ.
segs.e: There he’d see a large green sal tree, straight and young and grown unskewed.
He’d cut it down at the base,
cut off the top,
and completely strip off the branches and foliage.
Then he’d trim it with axes and
machetes.

segs.p: vāsīhi tacchetvā nikhādanaṁ ādāya anto suvisodhitaṁ visodheyya;
segs.e: Then he’d take a chisel and completely clear it out inside.
Then he’d plane it,
sand it with a rock,
and make it into a boat.
Finally he’d fix it with oars and rudder,
and launch out on the river.
What do you think, Sāḷha?

segs.p: bhabbo nu kho so puriso nadiṁ taritun”ti?
segs.e: Is that man capable of crossing the river?”
“Yes, sir.
Why is that?

segs.p: “Asu hi, bhante, sālalaṭṭhi bahiddhā suparikammakatā, anto suvisuddhā nāvākatā phiyārittabaddhā.
segs.e: Because that green sal tree is well worked on the outside, cleared out on the inside, made into a boat, and fixed with oars and rudder.
I’d expect

segs.p: ‘nāvā na saṁsīdissati, puriso sotthinā pāraṁ gamissatī’”ti.
segs.e: that boat to not sink, and the man to safely make it to the far shore.”

segs.p: “Evamevaṁ kho, sāḷha, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā na tapojigucchāvādā na tapojigucchāsārā na tapojigucchāallīnā viharanti, bhabbā te oghassa nittharaṇāya.
segs.e: “In the same way, Sāḷha, those ascetics and brahmins who don’t teach fervent mortification in disgust of sin—not regarding it as essential or sticking to it—are capable of crossing the flood.

segs.p: Yepi te, sāḷha, samaṇabrāhmaṇā parisuddhakāyasamācārā parisuddhavacīsamācārā parisuddhamanosamācārā parisuddhājīvā, bhabbā te ñāṇadassanāya anuttarāya sambodhāya.
segs.e: And those ascetics and brahmins whose behavior by way of body, speech, and mind is pure are also capable of knowing and seeing, of supreme awakening.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, sāḷha, yodhājīvo bahūni cepi kaṇḍacitrakāni jānāti;
segs.e: Suppose there was a warrior who knew lots of fancy archery tricks.

segs.p: atha kho so tīhi ṭhānehi rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: It is only with these three factors that he becomes worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and is reckoned a factor of kingship.
What three?

segs.p: Dūrepātī ca, akkhaṇavedhī ca, mahato ca kāyassa padāletā.
segs.e: He’s a long-distance shooter, a marksman, and one who shatters large objects.
Just as a warrior is a long-distance shooter,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, sāḷha, ariyasāvako sammāsamādhi hoti.
segs.e: a noble disciple has right immersion.

segs.p: Sammāsamādhi, sāḷha, ariyasāvako yaṁ kiñci rūpaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā sabbaṁ rūpaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: A noble disciple with right immersion truly sees any kind of form at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all form—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
They truly see any kind of feeling …
perception …
choices …

segs.p: yaṁ kiñci viññāṇaṁ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṁ ajjhattaṁ vā bahiddhā vā oḷārikaṁ vā sukhumaṁ vā hīnaṁ vā paṇītaṁ vā yaṁ dūre santike vā, sabbaṁ viññāṇaṁ ‘netaṁ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti evametaṁ yathābhūtaṁ sammappaññāya passati.
segs.e: consciousness at all—past, future, or present; internal or external; solid or subtle; inferior or superior; far or near: all consciousness—with right understanding: ‘This is not mine, I am not this, this is not my self.’
Just as a warrior is a marksman,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, sāḷha, ariyasāvako sammādiṭṭhi hoti.
segs.e: a noble disciple has right view.

segs.p: Sammādiṭṭhi, sāḷha, ariyasāvako ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: A noble disciple with right view truly understands: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, sāḷha, yodhājīvo mahato kāyassa padāletā;
segs.e: Just as a warrior shatters large objects,

segs.p: evamevaṁ kho, sāḷha, ariyasāvako sammāvimutti hoti.
segs.e: a noble disciple has right freedom.

segs.p: Sammāvimutti, sāḷha, ariyasāvako mahantaṁ avijjākkhandhaṁ padāletī”ti.
segs.e: A noble disciple with right freedom shatters the great mass of ignorance.”
Numbered Discourses 4.197
20. The Great Chapter
Queen Mallikā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho mallikā devī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho mallikā devī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Queen Mallikā went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekacco mātugāmo dubbaṇṇā ca hoti durūpā supāpikā dassanāya;
segs.e: “What is the cause, sir, what is the reason why in this life some ladies are ugly, unattractive, and bad-looking;

segs.p: daliddā ca hoti appassakā appabhogā appesakkhā ca?
segs.e: and poor, with few assets and possessions; and insignificant?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekacco mātugāmo dubbaṇṇā ca hoti durūpā supāpikā dassanāya;
segs.e: And why are some ladies ugly, unattractive, and bad-looking;

segs.p: aḍḍhā ca hoti mahaddhanā mahābhogā mahesakkhā ca?
segs.e: but rich, affluent, wealthy, and illustrious?

segs.p: Ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekacco mātugāmo abhirūpā ca hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā;
segs.e: And why are some ladies attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty;

segs.p: daliddā ca hoti appassakā appabhogā appesakkhā ca?
segs.e: but poor, with few assets and possessions; and insignificant?

segs.p: Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena midhekacco mātugāmo abhirūpā ca hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā, aḍḍhā ca hoti mahaddhanā mahābhogā mahesakkhā cā”ti?
segs.e: And why are some ladies attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty; and rich, affluent, wealthy, and illustrious?”

segs.p: “Idha, mallike, ekacco mātugāmo kodhanā hoti upāyāsabahulā.
segs.e: “Take a lady who is irritable and bad-tempered.

segs.p: Appampi vuttā samānā abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
segs.e: Even when criticized a little bit she loses her temper, becoming annoyed, hostile, and hard-hearted, and displaying annoyance, hate, and bitterness.

segs.p: Sā na dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: She doesn’t give to ascetics or brahmins such things as food, drink, clothing, vehicles; garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and bed, house, and lighting.
And she’s jealous,
envying, resenting, and begrudging the possessions, honor, respect, reverence, homage, and veneration given to others.

segs.p: Sā ce tato cutā itthattaṁ āgacchati, sā yattha yattha paccājāyati dubbaṇṇā ca hoti durūpā supāpikā dassanāya;
segs.e: If she comes back to this place after passing away, wherever she is reborn she’s ugly, unattractive, and bad-looking;

segs.p: daliddā ca hoti appassakā appabhogā appesakkhā ca.
segs.e: and poor, with few assets and possessions; and insignificant.

segs.p: Idha pana, mallike, ekacco mātugāmo kodhanā hoti upāyāsabahulā.
segs.e: Take another lady who is irritable and bad-tempered. …

segs.p: Appampi vuttā samānā abhisajjati kuppati byāpajjati patitthīyati, kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
Sā dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: But she does give to ascetics or brahmins …
And she’s not jealous …

segs.p: paralābhasakkāragarukāramānanavandanapūjanāsu na issati na upadussati na issaṁ bandhati.
Sā ce tato cutā itthattaṁ āgacchati, sā yattha yattha paccājāyati dubbaṇṇā ca hoti durūpā supāpikā dassanāya;
segs.e: If she comes back to this place after passing away, wherever she is reborn she’s ugly, unattractive, and bad-looking;

segs.p: aḍḍhā ca hoti mahaddhanā mahābhogā mahesakkhā ca.
segs.e: but rich, affluent, wealthy, and illustrious.

segs.p: Idha pana, mallike, ekacco mātugāmo akkodhanā hoti anupāyāsabahulā.
segs.e: Take another lady who isn’t irritable and bad-tempered. …

segs.p: Bahumpi vuttā samānā nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patitthīyati, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
Sā na dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṁ pānaṁ vatthaṁ yānaṁ mālāgandhavilepanaṁ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṁ.
segs.e: But she doesn’t give to ascetics or brahmins …
And she’s jealous …

segs.p: Sā ce tato cutā itthattaṁ āgacchati, sā yattha yattha paccājāyati abhirūpā ca hoti dassanīyā pāsādikā paramāya vaṇṇapokkharatāya samannāgatā;
segs.e: If she comes back to this place after passing away, wherever she is reborn she’s attractive, good-looking, lovely, of surpassing beauty;

segs.p: daliddā ca hoti appassakā appabhogā appesakkhā ca.
segs.e: but poor, with few assets and possessions; and insignificant.

segs.p: Idha pana, mallike, ekacco mātugāmo akkodhanā hoti anupāyāsabahulā.
segs.e: Take another lady who isn’t irritable and bad-tempered. …

segs.p: Bahumpi vuttā samānā nābhisajjati na kuppati na byāpajjati na patitthīyati, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātukaroti.
