24. Deeds
Blameworthy

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Sāvajjena kāyakammena, sāvajjena vacīkammena, sāvajjena manokammena, sāvajjāya diṭṭhiyā—
segs.e: Blameworthy deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameworthy view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Anavajjena kāyakammena, anavajjena vacīkammena, anavajjena manokammena, anavajjāya diṭṭhiyā—
segs.e: Blameless deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameless view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.240
24. Deeds
Pleasing

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Sabyābajjhena kāyakammena, sabyābajjhena vacīkammena, sabyābajjhena manokammena, sabyābajjhāya diṭṭhiyā—
segs.e: Hurtful deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and hurtful view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Abyābajjhena kāyakammena, abyābajjhena vacīkammena, abyābajjhena manokammena, abyābajjhāya diṭṭhiyā—
segs.e: Pleasing deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and pleasing view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.241
24. Deeds
Ascetics

segs.p: “‘Idheva, bhikkhave, paṭhamo samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo;
segs.e: “‘Only here is there a first ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, and here a fourth ascetic.
Other sects are empty of ascetics.’
This, mendicants, is how you should rightly roar your lion’s roar.
And who is the first ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who—with the ending of three fetters—is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
This is the first ascetic.
And who is the second ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṁ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṁ lokaṁ āgantvā dukkhassantaṁ karoti.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who—with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion—is a once-returner. They come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.
This is the second ascetic.
And who is the third ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who—with the ending of the five lower fetters—is reborn spontaneously. They’re extinguished there, and are not liable to return from that world.
This is the third ascetic.
And who is the fourth ascetic?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s a mendicant who realizes the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.
This is the fourth ascetic.

segs.p: ‘Idheva, bhikkhave, paṭhamo samaṇo, idha dutiyo samaṇo, idha tatiyo samaṇo, idha catuttho samaṇo;
segs.e: ‘Only here is there a first ascetic, here a second ascetic, here a third ascetic, and here a fourth ascetic.
Other sects are empty of ascetics.’
This, mendicants, is how you should rightly roar your lion’s roar.”
Numbered Discourses 4.242
24. Deeds
Benefits of Relying on a True Person
“Mendicants, you can expect four benefits from relying on a true person.
What four?

segs.p: Ariyena sīlena vaḍḍhati, ariyena samādhinā vaḍḍhati, ariyāya paññāya vaḍḍhati, ariyāya vimuttiyā vaḍḍhati—
segs.e: Growth in noble ethics, immersion, wisdom, and freedom.

segs.p: sappurisaṁ, bhikkhave, nissāya ime cattāro ānisaṁsā pāṭikaṅkhā”ti.
segs.e: You can expect these four benefits from relying on a true person.”
Numbered Discourses 4.243
25. Perils of Offenses
Schism in the Saṅgha

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,
“Well, Ānanda, has that disciplinary issue been settled yet?”
“How could it be, sir?

segs.p: Āyasmato, bhante, anuruddhassa bāhiyo nāma saddhivihāriko kevalakappaṁ saṅghabhedāya ṭhito.
segs.e: Venerable Anuruddha’s protégé Bāhiya remains entirely committed to creating a schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Tatrāyasmā anuruddho na ekavācikampi bhaṇitabbaṁ maññatī”ti.
segs.e: But Anuruddha doesn’t think to say a single word about it.”
“But Ānanda, since when has Anuruddha been involved in disciplinary issues in the midst of the Saṅgha?

segs.p: Nanu, ānanda, yāni kānici adhikaraṇāni uppajjanti, sabbāni tāni tumhe ceva vūpasametha sāriputtamoggallānā ca.
segs.e: Shouldn’t you, together with Sāriputta and Moggallāna, settle all disciplinary issues that come up?

segs.p: Cattārome, ānanda, atthavase sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
segs.e: A bad monk sees four reasons to relish schism in the Saṅgha.
What four?

segs.p: Idhānanda, pāpabhikkhu dussīlo hoti pāpadhammo asuci saṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujāto.
segs.e: Take an unethical monk, of bad qualities, filthy, with suspicious behavior, underhand, no true ascetic or spiritual practitioner—though claiming to be one—rotten inside, festering, and depraved.
He thinks:
‘Suppose the monks know that I’m a bad monk …

segs.p: dussīlo pāpadhammo asuci saṅkassarasamācāro paṭicchannakammanto assamaṇo samaṇapaṭiñño abrahmacārī brahmacāripaṭiñño antopūti avassuto kasambujātoti, samaggā maṁ santā nāsessanti;
segs.e: If they’re in harmony, they’ll expel me,
but if they’re divided they won’t.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, ānanda, paṭhamaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
segs.e: A bad monk sees this as the first reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, pāpabhikkhu micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato.
segs.e: Furthermore, a bad monk has wrong view, he’s attached to an extremist view.
He thinks:
‘Suppose the monks know that I have wrong view …

segs.p: micchādiṭṭhiko antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgatoti, samaggā maṁ santā nāsessanti;
segs.e: If they’re in harmony they’ll expel me,
but if they’re divided they won’t.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, ānanda, dutiyaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
segs.e: A bad monk sees this as the second reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, pāpabhikkhu micchāājīvo hoti, micchāājīvena jīvikaṁ kappeti.
segs.e: Furthermore, a bad monk has wrong livelihood and earns a living by wrong livelihood.
He thinks:
‘Suppose the monks know that I have wrong livelihood …

segs.p: micchāājīvo micchāājīvena jīvikaṁ kappetīti, samaggā maṁ santā nāsessanti;
segs.e: If they’re in harmony they’ll expel me,
but if they’re divided they won’t.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, ānanda, tatiyaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
segs.e: A bad monk sees this as the third reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, pāpabhikkhu lābhakāmo hoti sakkārakāmo anavaññattikāmo.
segs.e: Furthermore, a bad monk desires material things, honor, and admiration.
He thinks:
‘Suppose the monks know that I desire material things, honor, and admiration.

segs.p: lābhakāmo sakkārakāmo anavaññattikāmoti, samaggā maṁ santā na sakkarissanti na garuṁ karissanti na mānessanti na pūjessanti;
segs.e: If they’re in harmony they won’t honor, respect, revere, or venerate me,

segs.p: vaggā pana maṁ sakkarissanti garuṁ karissanti mānessanti pūjessantī’ti.
segs.e: but if they’re divided they will.’

segs.p: Idaṁ, ānanda, catutthaṁ atthavasaṁ sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandati.
segs.e: A bad monk sees this as the fourth reason to relish schism in the Saṅgha.

segs.p: Ime kho, ānanda, cattāro atthavase sampassamāno pāpabhikkhu saṅghabhedena nandatī”ti.
segs.e: A bad monk sees these four reasons to relish schism in the Saṅgha.”
Numbered Discourses 4.244
25. Perils of Offenses
Perils of Offenses
“Mendicants, there are these four perils of offenses.
What four?

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, coraṁ āgucāriṁ gahetvā rañño dasseyyuṁ:
segs.e: Suppose they were to arrest a bandit, a criminal and present him to the king, saying:
‘Your Majesty, this is a bandit, a criminal.
May Your Majesty punish them!’
The king would say:

segs.p: ‘gacchatha, bho, imaṁ purisaṁ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṁ gāḷhabandhanaṁ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṁ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhāmetvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sīsaṁ chindathā’ti.
segs.e: ‘Go, my men, and tie this man’s arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope. Shave his head and march him from street to street and square to square to the beating of a harsh drum. Then take him out the south gate and there, to the south of the city, chop off his head.’

segs.p: Tamenaṁ rañño purisā daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṁ gāḷhabandhanaṁ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṁ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhāmetvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sīsaṁ chindeyyuṁ.
segs.e: The king’s men would do as they were told.
Then a bystander might think:

segs.p: ‘pāpakaṁ vata, bho, ayaṁ puriso kammaṁ akāsi gārayhaṁ sīsacchejjaṁ.
segs.e: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, a capital offense.

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma rañño purisā daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṁ gāḷhabandhanaṁ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṁ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhāmetvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sīsaṁ chindissanti.
So vatassāhaṁ evarūpaṁ pāpakammaṁ na kareyyaṁ gārayhaṁ sīsacchejjan’ti.
segs.e: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, a capital offense.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā evaṁ tibbā bhayasaññā paccupaṭṭhitā hoti pārājikesu dhammesu.
segs.e: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding expulsion offenses.

segs.p: Tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—anāpanno vā pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ na āpajjissati, āpanno vā pārājikaṁ dhammaṁ yathādhammaṁ paṭikarissati.
segs.e: It can be expected that if they haven’t committed an expulsion offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso kāḷavatthaṁ paridhāya kese pakiritvā musalaṁ khandhe āropetvā mahājanakāyaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Suppose a man was to put on a black cloth, mess up his hair, and put a club on his shoulder. Then he approaches a large crowd and says:

segs.p: ‘ahaṁ, bhante, pāpakammaṁ akāsiṁ gārayhaṁ mosallaṁ, yena me āyasmanto attamanā honti taṁ karomī’ti.
segs.e: ‘Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of clubbing. I submit to your pleasure.’
Then a bystander might think:

segs.p: ‘pāpakaṁ vata, bho, ayaṁ puriso kammaṁ akāsi gārayhaṁ mosallaṁ.
segs.e: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of clubbing. …

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma kāḷavatthaṁ paridhāya kese pakiritvā musalaṁ khandhe āropetvā mahājanakāyaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vakkhati:
“ahaṁ, bhante, pāpakammaṁ akāsiṁ gārayhaṁ mosallaṁ, yena me āyasmanto attamanā honti taṁ karomī”ti.
So vatassāhaṁ evarūpaṁ pāpakammaṁ na kareyyaṁ gārayhaṁ mosallan’ti.
segs.e: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of clubbing.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā evaṁ tibbā bhayasaññā paccupaṭṭhitā hoti saṅghādisesesu dhammesu, tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—anāpanno vā saṅghādisesaṁ dhammaṁ na āpajjissati, āpanno vā saṅghādisesaṁ dhammaṁ yathādhammaṁ paṭikarissati.
segs.e: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding suspension offenses. It can be expected that if they haven’t committed a suspension offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso kāḷavatthaṁ paridhāya kese pakiritvā bhasmapuṭaṁ khandhe āropetvā mahājanakāyaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Suppose a man was to put on a black cloth, mess up his hair, and put a sack of ashes on his shoulder. Then he approaches a large crowd and says:
‘Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of a sack of ashes.

segs.p: Yena me āyasmanto attamanā honti taṁ karomī’ti.
segs.e: I submit to your pleasure.’
Then a bystander might think:

segs.p: ‘pāpakaṁ vata, bho, ayaṁ puriso kammaṁ akāsi gārayhaṁ bhasmapuṭaṁ.
segs.e: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of a sack of ashes. …

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma kāḷavatthaṁ paridhāya kese pakiritvā bhasmapuṭaṁ khandhe āropetvā mahājanakāyaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vakkhati:
yena me āyasmanto attamanā honti taṁ karomī”ti.
So vatassāhaṁ evarūpaṁ pāpakammaṁ na kareyyaṁ gārayhaṁ bhasmapuṭan’ti.
segs.e: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of a sack of ashes.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā evaṁ tibbā bhayasaññā paccupaṭṭhitā hoti pācittiyesu dhammesu, tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—anāpanno vā pācittiyaṁ dhammaṁ na āpajjissati, āpanno vā pācittiyaṁ dhammaṁ yathādhammaṁ paṭikarissati.
segs.e: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding confessable offenses. It can be expected that if they haven’t committed a confessable offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso kāḷavatthaṁ paridhāya kese pakiritvā mahājanakāyaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya:
segs.e: Suppose a man was to put on a black cloth and mess up his hair. Then he approaches a large crowd and says:
‘Sirs, I’ve done a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of criticism.

segs.p: Yena me āyasmanto attamanā honti taṁ karomī’ti.
segs.e: I submit to your pleasure.’
Then a bystander might think:

segs.p: ‘pāpakaṁ vata, bho, ayaṁ puriso kammaṁ akāsi gārayhaṁ upavajjaṁ.
segs.e: ‘This man must have done a truly bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of criticism. …

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma kāḷavatthaṁ paridhāya kese pakiritvā mahājanakāyaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vakkhati:
yena me āyasmanto attamanā honti taṁ karomī”ti.
So vatassāhaṁ evarūpaṁ pāpakammaṁ na kareyyaṁ gārayhaṁ upavajjan’ti.
segs.e: There’s no way I’d ever do such a bad and reprehensible deed, deserving of criticism.’

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā evaṁ tibbā bhayasaññā paccupaṭṭhitā hoti pāṭidesanīyesu dhammesu, tassetaṁ pāṭikaṅkhaṁ—anāpanno vā pāṭidesanīyaṁ dhammaṁ na āpajjissati, āpanno vā pāṭidesanīyaṁ dhammaṁ yathādhammaṁ paṭikarissati.
segs.e: In the same way, take any monk or nun who has set up such an acute perception of peril regarding confessable offenses. It can be expected that if they haven’t committed a confessable offense they won’t, and if they committed one they will deal with it properly.
These are the four perils of offenses.”
Numbered Discourses 4.245
25. Perils of Offenses
The Benefits of Training

segs.p: “Sikkhānisaṁsamidaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ vussati paññuttaraṁ vimuttisāraṁ satādhipateyyaṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, this spiritual life is lived with training as its benefit, with wisdom as its overseer, with freedom as its core, and with mindfulness as its ruler.
And how is training its benefit?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ ābhisamācārikā sikkhā paññattā appasannānaṁ pasādāya pasannānaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya.
segs.e: Firstly, I laid down for my disciples the training that deals with supplementary regulations in order to inspire confidence in those without it and to increase confidence in those who have it.

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ ābhisamācārikā sikkhā paññattā appasannānaṁ pasādāya pasannānaṁ bhiyyobhāvāya tathā tathā so tassā sikkhāya akhaṇḍakārī hoti acchiddakārī asabalakārī akammāsakārī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: They undertake whatever supplementary regulations I have laid down, keeping them intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ ādibrahmacariyikā sikkhā paññattā sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: Furthermore, I laid down for my disciples the training that deals with the fundamentals of the spiritual life in order to rightly end suffering in every way.

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ ādibrahmacariyikā sikkhā paññattā sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya tathā tathā so tassā sikkhāya akhaṇḍakārī hoti acchiddakārī asabalakārī akammāsakārī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: They undertake whatever training that deals with the fundamentals of the spiritual life I have laid down, keeping it intact, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred.
That’s how training is its benefit.
And how is wisdom its overseer?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ dhammā desitā sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: I taught the Dhamma to my disciples in order to rightly end suffering in every way.

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ dhammā desitā sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya tathā tathāssa te dhammā paññāya samavekkhitā honti.
segs.e: They examine with wisdom any teachings I taught them.
That’s how wisdom is its overseer.
And how is freedom its core?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ dhammā desitā sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya.
segs.e: I taught the Dhamma to my disciples in order to rightly end suffering in every way.

segs.p: Yathā yathā, bhikkhave, mayā sāvakānaṁ dhammā desitā sabbaso sammā dukkhakkhayāya tathā tathāssa te dhammā vimuttiyā phusitā honti.
segs.e: They experience through freedom any teachings I taught them.
That’s how freedom is its core.
And how is mindfulness its ruler?

segs.p: ‘Iti aparipūraṁ vā ābhisamācārikaṁ sikkhaṁ paripūressāmi, paripūraṁ vā ābhisamācārikaṁ sikkhaṁ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmī’ti—ajjhattaṁyeva sati sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll fulfill the training dealing with supplementary regulations, or support with wisdom in every situation the training dealing with supplementary regulations I’ve already fulfilled.’

segs.p: ‘Iti aparipūraṁ vā ādibrahmacariyikaṁ sikkhaṁ paripūressāmi, paripūraṁ vā ādibrahmacariyikaṁ sikkhaṁ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmī’ti—ajjhattaṁyeva sati sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll fulfill the training dealing with the fundamentals of the spiritual life, or support with wisdom in every situation the training dealing with the fundamentals of the spiritual life I’ve already fulfilled.’

segs.p: ‘Iti asamavekkhitaṁ vā dhammaṁ paññāya samavekkhissāmi, samavekkhitaṁ vā dhammaṁ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmī’ti—ajjhattaṁyeva sati sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll examine with wisdom the teaching that I haven’t yet examined, or support with wisdom in every situation the teaching I’ve already examined.’

segs.p: ‘Iti aphusitaṁ vā dhammaṁ vimuttiyā phusissāmi, phusitaṁ vā dhammaṁ tattha tattha paññāya anuggahessāmī’ti—ajjhattaṁyeva sati sūpaṭṭhitā hoti.
segs.e: Mindfulness is well established in oneself: ‘In this way I’ll experience through freedom the teaching that I haven’t yet experienced, or support with wisdom in every situation the teaching I’ve already experienced.’
That’s how mindfulness is its ruler.

segs.p: ‘Sikkhānisaṁsamidaṁ, bhikkhave, brahmacariyaṁ vussati paññuttaraṁ vimuttisāraṁ satādhipateyyan’ti,
segs.e: ‘This spiritual life is lived with training as its benefit, with wisdom as its overseer, with freedom as its core, and with mindfulness as its ruler.’

segs.p: iti yaṁ taṁ vuttaṁ idametaṁ paṭicca vuttan”ti.
segs.e: That’s what I said, and this is why I said it.”

25. Perils of Offenses
Lying Postures
“Mendicants, there are these four ways of lying down.
What four?
The ways a corpse, a pleasure seeker, a lion, and a Realized One lie down.
And how does a corpse lie down?
Corpses usually lie flat on their backs.
This is called the way a corpse lies down.
And how does a pleasure seeker lie down?

segs.p: Yebhuyyena, bhikkhave, kāmabhogī vāmena passena senti;
segs.e: Pleasure seekers usually lie down on their left side.
This is called the way a pleasure seeker lies down.
And how does a lion lie down?

segs.p: Sīho, bhikkhave, migarājā dakkhiṇena passena seyyaṁ kappeti, pāde pādaṁ accādhāya, antarasatthimhi naṅguṭṭhaṁ anupakkhipitvā.
segs.e: The lion, king of beasts, lies down on the right side, placing one foot on top of the other, with his tail tucked between his thighs.

segs.p: So paṭibujjhitvā purimaṁ kāyaṁ abbhunnāmetvā pacchimaṁ kāyaṁ anuviloketi.
segs.e: When he wakes, he lifts his front quarters and checks his hind quarters.

segs.p: Sace, bhikkhave, sīho migarājā kiñci passati kāyassa vikkhittaṁ vā visaṭaṁ vā, tena, bhikkhave, sīho migarājā anattamano hoti.
segs.e: If he sees that any part of his body is disordered or displaced, he is displeased.

segs.p: Sace pana, bhikkhave, sīho migarājā na kiñci passati kāyassa vikkhittaṁ vā visaṭaṁ vā, tena, bhikkhave, sīho migarājā attamano hoti.
segs.e: But if he sees that no part of his body is disordered or displaced, he is pleased.
This is called the way a lion lies down.
And how does a Realized One lie down?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato vivicceva kāmehi …pe… catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: It’s when a Realized One, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unskillful qualities, enters and remains in the first absorption … second absorption … third absorption … fourth absorption.
This is called the way a Realized One lies down.
These are the four ways of lying down.”
Numbered Discourses 4.247
25. Perils of Offenses
Worthy of a Monument
“Mendicants, these four are worthy of a monument.
What four?

segs.p: Tathāgato arahaṁ sammāsambuddho thūpāraho, paccekabuddho thūpāraho, tathāgatasāvako thūpāraho, rājā cakkavattī thūpāraho—
segs.e: A Realized One, a perfected one, a fully awakened Buddha; an independent Buddha; a disciple of a Realized One; and a wheel-turning monarch.
These four are worthy of a monument.”
Numbered Discourses 4.248
25. Perils of Offenses
The Growth of Wisdom
“Mendicants, these four things lead to the growth of wisdom.
What four?
Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā paññāvuddhiyā saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: These four things lead to the growth of wisdom.”
Numbered Discourses 4.249
25. Perils of Offenses
Very Helpful
“Mendicants, these four things are very helpful to a human being.
What four?
Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā manussabhūtassa bahukārā hontī”ti.
segs.e: These four things are very helpful to a human being.”
Numbered Discourses 4.250
25. Perils of Offenses
Expressions (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these four ignoble expressions.
What four?

segs.p: Adiṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, asute sutavāditā, amute mutavāditā, aviññāte viññātavāditā—
segs.e: Saying you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known something, but you haven’t.
These are the four ignoble expressions.”

25. Perils of Offenses
Expressions (2nd)
“Mendicants, there are these four noble expressions.
What four?

segs.p: Adiṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, asute asutavāditā, amute amutavāditā, aviññāte aviññātavāditā—
segs.e: Saying you haven’t seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you haven’t.
These are the four noble expressions.”

25. Perils of Offenses
Expressions (3rd)
“Mendicants, there are these four ignoble expressions.
What four?

segs.p: Diṭṭhe adiṭṭhavāditā, sute asutavāditā, mute amutavāditā, viññāte aviññātavāditā—
segs.e: Saying you haven’t seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you have.
These are the four ignoble expressions.”

25. Perils of Offenses
Expressions (4th)
“Mendicants, there are these four noble expressions.
What four?

segs.p: Diṭṭhe diṭṭhavāditā, sute sutavāditā, mute mutavāditā, viññāte viññātavāditā—
segs.e: Saying you’ve seen, heard, thought, or known something, and you have.
These are the four noble expressions.”

26. Insight
Insight
“Mendicants, there are these four things.
What four?
There are things that should be completely understood by direct knowledge.
There are things that should be given up by direct knowledge.
There are things that should be developed by direct knowledge.
There are things that should be realized by direct knowledge.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā?
segs.e: And what are the things that should be completely understood by direct knowledge?
The five grasping aggregates.

segs.p: ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pariññeyyā.
segs.e: These are called the things that should be completely understood by direct knowledge.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā?
segs.e: And what are the things that should be given up by direct knowledge?
Ignorance and craving for continued existence.

segs.p: ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā pahātabbā.
segs.e: These are called the things that should be given up by direct knowledge.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā?
segs.e: And what are the things that should be developed by direct knowledge?
Serenity and discernment.

segs.p: ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā bhāvetabbā.
segs.e: These are called the things that should be developed by direct knowledge.

segs.p: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā?
segs.e: And what are the things that should be realized by direct knowledge?
Knowledge and freedom.

segs.p: ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā abhiññā sacchikātabbā.
segs.e: These are called the things that should be realized by direct knowledge.
These are the four things.”
Numbered Discourses 4.255
26. Insight
Searches
“Mendicants, there are these four ignoble searches.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhammaṁyeva pariyesati;
segs.e: Someone liable to old age searches only for what grows old.
Someone liable to sickness searches only for what gets sick.
Someone liable to death searches only for what dies.
Someone liable to become corrupted searches only for what is defiled.
These are the four ignoble searches.
There are these four noble searches.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco attanā jarādhammo samāno jarādhamme ādīnavaṁ viditvā ajaraṁ anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ nibbānaṁ pariyesati;
segs.e: Someone who is liable to grow old, knowing the drawback in what grows old, searches for that which is free of old age, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

segs.p: attanā byādhidhammo samāno byādhidhamme ādīnavaṁ viditvā abyādhiṁ anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ nibbānaṁ pariyesati;
segs.e: Someone who is liable to get sick, knowing the drawback in what gets sick, searches for that which is free of sickness, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

segs.p: attanā maraṇadhammo samāno maraṇadhamme ādīnavaṁ viditvā amataṁ anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ nibbānaṁ pariyesati;
segs.e: Someone who is liable to die, knowing the drawback in what dies, searches for that which is free of death, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.

segs.p: attanā saṅkilesadhammo samāno saṅkilesadhamme ādīnavaṁ viditvā asaṅkiliṭṭhaṁ anuttaraṁ yogakkhemaṁ nibbānaṁ pariyesati.
segs.e: Someone liable to become corrupted, knowing the drawback in what is defiled, searches for the undefiled supreme sanctuary from the yoke, extinguishment.
These are the four noble searches.”
Numbered Discourses 4.256
26. Insight
Ways of Being Inclusive
“Mendicants, there are these four ways of being inclusive.
What four?
Giving, kindly words, taking care, and equality.
These are the four ways of being inclusive.”
Numbered Discourses 4.257
26. Insight
With Māluṅkyaputta

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mālukyaputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Māluṅkyaputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu, yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”

segs.p: “Ettha idāni, mālukyaputta, kiṁ dahare bhikkhū vakkhāma;
segs.e: “Well now, Māluṅkyaputta, what are we to say to the young monks,

segs.p: yatra hi nāma tvaṁ jiṇṇo vuddho mahallako tathāgatassa saṅkhittena ovādaṁ yācasī”ti.
segs.e: when even an old man like you, elderly and senior, asks the Realized One for brief advice?”

segs.p: “Desetu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ; desetu sugato saṅkhittena dhammaṁ. Appeva nāmāhaṁ bhagavato bhāsitassa atthaṁ ājāneyyaṁ; appeva nāmāhaṁ bhagavato bhāsitassa dāyādo assan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief! May the Holy One teach me the Dhamma in brief! Hopefully I can understand the meaning of what the Buddha says! Hopefully I can be an heir of the Buddha’s teaching!”

segs.p: “Cattārome, mālukyaputta, taṇhuppādā yattha bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: “Māluṅkyaputta, there are four things that give rise to craving in a mendicant.
What four?

segs.p: Cīvarahetu vā, mālukyaputta, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: For the sake of robes,

segs.p: Piṇḍapātahetu vā, mālukyaputta, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: almsfood,

segs.p: Senāsanahetu vā, mālukyaputta, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: lodgings,

segs.p: Itibhavābhavahetu vā, mālukyaputta, bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: or rebirth in this or that state.

segs.p: Ime kho, mālukyaputta, cattāro taṇhuppādā yattha bhikkhuno taṇhā uppajjamānā uppajjati.
segs.e: These are the four things that give rise to craving in a mendicant.

segs.p: Yato kho, mālukyaputta, bhikkhuno taṇhā pahīnā hoti ucchinnamūlā tālāvatthukatā anabhāvaṅkatā āyatiṁ anuppādadhammā, ayaṁ vuccati, mālukyaputta, ‘bhikkhu acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassā’”ti.
segs.e: That craving is given up by a mendicant, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, obliterated, and unable to arise in the future. Then they’re called a mendicant who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mālukyaputto bhagavatā iminā ovādena ovadito uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṁ katvā pakkāmi.
segs.e: When Māluṅkyaputta had been given this advice by the Buddha, he rose from his seat, bowed, and respectfully circled the Buddha, keeping him on his right, before leaving.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā mālukyaputto eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva—yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṁ—brahmacariyapariyosānaṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihāsi.
segs.e: Then Māluṅkyaputta, living alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute, soon realized the supreme culmination of the spiritual path in this very life. He lived having achieved with his own insight the goal for which gentlemen rightly go forth from the lay life to homelessness.

segs.p: “Khīṇā jāti, vusitaṁ brahmacariyaṁ, kataṁ karaṇīyaṁ, nāparaṁ itthattāyā”ti abbhaññāsi.
segs.e: He understood: “Rebirth is ended; the spiritual journey has been completed; what had to be done has been done; there is nothing further for this place.”

segs.p: Aññataro ca panāyasmā mālukyaputto arahataṁ ahosīti.
segs.e: And Venerable Māluṅkyaputta became one of the perfected.
Numbered Discourses 4.258
26. Insight
Families

segs.p: “Yāni kānici, bhikkhave, kulāni bhogesu mahattaṁ pattāni na ciraṭṭhitikāni bhavanti, sabbāni tāni catūhi ṭhānehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when families don’t stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.
What four?

segs.p: Naṭṭhaṁ na gavesanti, jiṇṇaṁ na paṭisaṅkharonti, aparimitapānabhojanā honti, dussīlaṁ itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā ādhipacce ṭhapenti.
segs.e: They don’t look for what’s lost; they don’t repair old things; they eat and drink too much; or they put an unethical woman or man in charge.

segs.p: Yāni kānici, bhikkhave, kulāni bhogesu mahattaṁ pattāni na ciraṭṭhitikāni bhavanti, sabbāni tāni imehi catūhi ṭhānehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: When families don’t stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.

segs.p: Yāni kānici, bhikkhave, kulāni bhogesu mahattaṁ pattāni ciraṭṭhitikāni bhavanti, sabbāni tāni catūhi ṭhānehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarena.
segs.e: When families do stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.
What four?

segs.p: Naṭṭhaṁ gavesanti, jiṇṇaṁ paṭisaṅkharonti, parimitapānabhojanā honti, sīlavantaṁ itthiṁ vā purisaṁ vā ādhipacce ṭhapenti.
segs.e: They look for what’s lost; they repair old things; they eat and drink in moderation; and they put an ethical woman or man in charge.

segs.p: Yāni kānici, bhikkhave, kulāni bhogesu mahattaṁ pattāni ciraṭṭhitikāni bhavanti, sabbāni tāni imehi catūhi ṭhānehi, etesaṁ vā aññatarenā”ti.
segs.e: When families do stay wealthy for long, it’s always for one or more of these four reasons.”
Numbered Discourses 4.259
26. Insight
A Thoroughbred (1st)

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a fine royal thoroughbred with four factors is worthy of a king, fit to serve a king, and reckoned a factor of kingship.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, rañño bhadro assājānīyo vaṇṇasampanno ca hoti balasampanno ca javasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: It’s when a fine royal thoroughbred is beautiful, strong, fast, and well-proportioned.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi aṅgehi samannāgato rañño bhadro assājānīyo rājāraho hoti rājabhoggo, rañño aṅganteva saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: A fine royal thoroughbred with these four factors is worthy of a king. …

segs.p: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant with four qualities is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of veneration with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vaṇṇasampanno ca hoti balasampanno ca javasampanno ca ārohapariṇāhasampanno ca.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is beautiful, strong, fast, and well proportioned.
And how is a mendicant beautiful?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vaṇṇasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is beautiful.
And how is a mendicant strong?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya, kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu.
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant lives with energy roused up for giving up unskillful qualities and embracing skillful qualities. They are strong, staunchly vigorous, not slacking off when it comes to developing skillful qualities.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu balasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is strong.
And how is a mendicant fast?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘idaṁ dukkhan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti …pe… ‘ayaṁ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
segs.e: It’s when they truly understand: ‘This is suffering’ … ‘This is the origin of suffering’ … ‘This is the cessation of suffering’ … ‘This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering’.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu javasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is fast.
And how is a mendicant well proportioned?
It’s when a mendicant receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ārohapariṇāhasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is well proportioned.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu āhuneyyo hoti …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
segs.e: A mendicant with these four qualities … is the supreme field of merit for the world.”
Numbered Discourses 4.260

Numbered Discourses 4.261
26. Insight
Powers
“Mendicants, there are these four powers.
What four?
The powers of energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.
These are the four powers.”
Numbered Discourses 4.262
26. Insight
Wilderness

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṁ araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when a mendicant has four qualities they’re not ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.
What four?

segs.p: Kāmavitakkena, byāpādavitakkena, vihiṁsāvitakkena, duppañño hoti jaḷo elamūgo—
segs.e: They have sensual, malicious, and cruel thoughts; or they’re witless, dull, and idiotic.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu nālaṁ araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these four qualities they’re not ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevituṁ.
segs.e: When a mendicant has four qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.
What four?

segs.p: Nekkhammavitakkena, abyāpādavitakkena, avihiṁsāvitakkena, paññavā hoti ajaḷo anelamūgo—
segs.e: They have thoughts of renunciation, good will, and harmlessness; and they’re wise, bright, and clever.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu alaṁ araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevitun”ti.
segs.e: When a mendicant possesses these four qualities they’re ready to frequent remote lodgings in the wilderness and the forest.”
Numbered Discourses 4.263
26. Insight
Deeds

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bālo abyatto asappuriso khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: “When a foolish, incompetent untrue person has four qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.
What four?

segs.p: Sāvajjena kāyakammena, sāvajjena vacīkammena, sāvajjena manokammena, sāvajjāya diṭṭhiyā—
segs.e: Blameworthy deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameworthy view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato bālo abyatto asappuriso khataṁ upahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, sāvajjo ca hoti sānuvajjo viññūnaṁ, bahuñca apuññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: When a foolish, incompetent untrue person possesses these four qualities they keep themselves broken and damaged. They deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much wickedness.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito viyatto sappuriso akkhataṁ anupahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, anavajjo ca hoti ananuvajjo viññūnaṁ, bahuñca puññaṁ pasavati.
segs.e: When an astute, competent true person has four qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.
What four?

segs.p: Anavajjena kāyakammena, anavajjena vacīkammena, anavajjena manokammena, anavajjāya diṭṭhiyā—
segs.e: Blameless deeds by way of body, speech, and mind, and blameless view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito viyatto sappuriso akkhataṁ anupahataṁ attānaṁ pariharati, anavajjo ca hoti ananuvajjo viññūnaṁ, bahuñca puññaṁ pasavatī”ti.
segs.e: When an astute, competent true person possesses these four qualities they keep themselves healthy and whole. They don’t deserve to be blamed and criticized by sensible people, and they brim with much merit.”
Numbered Discourses 4.264
27. Ways of Performing Deeds
Killing Living Creatures

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: “Mendicants, someone with four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Attanā ca pāṇātipātī hoti, parañca pāṇātipāte samādapeti, pāṇātipāte ca samanuñño hoti, pāṇātipātassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—
segs.e: They themselves kill living creatures; they encourage others to kill living creatures; they approve of killing living creatures; and they praise killing living creatures.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ niraye.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in hell as if delivered there.

segs.p: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge.
segs.e: Someone with four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.
What four?

segs.p: Attanā ca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, parañca pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—
segs.e: They don’t themselves kill living creatures; they encourage others to not kill living creatures; they approve of not killing living creatures; and they praise not killing living creatures.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ sagge”ti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.265

Misconduct

Lying

segs.p: …pe… Attanā ca musāvādī hoti, parañca musāvāde samādapeti, musāvāde ca samanuñño hoti, musāvādassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi kho …pe….
segs.e: “… They themselves lie …

27. Ways of Performing Deeds
Backbiting

segs.p: …pe… Attanā ca pisuṇavāco hoti, parañca pisuṇāya vācāya samādapeti, pisuṇāya vācāya ca samanuñño hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi …pe….
segs.e: “… They themselves backbite …

segs.e: … They don’t themselves backbite …”
Numbered Discourses 4.269
27. Ways of Performing Deeds
Harsh Speech

segs.p: …pe… Attanā ca pharusavāco hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya samādapeti, pharusāya vācāya ca samanuñño hoti, pharusāya vācāya ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati …pe….
segs.e: “… They themselves speak harshly …

segs.p: Attanā ca pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi kho …pe….
segs.e: … They don’t themselves speak harshly …”
Numbered Discourses 4.270
27. Ways of Performing Deeds
Talking Nonsense

segs.p: …pe… Attanā ca samphappalāpī hoti, parañca samphappalāpe samādapeti, samphappalāpe ca samanuñño hoti, samphappalāpassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi …pe….
segs.e: “… They themselves talk nonsense …

segs.p: Attanā ca samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, parañca samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi kho, bhikkhave …pe….
segs.e: … They don’t themselves talk nonsense …”
Numbered Discourses 4.271
27. Ways of Performing Deeds
Covetousness

segs.p: …pe… Attanā ca abhijjhālu hoti, parañca abhijjhāya samādapeti, abhijjhāya ca samanuñño hoti, abhijjhāya ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati …pe….
segs.e: “… They themselves are covetous …

segs.p: Attanā ca anabhijjhālu hoti, parañca anabhijjhāya samādapeti, anabhijjhāya ca samanuñño hoti, anabhijjhāya ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi kho …pe….
segs.e: … They themselves are content …”
Numbered Discourses 4.272
27. Ways of Performing Deeds
Ill Will

segs.p: …pe… Attanā ca byāpannacitto hoti, parañca byāpāde samādapeti, byāpāde ca samanuñño hoti, byāpādassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi …pe….
segs.e: “… They themselves have ill will …

segs.p: Attanā ca abyāpannacitto hoti, parañca abyāpāde samādapeti, abyāpāde ca samanuñño hoti, abyāpādassa ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi …pe….
segs.e: … They themselves have good will …”
Numbered Discourses 4.273
27. Ways of Performing Deeds
Wrong View

segs.p: …pe… Attanā ca micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, parañca micchādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti, micchādiṭṭhiyā ca samanuñño hoti, micchādiṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—imehi …pe….
segs.e: “… They themselves have wrong view …

segs.p: Attanā ca sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, parañca sammādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti, sammādiṭṭhiyā ca samanuñño hoti, sammādiṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati—
segs.e: They themselves have right view; they encourage others to have right view; they approve of right view; and they praise right view.

segs.p: imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṁ nikkhitto evaṁ saggeti.
segs.e: Someone with these four qualities is placed in heaven as if delivered there.”
Numbered Discourses 4.274
28. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Mindfulness Meditation
“For insight into greed, four things should be developed.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ;
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: vedanāsu …pe… citte …pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
segs.e: They meditate observing an aspect of feelings … mind … principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

segs.p: Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime cattāro dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these four things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 4.275
28. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Right Efforts
“For insight into greed, four things should be developed.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anuppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ anuppādāya chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati;
segs.e: Firstly, a mendicant generates enthusiasm, tries, makes an effort, exerts the mind, and strives so that bad, unskillful qualities don’t arise.

segs.p: uppannānaṁ pāpakānaṁ akusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ pahānāya …pe… anuppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ uppādāya …pe… uppannānaṁ kusalānaṁ dhammānaṁ ṭhitiyā asammosāya bhiyyobhāvāya vepullāya bhāvanāya pāripūriyā chandaṁ janeti vāyamati vīriyaṁ ārabhati cittaṁ paggaṇhāti padahati.
segs.e: …so that unskillful qualities that have arisen are given up … so that skillful qualities arise … so that skillful qualities that have arisen remain, are not lost, but increase, mature, and are fully developed.

segs.p: Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime cattāro dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these four things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 4.276
28. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Bases of Psychic Power
“For insight into greed, four things should be developed.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṁ iddhipādaṁ bhāveti;
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant develops the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to enthusiasm, and active effort.
They develop the basis of psychic power that has immersion due to energy …
mental development …
inquiry, and active effort.

segs.p: Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime cattāro dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: For insight into greed, these four things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 4.277–303
28. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Complete Understanding, Etc.

segs.p: “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, pariññāya …pe… parikkhayāya … pahānāya … khayāya … vayāya … virāgāya … nirodhāya … cāgāya … paṭinissaggāya cattāro dhammā bhāvetabbā …pe….
segs.e: “For the complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go of greed, four things should be developed.”
Numbered Discourses 4.304–783
28. Abbreviated Texts Beginning with Greed
Insight into Hate, Etc.

segs.p: “Dosassa …pe… mohassa … kodhassa … upanāhassa … makkhassa … paḷāsassa … issāya … macchariyassa … māyāya … sāṭheyyassa … thambhassa … sārambhassa … mānassa … atimānassa … madassa … pamādassa abhiññāya … pariññāya … parikkhayāya … pahānāya … khayāya … vayāya … virāgāya … nirodhāya … cāgāya … paṭinissaggāya ime cattāro dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.
segs.e: “Of hate … delusion … anger … acrimony … disdain … contempt … jealousy … stinginess … deceit … deviousness … obstinacy … aggression … conceit … arrogance … vanity … negligence … for insight … complete understanding … finishing … giving up … ending … vanishing … fading away … cessation … giving away … letting go … four things should be developed.”
The Book of the Fours is finished.
